# Clockspeed - Ledger

**Section status: HISTORICAL.** Every section in this file is a record, so a dated
heading here may mark its own section historical.

**Append-only, NEWEST FIRST. One record per closed work item.**

**This file owns:** the per-item completion record - what closed, when, and how to verify
it independently.

**This file never contains:** rules, open work, aspirational items, or architecture. Open
work lives in `ROADMAP.md`, aspirational work in `BACKLOG.md`, externally blocked work in
`docs/GATED.md`, and settled decisions in `docs/adr/` plus the `Settled` section of
`CLAUDE.md`.

Nothing in this file is ever edited or deleted once written. A record that turns out to
be wrong gets a **new, later** record that corrects it and says so. Pruned records move
to `docs/history_notes.md`; they are never dropped.

---

## Entry shape

Newest entry goes directly under the `## Entries` heading. Each entry is:

```
### YYYY-MM-DD - <ITEM-ID> - <one line: what closed>
Verification: <pointer>
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| Date | `YYYY-MM-DD`, the date the item actually closed. |
| Item ID | The permanent `CS-` ID from `ROADMAP.md`. Never invented at close time, never reused, never renumbered. |
| One line | What closed. One line. If it needs a paragraph it needs its own file and this line becomes a pointer to it. |
| Verification pointer | How someone else confirms it, independently, without asking you. Mandatory. A line pointer is a citation with a shelf life - cite the symbol. `path.py::name` survives every edit above it; `path.py:NNN` is dead the moment one lands, and this file is append-only so it can never be repaired where it stands. The rule binds the whole record, not the pointer field alone. |

An entry may add an `ADR:` line citing `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` when the item settled a
decision. An entry that closes a gated item states which external condition was met and
who or what observed it.

---

## The verification pointer - what makes one valid

**Cite the item ID, the merged file, and the test name. Do not cite the slice SHA.**

A ledger entry whose only evidence is a commit SHA is **fragile**. The reason is
mechanical, not stylistic: work is produced in worktree-isolated agent slices, and those
slice commits frequently do not survive the cherry-pick into the main line. The SHA in
the entry then refers to an object that is unreachable, or reachable but not the version
that shipped. The entry looks precise and verifies nothing.

The item ID, the merged file path and the test name all survive the merge, because they
are properties of the shipped tree rather than of the branch that produced it.

**Valid pointers**

- `tests/save/test_header.py::test_world_token_stable_across_reload`
- `clockspeed/solve/exact.py` plus `tests/solve/test_exact.py::test_no_float_in_path`
- `tools/drift_guard.py` red-then-green transcript recorded under the item ID
- A named CI job on the tier-1 lane, plus the file it asserts on

**Invalid pointers**

- A bare commit SHA
- "tests pass" or "CI green" with nothing named
- A count of tests with no file and no test name behind it
- A link to a transcript or a chat message

Counts are never restated here as prose. If a count is worth citing, cite the
machine-checked artifact that produces it.

cards.py:97-119, ledger.py:694-707, non-negotiable 7. Reversed by: an engine issuing one card per
subject per rule (keys then per class).
G2 SPLIT BY RULE: power.fuel_supply records one indeterminate step per INDETERMINATE class
(unsettled, fails closed); BACKLOG line: a world with a built solid burner never auto-completes a
supply card. power.fuel_demand settles like power.draw_incomplete: for each class it fires on it
records reject("state a supply verdict for <class>", <REASON_DETAIL line>); indeterminate only where
its own burn figure is unknown (G5). Rejected per-subject settlement (a ledger.py change); rejected
indeterminate on the demand rule (category error - it never attempts the supply comparison). Decided

to its audit field, keyed by class key inside the value. The rule reads leaf figures and computes
demand, supply MW per fuel, pooled MW, shortfall, shortfall rate per fuel and burn per fuel through

no card). Red first: a mis-paired fuel and energy in the adapter must end in a rule-error. Rejected:

fallback as a reject step. Test registries use invented names only. Rejected keys only; rejected an
unrecorded adapter fallback. Reversed by: a ruling that advice text carries class keys only, or
evidence a display name leaks personal data.
G5: when no INDETERMINATE class has a known burn, the demand card still fires with a burn-unknown
headline; each unknown burn is an indeterminate step carrying its DEMAND_REASONS detail line; if any
fired class has a known burn, the headline is the first such class by key. Rejected silent (breaks

### 2026-10-12 - CS-1312 - CLOSED by the guard route: `purge_work_dir` shares `discard_copy`'s forbidden-root and parent checks, and the one forbidden-root compare refuses a respelled or linked route into a save directory
Verification: `clockspeed/save/workdir.py::purge_work_dir`, `clockspeed/save/workdir.py::discard_copy`
and `clockspeed/save/workdir.py::copy_for_read`, over the shared gate
`clockspeed/save/workdir.py::_copies_home`, `clockspeed/save/workdir.py::_discard_from`,
`clockspeed/save/workdir.py::_refuse_if_forbidden`, `clockspeed/save/workdir.py::_inside`,
`clockspeed/save/workdir.py::_canonical` and `clockspeed/save/workdir.py::_identity`. The tests:
`tests/save/test_workdir.py::test_purge_through_a_copies_directory_reaching_the_save_directory_removes_nothing`
(junction, symlink and nested),
`::test_purge_leaves_junctions_inside_the_copies_directory_and_what_is_behind_them`,
`::test_a_respelled_route_into_the_save_directory_is_refused_by_each_gated_caller`,
`::test_each_layer_of_the_forbidden_root_compare_refuses_a_respelled_route_alone`,
`::test_a_destination_the_identity_walk_cannot_stat_is_refused_without_a_path`,
`::test_a_link_left_at_the_partial_name_is_removed_not_written_through` (hardlink, symlink,
dangling-symlink and junction),
`::test_an_entry_that_survives_removal_at_the_partial_name_is_never_written_through`
(readonly-symlink, readonly-dangling-symlink, readonly-junction, readonly-directory-symlink and
directory) and `::test_an_entry_at_the_partial_name_whose_lstat_is_denied_is_refused` (symlink
and dangling-symlink). Each was red first on its parent at "the save directory changed", or for
the junction at the partial name at "the copy refused", per its builder; not re-observed here.
The exceptions, per the fix 3 and fix 4 builders: the directory, readonly-junction and
readonly-directory-symlink arms passed on their parents and pin the classification against
widening. Merged: `clockspeed/save/workdir.py` and `tests/save/test_workdir.py`. The commits are
named by subject, "CS-1312 - purge_work_dir refuses a copies dir that reaches a save dir" through
"CS-1312 - an unreadable entry at the partial name is refused". The item's section is relocated
verbatim to `docs/history_notes.md`.
THE ACCEPTANCE, by its guard branch: the purge now passes `discard_copy`'s forbidden-root check
before it lists the copies directory, and each entry through the same parent check, both through
the two shared helpers so the delete paths cannot drift; the junction, symlink and nested arms
hold a fake save directory byte-identical by hash; and a distinct adversary pass followed, two
adversary rounds and three verifier rounds below. CS-453's guard branch, absorbed by this item, is met by the same route.
DECISION RECORD (decided by the session 138 merger): ROUTE GUARD OVER REMOVE. No production
caller exists. Consumer evidence, `git grep -n purge_work_dir` on the landing branch: the
definition and the module's own docstrings and comments in `clockspeed/save/workdir.py`; call
sites only in `tests/save/test_workdir.py` and `tests/save/test_newest_world.py` (six before this
item's arms), a docstring mention in `tests/save/test_phase4_gate.py`, and doc citations; no
caller in `clockspeed/` outside its own module, nor in `shell/`, `ops/`, `tools/` or `scripts/`.
The module keeps the purge to clear personal-data-bearing copies that pile up across runs.
REMOVE LOST: six files of citation-pin churn, a ledger-cited test body rewritten, and no cleanup
path left. REVERSED BY: a consumer check finding `purge_work_dir` still uncalled once its cleanup
role is served elsewhere - then REMOVE, under a new item.
ADVERSARY HISTORY. Round 1, the deletion-path lens, REFUTED the first candidate: a `\\?\`,
`\\?\UNC\` or `\\localhost\C$` spelling of the work or save root, reachable through the
CLOCKSPEED_WORK_ROOT and CLOCKSPEED_SAVE_ROOT variables (named, never valued), passed the
forbidden-root compare for `purge_work_dir`, `discard_copy` AND `copy_for_read` - the last a write
into the save directory, older than this item. Fix 1 repaired it at the shared compare: a
spelling canonicalisation plus a file-identity ancestor walk, either one refusing, failing closed
on a stat that fails for any reason but absence. Round 2, the path-identity and false-refusal
lens, read NOT REFUTED over 738 probes (agent-reported), and normal reads were not refused. The
landing check then found that `copy_for_read` opened its `.partial` name through a planted link,
no race needed; fix 2 removes a leftover entry at that name, as an entry and never what it
reaches, before the stream. THE VERIFIER on fix 2 REFUTED it: a symlink at the `.partial` name
with the read-only attribute set on the link itself survived the removal, and the "wb" open
followed it - a live one overwrote the target save, a dangling one created a new file in the save
directory. Fix 3 refuses anything left at the partial name after the removal with
`clockspeed/save/workdir.py::DestinationRefusedError`, rendering no path, except a plain
directory (no link, no reparse point), which the open cannot write through and which is kept so
the forced arm of `tests/test_chained_cause.py` still reaches its handler. THE VERIFIER on fix 3
REFUTED it: a link denied delete and read-attributes, inside a copies directory denied
delete-child and list, with the backup and restore privileges disabled, was invisible to
os.path.lexists - the lstat raised and lexists swallowed it - and the open followed it. Fix 4
makes the check one lstat: not found proceeds, any other OSError refuses, a plain directory
passes to the open, anything else refuses. THE VERIFIER on fix 4 CONFIRMED it: 21 real-ACL
attacks with the privileges disabled, every one refused with the fake save root byte-identical,
where the previous candidate in the same harness wrote into the fake save directory in 12 of
them; a normal copy still byte-exact (agent-reported). ADVERSARY LOOP STOPPED BY COST AGAINST
RISK after round 2, three verifier rounds and fix 4 confirmed. Reversed by: a residual below
reached from a real input.
RESIDUALS, recorded and not fixed.
(a) J9: the copies directory swapped between the check and the unlink, which needs a hostile
local process.
(b) The `.partial` re-plant race: a hostile process re-planting a link between the removal and
the open. An exclusive create would narrow it to the dangling-symlink case only, and
`tests/save/test_phase4_gate.py::WRITER_WRITE_SURFACE` pins the open mode.
(c) A file id of 0, as on a FAT drive root, leaves only the spelling compare, reachable only
through an operator-set variable.
(d) ReFS 128-bit file ids are unmeasured.
(e) A false refusal on a case-sensitive directory, which predates this item.
(f) Volumes that share a serial number could be falsely refused.
(g) The per-entry parent check inside the purge cannot be isolated by a failing test: its mutant
survives, because the check differs only inside the J9 window.
(h) The denied-lstat arm reproduces the denial by injection: Python 3.14's os.path.lexists on
Windows is a C builtin that bypasses os.lstat, so the test denies both.
(i) The real-ACL attack that refuted fix 3 is verified against fix 4 but is not a test.
(j) An exclusive create would still follow a dangling symlink on Windows and create its target
(measured).

settings table and its operator steps, all edited by the commit carrying this record.
DECISION: the flip session turns the three on through `gh api` with the existing token. The
repo scope suffices: the private-vulnerability-reporting endpoint's accepted-scopes header names
repo, and its 404 comes from the repository being private. It is a NEW act inside S12a, after
act (ii) - the post-S12 ledger commit read back pushed - and before the S7q lift, which was act
(iii) and is now act (iv); "three acts" becomes "four". Order: private vulnerability reporting,
then secret scanning, then push protection, each read back. Repeating it is harmless. If the API
refuses, the refusal is recorded in the note and the sequence carries on. One conditional line
joins the step-e ask: "(4) if I report that any of the three did not turn on through the API,
switch it on at Settings > Code security."
ALTERNATIVES: the operator by browser, as findings M1 and M2 had it - lost to FLEET item 1,
because it is a reversible change the token can make. At S11 - lost: it reads 404 and null while
the repository is private. After the hold is lifted - lost: the resume table reads that state as
complete, so a halt there would drop the settings. Before acts (i) and (ii) - lost: push
protection would scan the closing ledger push, and a block there would need a bypass that no
halt rule covers.
REVERSED BY: the calls refused on the public repository (the conditional line fires); GitHub
requiring a scope other than repo (it joins the step-e `gh auth refresh -s` line); or the
operator's own words, or a MAIN ruling, that these are set by hand.

scopes gist, read:org, repo and workflow; the private-vulnerability-reporting GET answers 404;

earlier than this record's. This record's first text described a guard that no commit held

DECISION: the checkout root - its drive-letter spelling and the old junction spelling on the
system drive - is NOT personal data. It is not a home path, an account id, a machine name or
a personal identifier (`CLAUDE.md` section 2, `CONVENTIONS.md` section 17). The scrub is for

(`docs/CHANNEL.md` and `ops/fleet_kit/`) carry none.
KEPT, each line and why:

record first copied; the list below names 11): BOOTSTRAP.md:590, `docs/_archive/spike-report-s1-s2-s3-s7.md`
line 541, `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-900.md` lines 762 and 774 (the second is the
folder's 8.3 short name), `docs/item_notes/phase4.md` line 214, `docs/item_notes/phase7.md`

value in `tests/test_queue_loop.py` (now built under `tmp_path`), and the hand-off's line 129
on the s136-land branch only - this branch leaves that line alone, because main's rewritten
hand-off, which carries no spelling, wins at landing. Under the same
rule, the two-part junction spelling on line 761 of `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-900.md`,
which the single-token pattern does not see, is rewritten in the `<repo>` style, and a
markdown-only arm for a quoted drive root beside the quoted folder name pins it.
THE GUARD, as it ships after four fix rounds: CS-1292's path guard is widened from four docs
to every tracked path, against a kept table pinned by line CONTENT - per path, the digests of
the lines that spell the root, each line's text fixing how many spellings it holds - so an
added, changed, moved, doubled or removed spelling fails and an edit that only shifts line
numbers does not. The guard's own file is scanned like any other, its pattern lines kept one
by one. Each path is read by its index mode: a symlink as its blob, the link text git
publishes, never followed; a gitlink not at all, its commit id being hexadecimal; any other
entry from the work tree, or from its index blob when the work tree has no file there. A
link's text and a missing file's blob are counted line by line like any other body, never
failed as unscannable. Any other read error fails the path as unscannable. Only the hash-pinned binaries CS-1292
admitted for the SHA citation gate are skipped, by path and bytes through that gate's own
loader. Each body is read as strict UTF-8, or byte for byte when strict UTF-8 refuses it; a
body carrying a NUL or a wide byte-order mark is also read with every NUL removed and as
lenient UTF-16 and UTF-32 at every alignment; a body that neither strict UTF-8 nor a strict
wide read decodes fails as unscannable. The pattern also reads Git Bash's form JSON-escaped;
a Git Bash form with a doubled separator or a dot segment after its drive letter; a WSL form,
whose branch Cygwin's shares, with a doubled separator after its drive letter or a dot
segment before it; a drive-relative or Git Bash form behind an underscore or a glued
single-letter option; a Git Bash form behind a hyphen, as bash's default-value expansion
writes it with or without the colon, or led by two or three separators, as MSYS's double
slash and a file URI's empty authority write it, a glued option included; the 8.3 short name
behind anything but a letter, a digit included; and backslash-u and backslash-x escapes of a
separator or the colon. It does not read a hyphenated relative segment before a one-letter
segment, with one separator between them or two; a dot, a home tilde or a segment ending in
a digit before one; or a one-letter segment of a URL behind its host. Measured at fix round
2 against fix round 1's pattern, and again at fix round 3 against fix round 2's: the
widening adds no hit on main or on s136-land, and on the branch only the guard's own new
pattern cases. Fix round 4 makes each separator token an atomic group, its escapes tried
before the bare backslash, so a run of separators cannot backtrack exponentially; a test
times three 40-unit runs in a child killed after 10 seconds against a quarter-second budget,
and the change moves no hit on main, on s136-land or on the branch. This widens an existing
test; it is not a new guard. It blocks the public flip because
the acceptance needs it and CS-1292's four-file audit missed 13 files.
ALTERNATIVES: scrub everything, the kept lines included - lost, because it rewrites a settled
entry and an accepted ADR. Scrub nothing and drop the blocker status - lost to MAIN's
`<repo>` rule and to wrong paths in an outsider's clone. Exempt whole kept files - lost,
because a new spelling inside one would slip through. A blanket vendored exemption - lost,
because those files carry none. Runner-up: also keep BOOTSTRAP.md:590, which ADR 0026
decision 4 calls live root text - lost, because that decision records what the move touched,
not a spelling to keep forever.
REVERSED BY: the root moving under a home directory (non-negotiable 3 then covers every
spelling), the operator's own words changing the section 7 entry, or a new ADR moving the
root.
COMMON-MODE RISK: every check here is a text regex run on one tip, by agents reading the same
pattern. Re-grep the LANDED tip, not the branch.
RESIDUAL: a spelling split across lines or assembled by string concatenation is invisible to
any line regex, and so is one in an encoding the pattern does not name (an octal escape,
base64, a drive named through an environment variable such as `%SystemDrive%`, a colon
escaped as `E\:`, a doubly URL-encoded separator or colon, and the like). Removing NULs joins
a spelling's neighbours too, so a letter set against its left edge only through NULs blocks
the pattern as if written glued. A staged blob that differs from the work tree is not read,
nor is the text of a link the work tree holds where the index records a plain file. Read but
pinned by no case, either way: admitting a hyphen also reads a relative segment ending in a
hyphen before the Git Bash form, and two leading separators read a URL or a UNC path whose
host is one letter; none occurs on main or on s136-land. Four or more leading separators
are not read, and a file URI that names a host, `localhost` included, hides a Git Bash form
behind it. The fix loop is held to cost against
risk, the root being ruled not personal data; round 3 closed three plain Git Bash forms the
final adversary planted and found green. One
assembled spelling of the junction root stands, unruled: a negative sample in
`tests/test_scaffold.py::test_home_path_detector_actually_detects`, built from fragments on
purpose; it needs a slice that owns that file. 39 commits on s136-land touch a root spelling
in history; CS-700 should state its handling, though no safety floor applies. The sidecar
root is outside this item
(ADR 0026 lines 39 and 61 stay under CS-1293). The fragment of another tree that

longest measured whole suite (1251.555 s, a 2026-10-09 junit record) rounded up to a whole

### 2026-10-09 - CS-1301 - CLOSED: the canary arms' leaky controls cut collection at their own tmp dir, and every child failure names itself

Cause traced: each forced-red arm's leaky control ran a child pytest from the repo on one
drive against a path under the temp root on another; with no common ancestor the child's
confcutdir stayed at the repo, so its collection walked every ancestor of the temp path and
lstat'ed each sibling, and a sibling a concurrent run's temp cleanup removed mid-walk gave
exit 2 (FileNotFoundError in lstat). Fixed there: `control_pytest` passes
`--confcutdir=<tmp_path>` on the leaky-control child calls only - the forced runs' paths are
in the repo and keep `child_pytest` unchanged; neither leaky control is weakened and no
budget is raised. A non-1 control exit and a forced run that does not fail both report
through `child_failure` - error types and frames only, canary values redacted, an exit past
255 shown in hex as the Windows status it is. New arms in both files load a `-p` plugin that
rmdirs a sibling of `tmp_path` during collection: red before the cut (exit 2, FileNotFoundError
in lstat), green after. Adversary pass (lenses scope, leak, red-for-right-reason): NOT
REFUTED. Landed by cherry-pick with the builder's two commit messages; read back on main: both
files byte-equal to the candidate tip, `python -m pytest tests/test_cs1172_branch_canaries.py
tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py -q -n 2 --dist loadfile` exit 0, `python
tools/drift_guard.py` CLEAN exit 0. Residual filed: the builder's first 30x loop, on a box at

CS-1304. Ruling (adjudicator) on a sibling the brief named,
`tests/save/test_synthetic.py::test_a_failing_builder_call_renders_its_arguments`: FILE
NOTHING. Its `_probe_sandbox` plants a `pytest.ini`, so pytest roots the child and defaults
its confcutdir at the sandbox and neither upward walk runs - measured, a child started from
the repo against a temp sandbox reports both at the sandbox -
and `test_the_probe_sandbox_pins_the_child_rootdir_at_itself` already reddens if the pin goes.

and a BACKLOG line (its trigger would surface as a red suite anyway). Section relocated to

### 2026-10-08 - CS-1280 - DECISION RECORD. NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. NOTHING CLOSED. CS-1280 STAYS OPEN. The tagless-consumer pricing is RULED: option A with a carve-out - priced at its class default in its own counted group only when its payload read clean
Verification: `docs/item_notes/phase5.md` section CS-1280, heading `Filed 2026-10-08 by
CS-1266's builder`, whose `### Acceptance` clause names option A first and is unchanged by this
ruling. Adjudicated in session 133, grounded in the session 133 CS-1280 measurement.
DECISION: option A with a carve-out. A tagless consumer is priced at its class default, in its
own counted group with its own warning, only when its payload read clean: no `mCurrentPotential`
or `mPendingPotential` tag, no production-boost tag decoded or undecoded
(`clockspeed/audit/machines.py::PRODUCTION_BOOST_PROPERTY_NAMES`), and no disagreeing value -
the clean-payload test the elided clock uses (`clockspeed/audit/machines.py::MachineState`,
field `overclock_elided`, as `clockspeed/audit/machines.py::machines_of` computes it), which
reads `mCurrentPotential` decoded or undecoded, the payload read and the disagreeing-value
count; `mPendingPotential` is read by neither that test nor the module
(`clockspeed/audit/machines.py::PROPERTY_OVERCLOCK`), so the carve-out adds it, and the boost
tags the elided clock meets as its own refusal (`MachineState` field `production_boost_tagged`).
Anything else stays a `no-machine-state` omission
(`clockspeed/audit/balance.py::GAP_NO_MACHINE_STATE`): the 10 MinerMk1 and 2 WaterPump tagless
records carry `mPendingPotential` and stay omitted.
WHY: the balance draw is nameplate at clock. `clockspeed/audit/balance.py::clocked_draw_of`
prices every admitted machine at its own clock through
`clockspeed/audit/balance.py::_clocked_outcome`, from `clockspeed/solve/power.py::declared_draw`,
and never consults the producing flag, `MachineState` field `producing`; CS-1263 ruled the same
for the elided clock (its 2026-10-04 record below). 1772 admitted idle machines record 1/10 MW
yet are priced at the class default, so pricing only the tagless ones at 1/10 would mix two
questions in one sum.
ALTERNATIVES, ranked: (D, runner-up) the recorded `mTargetConsumption` - exact and from the save
itself, joinable through `clockspeed/save/world.py::RecordProperties`, field
`reference_targets`, and `clockspeed/save/world.py::WorldParents`; lost because it answers an
instantaneous-draw question the balance does not ask - a live-draw figure would be its own item.
(C) the named omission, the status quo - leaves every non-empty save's draw incomplete. (B) zero
as idle - the confident zero the module is built against (`clockspeed/audit/balance.py`, module
docstring); refuted by the data: lights record their full default, and an idle record reads
1/10 MW, not 0.
Measurement read back by the session 133 CS-1280 measurement, read-only from save copies, counts
only: 41 saves, 3005 built consumers, 2524 considered, 481 omitted, all tagless, across 9
classes, matching CS-1266; library totals 4475 MW at class default against 1271/10 MW recorded.
Acceptance: unchanged - A is the option the CS-1280 `### Acceptance` clause names first.
COMMON-MODE RISK: the measurement and CS-1266 share
`clockspeed/audit/balance.py::_is_power_consumer` and the admission rule,
`clockspeed/audit/machines.py::_is_machine`, so their agreement is not independent.
RESIDUAL: the measured omitted count is re-published once CS-1280 lands; the MinerMk2 draw
anomaly - 4 records reading 12 MW against a declared 15 MW - is filed as CS-1286.

### 2026-10-08 - CS-1285 - DECISION RECORD. NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. NOTHING CLOSED. CS-1285 STAYS OPEN. The D4 fuel rule's design is RULED: accepted fuels on the registry generator, pooled per-class demand against per-fuel supply, and a companion demand card
Verification: `docs/item_notes/phase5.md` section CS-1285, heading `Filed 2026-10-08 by the
session 133 planner`, whose `### Acceptance` clause carries all three rulings. Adjudicated in
session 133, three questions.
Q1, WHERE THE FUELS LIVE. Decision: the accepted fuels are an appended, defaulted field on
`clockspeed/data/registry.py::Generator`, read from `mFuel`. Alternative rejected: a new fuels
module in `clockspeed/data/` - lost because file size is not a seam, and the surface loads the
registry alone: `clockspeed/surface/providers.py::InstalledRegistryProvider` builds it and
`clockspeed/surface/providers.py::StoreAdviceSource` hands the advisor the world and the
registry and nothing else, so a second data module needs a second load path through the surface.
Q2, WHAT SUFFICES. Decision: per built fuel generator class, demand is pooled against the supply
of every fuel it accepts, aggregated per fuel; the rule fires only when the pooled energy falls
short of the class's demand, and a fuel two built classes accept makes both indeterminate.
Alternatives rejected: (1) any single accepted fuel covering demand - it falsely fires under
split supply, where no one fuel covers but the fuels together do, and falsely rejects under
shared supply, where one fuel's supply is counted whole for two classes; (2) indeterminate on
any multi-fuel class - lost because every fuel class on the pinned build accepts several (biomass
6, coal 3, fuel 5, nuclear 3), so the rule would never decide.
Q3, OVER AN INCOMPLETE FLOW. Decision: a companion demand card states each class's nameplate
burn per accepted fuel, claims nothing about supply, and never fires where `power.fuel_supply`
decides. Alternative rejected: accept a mostly-indeterminate rule - lost because node purity is
never in a save (CS-1048), so miners never flow and real worlds read incomplete flows, while the
settled four-domain rule (`CLAUDE.md` section 7) needs fuel chain sizing shipped in v1.
Measurement read back by the session 133 doc filer from the shipped docs on the pinned build,
read-only: `mFuel` is a list of objects with exactly four fields - `mFuelClass`,
`mSupplementalResourceClass`, `mByproduct`, `mByproductAmount` - and no wildcard value, with the
per-class counts above; a fluid's `mEnergyValue` is MJ per litre - the packaging recipe of each
of the five fluids the fuel generator accepts balances under that reading, as do crude oil's and
heavy oil residue's; no generator carries a production exponent, the only exponent keys present
being the two power-consumption ones; the geothermal generator has no `mFuel`.

### 2026-10-08 - CS-700 - DECISION RECORD. NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. NOTHING CLOSED. CS-700 STAYS OPEN. The flip block's order, its two mains and the S7q responder check are RULED
Verification: `docs/item_notes/phase7.md` section CS-700, heading `Filed 2026-10-08 (session
131): the flip block's order, two mains and the S7q responder check`. Ruled in session 131 by a
distinct adjudicator, five questions.
Q1, ORDER. Decision: the citation-set regeneration - `--emit-historical`, its commit, its push
and its tier1 read - runs BEFORE S3 and S7q, and from it until S12a's closing commit no commit
of any kind lands on the main tree's `main`. `--flip-readiness` re-runs read-only at the S7a
baseline, and any non-zero exit aborts. Before emitting, the local tags must equal the
`git ls-remote` tags by name and SHA, and HEAD must equal `origin/main`. A `/done` between the
regeneration and S7a re-stales the set, so none may fall there. Alternatives rejected: (1) the
literal order - the regeneration commit could not be pushed or tier1-graded with the remote
archived, and a red Part 2 would force an unarchive; (2) regenerate now and then `/done` - the
`/done` commit re-stales the set. Reversed by: `--flip-readiness` failing at the baseline under
this order.
Q2, PART 2. Decision: a commit changing only `tools/sha_citation_historical.json` and the
gate's pin line IS a suite-path change, so Part 2 runs once, at the regeneration tip, which is
the S7a tip - `tests/test_sha_citation_gate.py::test_this_tree_cites_only_published_commits`
reads the clone's published refs.
Q3, SHAPE. Decision: interactive sessions only, and the block is the session's last work. The
next hand-off is committed in the records commit just before the regeneration, with a recovery
rule. At step e the session WAITS and never runs `/done` on its own. If the operator ends the
session without the S9 own-words line: unarchive the remote and read it back, remove `STOP` and
INBOX_STOP, treat S7a to S8a as void and keep the bundles, and run a `/done` that adds no SHA
and touches no Part 2 or CS-G03-reversal path. A headless session never starts the block.
Session 131 did not start the block: the operator ended the session before it. Alternatives
rejected: (1) abandoning the block at a brief absence; (2) deferring it on a promise of
presence.
Q4, TWO MAINS. Decision: for S8, S8a and S10 to S12, "local main" is `main` in the S7a rewrite
clone outside the tree, and S10 pushes from it by SHA to an explicit forge URL. The late-commit
check is that the main tree's `main` still equals the S7a baseline SHA. The main tree is reset
onto the adjudicated SHA only after S12a's post-flip reads pass, and the closing ledger commit
is made there.
Q5, S7q PART 2. Decision: the process check adds `ops/loop/inbox_responder.py` and every
kit-spawned headless worker - a command line it cannot read counts as a hit, and the positive
control carries the new strings - and reads the inbox status file idle; INBOX_STOP is written
before the regeneration commit.

batched into the S9 ask.

declined in section 6. Why: no mitigation exists inside the fences, and the exposure is
confirmation of a guess, not disclosure. Adjudicated ACCEPT; the OPERATOR confirmed in their own
words in the main session on 2026-10-04: "the adjudicators finding is fine, im not worried
about". Reversed by: only the operator's own words that the old address must be unconfirmable,

### 2026-10-02 - CS-1225 - OPERATOR RULINGS RECORDED. NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. MAIN speaks for the operator; headless spawns route through the operator's second subscription; arm an inbox responder
Verification: `CLAUDE.md` section 6.1, the paragraph beginning "MAIN SPEAKS FOR THE OPERATOR". The operator pasted a four-part directive into this repository's own session and, asked to confirm it in their own words, replied "confirmed".

THE FOUR PARTS. (1) Every headless `claude` spawn reads `CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BASE_URL` from the user environment store at spawn time, sets it as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in the CHILD environment only, and FAILS CLOSED when the variable is unset or the local proxy port refuses - no direct fallback, no auto-fallback, a usage-limit refusal backs off. The URL is never written into a tracked file; deleting the variable is the operator's kill switch. Prove once with one real spawn checked against the proxy's activity log. (2) Arm autonomous inbox handling; this tree had no responder, so one is built under the usual rules. It SUPERSEDES the CS-1104 "surfacing, never replying" fence for the new responder module only - the lane itself still never replies. (3) MAIN's notes carry the operator's authority, provenance-checked, superseding the 2026-09-22 narrower scope; MAIN never commits here, supplies no credential or physical act, and lifts no safety floor. (4) Report to MAIN by channel note.

RAISED BEFORE CONFIRMATION, so the record shows the operator decided with them in view: whether pooling a second subscription behind a proxy fits the plans' terms is the operator's to judge; and widening MAIN means whoever can write MAIN's outbox can direct changes here, since the SHA-256 check proves the outbox, not the author. CS-1225 carries the routing and CS-1226 the responder.

### 2026-10-02 - CS-1222 - CLOSED. A tracked gate resolves every sha-shaped citation in the authored docs and fails on one that is not a published commit
Verification: `python tools/sha_citation_gate.py` - exit 0, and every run prints its inclusion rule, each excluded token with its class and site, its resolver, and whether the filter-repo discriminator is available - and `python -m pytest tests/test_sha_citation_gate.py -q -p no:randomly`. The merged files are `tools/sha_citation_gate.py`, `tests/test_sha_citation_gate.py` and `.github/workflows/tier1.yml`, where the module runs in the full-history save job and is ignored on the catch-all; plus rewrites of the unpublished slice shas the first sweep found in `docs/LEDGER.md`, `docs/history_notes.md` and three item-notes leaves, each now naming its item and commit subject instead. Arms: `test_an_unresolvable_sha_in_a_guarded_doc_is_refused_by_name`, `test_a_published_sha_in_a_guarded_doc_passes` (the resolvable control, so the gate is not refusing every hex run), `test_an_unpublished_commit_is_refused`, `test_an_ancestor_of_head_not_yet_on_origin_main_passes`, `test_a_not_admitted_run_naming_an_unpublished_commit_fails`, `test_every_escape_shape_is_refused_in_a_ledger_copy`, `test_an_allowlisted_token_that_is_a_published_commit_reddens_the_gate`, `test_an_empty_sweep_is_never_a_pass`, `test_a_shallow_clone_cannot_judge`, `test_every_run_publishes_its_rule_its_exclusions_and_its_discriminator` and `test_this_tree_cites_only_published_commits`.

WHAT THE GATE MEANS BY PUBLISHED. A citation counts only when `<sha>^{commit}` resolves AND that commit is reachable from HEAD, `refs/remotes/origin/main` or a tag, every token resolved in one `git cat-file --batch-check`. A commit object that merely sits in the local store is NOT published: a slice commit that never survived the cherry-pick resolves here and nowhere else, which is exactly the citation this file forbids. The known non-commit classes the filed clause listed - agent and worktree ids, sha256 prefixes, foreign licence pins, blob sha1s, lane run ids, fixture vectors - are excluded by an EXACT-TOKEN allowlist carrying a class and a reason per row, never by a path and never by a shape, and an allowlisted token that is itself a published commit reddens the gate. Hex runs the inclusion rule does not admit are resolved as well, and fail if they name an unpublished commit.

FOUR ADVERSARY REFUTATIONS, ALL REPAIRED BEFORE CLOSE. In `.githooks/pre-commit`, only the text that surfaces the gate's refusal may change.

CONDITIONS THAT ARE PART OF THE GRANT.
1. FAIL CLOSED ON A TIMEOUT, AT EVERY RUNG. A probe that exceeds the bound REFUSES the hook with a non-zero exit. It never falls through to the next ladder rung, because the last rung is `py -3`, the measured toolchain-less interpreter. It never proceeds. The existing fall-through on a plain probe MISMATCH does not change.
2. THE EXIT STATUS IS GRADED BEFORE THE TOKEN. Measured at this grant: under a 3 second bound, `PYTHONINSPECT=1` returned 124 while the capture held the correct token. Any timeout or kill status refuses, whatever the capture says.
3. THE BOUNDING BINARY IS VERIFIED BY BEHAVIOUR, NEVER BY NAME. `C:/Windows/System32/timeout.exe` is on PATH on this box, behind GNU timeout, and has unrelated semantics. Before use, the hook proves that the binary returns 124 when the bound expires and passes an ordinary exit status through. If the binary is absent or fails that check, the hook REFUSES with a message naming the fix. It never runs unbounded.
4. The bound is ONE literal constant, byte-identical in all three hooks and not overridable by environment or config. Its value is justified in the closing entry against a cold-start measurement recorded on this box.
5. BYTE IDENTITY. The probe block, the bound constant, the binary check and the two ladder markers stay byte-identical across the three hooks. `tests/test_hook_interpreter_ladder.py::test_the_three_hooks_carry_a_byte_identical_probe` is extended to pin the marked region.
6. NO GATE WEAKENED. No existing arm in the M1 targeted command is deleted, loosened or newly skipped. The skip count is read, not just the exit code. The value of CLOCKSPEED_PYTHON stays unechoed. The new refusal messages echo no environment value, no interpreter path and no home path. The CS-817 refusal never prints `sys.executable`.
7. CS-817 REFUSES ONLY UNDER `--staged`. `tools/edit_lint_check.py` and `--files` keep today's note, and the existing ruff-absent skip arms in `tests/test_precommit_gate.py` are not edited. The refusal is a blocking finding in the gate report, and it names ruff and the fix.
8. PROOF, CS-816: a REAL commit under `PYTHONINSPECT=1` exits non-zero inside the bound with HEAD unmoved, read with `git rev-parse HEAD` before and after, and the harness sits inside an outer timeout. The same proof is required for the other two measured shapes: a background child holding stdout, and a wrapper that execs python with stdin from /dev/null. Each shape has a control in which a well-behaved interpreter commits. The arms pass on this Windows box and on the ubuntu runner, with any skip carrying a stated reason. Children from hang probes are reaped.
9. PROOF, CS-817: the interpreter is genuinely python and genuinely missing ruff - a venv created without the toolchain, with ruff scrubbed from PATH for that arm. A real commit is refused and HEAD is unmoved. The control uses the same venv with ruff reachable, and the commit passes.
10. END TO END, after the merge and before the close (CLAUDE.md s2.2): in a fresh clone with the hooks installed, stage a violation whose non-ASCII byte is generated at runtime, attempt a real commit, and assert HEAD is unchanged. A hook's presence is not evidence that it fires.
11. ONE COMMIT PER ITEM: CS-816 first, then CS-817. Each commit's diff stays inside its own scope above, so the blast radius of each grant can be audited separately.

BLAST RADIUS. Every commit and push in every worktree and every lane runs these hooks. A bound set too low refuses healthy commits on a cold box. A binary check that is wrong refuses every commit. Both failures are loud and fail closed, and neither passes a bad commit. A mis-scoped CS-817 would block PostToolUse lint on every edit, which is why condition 7 exists. RESIDUAL, NOT GRANTED: a ruff whose version differs from CI's is CS-838's, and a ruff that is present but broken belongs to CS-821.

### 2026-09-24 - CS-956 - CLOSED. Three hook properties measured end to end on real clones, each with a control that produced the opposite answer
Verification: measurement only, no code, so no test name exists - the recorded procedure below IS the verification, and it is reproducible from its own description. The scratch instrument is not tracked and its request bodies carry local paths, so none of it is copied here. The adjudicator ruled CLOSE conditional on this record landing, and recorded as a residual that the interactive arm and the python-resolution arm were not replicated by any second agent.

CS-956 - MEASURED, all three, each with a control that produced the opposite answer. Builder record for the merger; not self-graded.

INSTRUMENT. Client measured: the installed Claude Code CLI (version read from `claude --version` this run; not restated here). A scratch clone P_src of the local repo had planted hooks COMMITTED into its tracked .claude/settings.json; P_cloneA is a fresh `git clone` of it, P_cloneB a fresh clone of the repo with no plant. Every hook runs `python P_probe.py`, which writes a sentinel JSON (booleans and 16-hex digests only, no path, no env) and optionally prints a nonce and exits a chosen code. Each session used a BRAND-NEW CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (zero trust records, verified: projects map empty after the run), the host session's CLAUDE*/ANTHROPIC* env stripped, and a local fake Messages API on 127.0.0.1 (CS band, scratch only) that records every request body - so "reaches the model" is read from the bytes the client actually sent.

(1) TRACKED HOOK IN AN UNTRUSTED FRESH CLONE.
- Headless (-p): FIRES. R1 on P_cloneA: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd sentinels all written, with no trust record anywhere. Controls: R1c (P_cloneB, hook absent) and R1c2 (P_cloneA, --setting-sources user) wrote NONE. The CLI help states the trust dialog is skipped in non-interactive mode; measured consistent.
- Interactive (real console): DOES NOT FIRE while the trust dialog is pending (I1, I3: dialog seen on screen, zero sentinels after 12-25s). After "Yes, I trust this folder" (I3) SessionStart fired within 8s and a trust record was written to the scratch config. Control I2 (trust record seeded) fired at start.
- UNMEASURED: whether a worktree under an already-trusted root inherits trust (assumed, not measured).

(2) HOOK STDOUT ON NON-ZERO EXIT. Nonce per case, SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit:
- exit 0: nonce IN the model request, IN the persisted session JSONL (attachment hook_success). Control that the instrument sees YES.
- exit 1 and exit 3: nonce NOT in any model request; IS in the persisted session JSONL as attachment hook_non_blocking_error (no content key); IS in the stream-json hook_response event.
- exit 2 (SessionStart): stdout in neither the model request nor the session JSONL; only in the stream-json hook event.
So a non-zero-exit hook's stdout never reaches the MODEL; it is recorded in the session file for display.

(3) `python` IN A HOOK COMMAND. R3b (tool mode, one real Bash call): for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and SessionEnd, `python` resolved to an interpreter EQUAL to the shell's `python` (same install), and ruff, mypy and pytest all import; `pythonw` in PreToolUse resolved to the same install, toolchain imports. Resolution is by the client process PATH, identically for every event type; no event is special. A PATH prefix written INSIDE the hook command did NOT redirect it (void arm, not used as a control; likely POSIX PATH splitting on the drive colon - not analysed).

BEARING ON CS-952. (1) SUPPORTS the refusal's premise that tracked wiring fires in a clone (headless always; interactive once trusted) - so a tracked watcher would run where the channel is absent, which is the CS-1101 reason. (2) CONFIRMS the adversary's claim for the model context: a non-zero exit loses its stdout to the model. The retired EXIT-3 half stays retired (CS-1101); this is the measurement CS-1107 says the prose lacked. Precision: the stdout is still written to the session file, so "loses its stdout" is true of the model, not of the transcript file. (3) Not load-bearing in CS-952; it shows PreToolUse's interpreter guard protects no event the others lack, since all resolve the same way.

Evidence (scratch, reproducible): P_cs956/P_setup.py, P_run.py, P_prop2.py, P_prop3.py, P_interactive.py, P_fakeapi.py, P_probe.py; outputs under P_cs956/out (fires/, req/, *.stream.jsonl). The request bodies and cfg_* dirs contain local paths - never copy them into a tracked file.

### 2026-09-24 - CS-1176 - CLOSED, CONDITIONAL ON CI GREEN ON THE PUSHED TIP. A deleted provenance manifest is restored from history and never re-seeded, and a first-add row that entered any manifest version outside the seed reddens naming it
Verification: `python -m pytest tests/test_provenance_manifest.py tests/test_provenance_stamp.py -q -p no:randomly`. The mechanism is in `tools/provenance_stamp.py`. The acceptance mutation is `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_cs1176_a_reseed_after_a_deletion_is_refused_and_the_red_names_the_lift` beside the pristine control `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_cs1176_the_seeded_repo_is_green_pristine`; the real-tree arm is `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_no_first_add_row_postdates_the_seed`; the review findings are pinned by `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_cs1176_f1_a_row_that_left_and_returned_through_a_reseed_is_named`, `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_cs1176_f2_a_stale_branch_seed_merged_back_is_named`, `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_cs1176_r1_a_replace_graft_cannot_hide_a_reseed` and `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_cs1176_the_before_anchor_is_the_gap_commits_parent_not_the_last_version`; the refusal arms are `tests/test_provenance_stamp.py::test_bootstrap_refuses_once_history_holds_a_manifest`, `tests/test_provenance_stamp.py::test_bootstrap_refuses_while_only_a_remote_ref_holds_a_manifest` and `tests/test_provenance_stamp.py::test_bootstrap_refuses_on_a_detached_head_with_no_refs_at_all`; the message arms are `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_a_missing_manifest_is_red_naming_the_restore_and_never_the_seed` and `tests/test_provenance_stamp.py::test_check_on_a_missing_manifest_names_it_and_never_recommends_the_seed`.

THE SEED REFUSES WHEREVER A MANIFEST EVER EXISTED. `bootstrap` refuses when HEAD's history, or any ref - tags and `refs/remotes` included - ever held `tools/provenance.tsv`, and names the restore, `git checkout <rev> -- tools/provenance.tsv`, at the newest commit that holds it. The missing-manifest messages, from the arm and from the tool, never recommend the seed, and say to restore BEFORE editing any file.

THE RE-SEED ARM. A first-add row must be in the seed and in every later manifest version, walked with `--full-history` so no side of a merge is simplified away. A gap - versions in which the row is absent - is forgiven only when the path's blob in the PARENT of the gap-opening commit (any merge parent holding the row) equals its blob at the gap-closing commit, so a revert, a typo row fixed the next commit and the advised restore stay green, while a row that left and returned through a re-seed is named. `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` is set in the arm and in the tool, so a local replace graft cannot hide a version.

REVIEW RECORD. Round one was REFUTED twice: F1 a reused path, F2 a stale-branch seed merged back, F3 real-tree wiring no mutation had exercised, F4 an orphan squash. Round two was REFUTED: false reds on a revert and on a typo version, a detached HEAD with no refs was seeded, and the shallow-clone message did not name the truncation. Round three was REFUTED: anchoring the gap at the last manifest version made honest edits red. Round four found no acceptance-breaking bypass across merge, octopus, criss-cross and evil-merge histories, and the residual graft bypass it did find was fixed. The adjudicator ruled CLOSE on the final candidate, conditional on CI green on the pushed tip.

RESIDUALS, AS THE ADJUDICATOR RECORDED THEM. The re-seed arm skips on a shallow clone, so the depth-1 CI leg does not grade it. A history rewrite that deletes every ref reaching a manifest, leaving one only in the reflog, is not searched. Restoring the manifest and then editing a file to lifted bytes in a later commit is green - indistinguishable from authoring. Deleting the manifest, making an honest edit and then restoring is a permanent fail-closed red whose recovery through `rm` and a re-`add` is unproven; that is CS-1179.

### 2026-09-24 - CS-1175 - CLOSED, CONDITIONAL ON CI GREEN ON THE PUSHED TIP. A narrowed secret rule reddens the credential row naming the rule and what changed, against a derived fingerprint, and no canary value renders under `--showlocals`
Verification: `python -m pytest tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py tests/test_cs1167_credential_canary_coverage.py tests/test_cs1172_branch_canaries.py -q -p no:randomly`. The mechanism is in `tools/outbound_gate.py`. The narrowing arms are `tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py::test_a_narrowed_rule_reddens_the_row_by_rule_and_change`, `tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py::test_a_widening_reddens_too`, `tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py::test_every_rule_has_a_recorded_fingerprint_and_none_is_stale` and `tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py::test_the_recorded_population_reaches_every_kind`; the re-record command is `tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py::test_print_fingerprints_emits_the_table_as_source`; the parser half is `tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py::test_a_missing_private_regex_module_names_every_rule`; the echo half is `tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py::test_showlocals_forced_red_output_renders_no_canary`, with the canary arms it forces red in `tests/test_cs1167_credential_canary_coverage.py` and `tests/test_cs1172_branch_canaries.py` reshaped so they hold no canary in a rendered local. `tools/precommit_gate.py` was not touched.

THE FINGERPRINT ROUTE, FOR ALL FOUR NARROWING KINDS. The acceptance offered canaries or a derived fingerprint, and canaries cannot grade a narrowing without a hand list: a canary derived from the live rule is derived from the narrowed rule and matches it, and a hand-written one is exactly the hand list the acceptance excludes. So each rule's fingerprint is derived from its compiled parse and records its flags, every quantifier with its bounds, every character class, category and dot node with its members, and a 16-hex SHA-256 of the rule's source, so a change the structured fields do not describe is still named as a change. A narrowing or a widening reddens the row naming the rule and the change; a rule with no recorded fingerprint, and a fingerprint for no such rule, are each named. `python tools/outbound_gate.py --print-fingerprints` prints the table as source for a deliberate re-record and never writes a file.

THE ECHO HALF, MEASURED. With the canary arms forced red under `--showlocals`, 44 canary values rendered before the repair and 0 after.

THE COMMENT WAS FALSE, AND NOW STATES WHAT HAPPENS. The module claimed a missing private regex parser would be named underivable; measured, a missing `re._parser` crashed the gate at import. Now a missing `re._parser` or `re._constants` leaves the gate running, exit 3 on a clean payload, with every rule named underivable.

REVIEW RECORD. The round-one acceptance adversary REFUTED the first candidate on three counts: the unquantified `\d` in the PuTTY rule was fingerprinted by no field, docstrings claimed "any change" was caught when it was not, and there was no re-record command. The round-one reproduce adversary did NOT REFUTE. After the repair the round-two adversary did NOT REFUTE, and the adjudicator ruled CLOSE, conditional on CI green on the pushed tip.

RESIDUALS, AS THE ADJUDICATOR RECORDED THEM. An exception raised in a helper frame, rather than an assertion, can still render canary locals under `--showlocals`, and `CANARY_SUITES` in `tests/test_cs1175_rule_narrowing.py` is a hand-kept list - both are CS-1177. A Python minor that changes `re._parser` output fails closed with exit 3, and is re-recorded through `--print-fingerprints`. The ubuntu leg was not run before the push. A scoped inline flag such as `(?i:...)` is caught only by the source digest, as a change outside the structured fields. COMMON MODE: every grading reads `re._parser`, so a defect in that parse is shared by the rule's reading, its fingerprint and the arm that grades it.

### 2026-09-22 - CS-1165 - CLOSED. Every tracked and untracked-unignored file must be accounted for in a produced provenance manifest, so a lift with no byte pin and no register row goes red naming it - branded or not
Verification: `python -m pytest tests/test_provenance_manifest.py tests/test_provenance_stamp.py tests/test_unregistered_lift.py -q -p no:randomly`. The manifest is `tools/provenance.tsv`, produced and maintained only through `tools/provenance_stamp.py`; the grading arm is `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_every_tracked_path_has_a_manifest_row` beside `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py::test_no_authored_row_is_a_near_duplicate_of_a_vendored_file`, and the branded half is `tests/test_unregistered_lift.py::test_no_unaccounted_file_spells_a_sibling_namespace_marker`.

THE ORACLE IS THE BYTES AND A PRODUCED RECORD, NOT A LIST OF EXPECTED VENDORINGS. The first cut graded only a lift that spells a sibling's namespace, and an adjudicator ruled that progress rather than closure, because the acceptance itself names a manifest every file must be entered in. Its vendored rows must equal the register in both directions, its item ids must resolve against the roadmap or this ledger, and an authored row whose lines overlap a vendored file by half or more is red. The stamp tool refuses an unclassified file, an unknown id, and an authored stamp on a near-duplicate; it has no bulk mode, and its one-time seed refuses once the manifest exists.

MUTATION, on the real tree: a plain copy of the declared fork at a new path with nothing added anywhere is red naming it, staged or not; stamping it authored through the tool is refused at full overlap; appending the row by hand is red on overlap. A de-branded copy with its docstring replaced and an identifier renamed was still refused. It passes in a depth-one clone and the whole suite run there as CI runs it, and a suite run leaves no untracked unignored file behind to flake it.

THE SEED FOUND A DEFECT IN ITSELF BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The id pattern read a block name as an id, stamping one row with an item that never existed; the builder stopped rather than hand-editing the row, the pattern was repaired in the tool and the arm test-first, and the re-seed carried the real id.

WHAT STAYS GREEN, AND IS NOT CLAIMED. A file lifted from a sibling that was never vendored here and stamped authored with a real id is a recorded false claim rather than a silent lift - no check inside this tree can see it. Deleting the manifest and re-running the seed would classify every unstamped file as authored, and nothing notices a re-seed; that is CS-1176. A lift edited until its overlap falls under half passes. And a DISCLOSURE: an adversary on this candidate compared manifest files against sibling trees on this machine read-only, against the ruling for this item that no sibling tree be read; no sibling path or byte entered a tracked file, and it found byte-identical copies only for the two registered files.

### 2026-09-20 - CS-946 - FROZEN-FILE GRANT. NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. NOTHING CLOSED. CS-946 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it. Granted by an adjudicator BEFORE the edit
Verification: this record is the grant; the repair closes under its own later entry. The measurement that decides it is reproducible in one minute and is the whole basis: `ruff format --check` against `ops/loop/slots.py` at its real path with the project config is exit 0, and against the identical bytes copied to a temp directory is exit 1. `ruff check` is 0 findings in place against 10 from the copy. Scope is `stage_for_lint`, `run_ruff`, `run_ruff_format` and the finding-name lookup in `tools/precommit_gate.py`, plus the docstrings in those four and in `ruff_config_args`. Nothing else in that file may change.

THE COLLISION. Vendoring `ops/loop/slots.py` byte-identical from four carrier trees - 9627 bytes, sha256 `71fa2a683f2eaa04dd61feb2bebc646b5f9086e692c5acc05a9239de49d07d1b` - put two rules head to head that neither side could yield on. `CLAUDE.md` section 4 says a guard refusing a vendored file takes the EXEMPTION, never the file. Section 6 freezes `tools/precommit_gate.py`, whose own module header states it has NO path allowlist of any kind, a deliberate `CONVENTIONS.md` section 15.1 decision on the ground that a guard which skips what it covers is worse than a loud one. Byte-identity IS the CS-946 deliverable, so reformatting the file was never available: a reformatted shared mutex is a SECOND mutex.

THE FACT NOBODY HAD, and it is why the first exemption failed. **Ruff resolves `exclude` and `per-file-ignores` against THE INVOCATION'S WORKING DIRECTORY** - not against the config file's location, and not against the absolute path. `force-exclude = true` is necessary and not sufficient. Under `--staged` the gate writes index bytes to a temp directory as `<tmp>/u0000/<basename>` and invokes ruff from the repository root, so no exclusion pattern the project can write will ever match. The exemption filed in `pyproject.toml` made `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` and `mypy` all exit 0 while the gate went on refusing, and the reason was invisible from either side.

**THE SHARED ASSUMPTION THAT FAILED IS THE REUSABLE PART.** The slice's `pyproject.toml` work and BOTH alternative candidates rested on one untested premise - that ruff resolves those keys against the config file's directory. It is false. The comment block written to justify `force-exclude` argues its case at length and never mentions the working directory, which is exactly why the exemption read correct on the tree and still lost to the gate. Three independent-looking approaches were one assumption wearing three hats.

THE PERMITTED CHANGE, and why it is delegation rather than an allowlist. Each staged unit is written at its REPO-RELATIVE path under the temp root, and ruff is invoked FROM that root with the real project config. Measured, that restores both bands - format exit 0 and "All checks passed!" - while a malformed file at a non-excluded path is still refused at exit 1. **The population the gate checks is unchanged: every staged unit is still read, still linted, still format-checked, and no path literal enters the gate.** The gate already delegates WHICH RULES EXIST to `pyproject.toml` through `--config`; this makes that delegation honest instead of accidentally partial, and the header sentence stays true verbatim.

THE HONEST COUNTER, ruled on rather than glossed. After this change an unfrozen `pyproject.toml` can remove a file from ruff's view and the gate cannot see the skip - a skip capability relocated into a file that is not frozen. Accepted and bounded: it lands inside the ruff band, which is already fail-open by design at every rung; the charset, secret, PII, world-token, path and syntax checks are untouched and unreachable from `pyproject.toml`; and an arm pins the exclusion list against a DERIVED vendored roster, so it cannot grow by hand.

WHAT WAS REJECTED, each on a measurement rather than a preference. A carve-out inside the gate IS the path allowlist the header forbids and makes the frozen file the list that grows. Relocating the vendored file is dead: `staged_paths` runs `git diff --cached --name-only` over the whole index, so no tracked path escapes. Setting a disk path when index bytes equal worktree bytes repairs a genuinely dead branch in fewer lines, but it hands ruff a WORKING-TREE path under `--staged` - the exposure this tree's own tests document as exclusive to `--files`, one dropped `--check` away from a commit hook rewriting the operator's tree - and it only helps when the file is clean, making a tier-0 gate's verdict depend on whether a file happens to be dirty.

A SECOND DEFECT FOUND AND FILED SEPARATELY. `ruff_config_args`' docstring reassures the reader that the staged-versus-project divergence "cannot change what blocks, because the blocking band is the prefix list". That was true when written. The FORMAT diagnostic is a second blocking band added later and is not governed by that prefix list, and `format.exclude` is precisely a config key that changes it. A narrowly true sentence inside a broadly false paragraph - the docstring-rot shape this project has already paid for twice today.

THE STANDING ALTERNATIVE, recorded so it is not lost. The long-run correct answer is a JOINT RE-PIN of the shared file at a ruff-formatted digest. It removes the exemption rather than housing it, and retires both this grant and the derived-roster arm. CS may not perform it unilaterally - a re-pin is a joint act and a round is open - so it is raised on the channel rather than taken.

BLAST RADIUS, and what the repair must verify beyond a green suite. This file is the tier-0 block on every commit AND the engine behind the `PostToolUse` edit check, which passes no root - so the nested-staging combination is NEW after this change and must be re-measured rather than assumed. Fail-open is far worse than fail-closed here, because CI runs only the TIP of a push and a hole rides in under every intermediate commit. Required: a REAL commit in a throwaway repository with hooks wired, asserting HEAD is unchanged on a violation and moves on a clean file - never inferred from the gate's exit code; one run proving a world token, a non-ASCII byte and a secret still block in the same invocation; the edit-check path exercised on one edited file; and a ubuntu CI run, read by its SKIP COUNT rather than its exit code, because separator and relative-path handling is the one thing that differs.

remainders read on its behalf - and it is exactly what made the omission silent in a caller
that did want them. The two shipped readings had been landing for two cycles into an

un-derived sweep and reported `assert 3 == 0` - all three pairs read zero remainders by a

### 2026-09-18 - CS-1147 - CLOSED. The ration blocking-protocol arm no longer races the child it measures

**THE DEFECT.** `tests/ops/test_suite_ration.py`'s `_HOLD_THEN_RELEASE` child called
`ration.release(...)` and THEN wrote its `child_released` marker. Between those two
statements the slot was FREE and the marker ABSENT, so a parent acquiring in that
window entered its body having seen two of the three protocol signals and the arm
failed naming the ration for its own child's ordering. Measured on run 35385454932
at `ba71cca`, job `clean-checkout probe (windows-latest)`.

**THE REPRODUCTION, BEFORE ANY REPAIR.** Widening the gap to 0.5s made it
deterministic and produced the byte-identical CI assertion:
`assert ['child_acquired', 'go'] == ['child_acquired', 'child_released', 'go']`.
With the marker written FIRST the SAME 0.5s widening passes. `_POLL_S` is
unchanged at 0.02 and no pre-existing timeout moved - the fix is the statement
order, and the marker's presence is now implied by the slot being free.

**THE ARM HAD NO TEETH, AND AN ADVERSARY FOUND IT, NOT THE AUTHOR.** The first
repair was committed claiming the teeth clause discharged on the strength of a
LIVE never-releasing child failing in 124.89s. An independent refutation pass
measured the CANONICAL mutant - delete the `release` call, change nothing else -
and it was GREEN in 0.15s, before the repair and after it. The child EXITED the
instant it stopped holding, the ration correctly reclaims a dead holder's slot,
and nothing in the arm distinguished a release from a death. The child now waits
for a `parent_done` dismissal written after the measurement, so it is ALIVE
across the parent's acquire and the release is the only door into the slot. That
same canonical mutant now fails in 120.33s.

**WHAT MAKES THE HANG A RED.** `hold_suite_slot` takes no ceiling in this arm by
design, so a child that never releases would have HUNG it. The parent's wait seam
now bounds its own patience at `_MAX_PARENT_WAITS`, whose floor is the seam's own
real `time.sleep(_POLL_S)` - at least 120s of actual sleeping whatever the runner
is doing. It is NOT derived from the child's `go` deadline; the first version of
the comment claimed it was, and the two clocks measure disjoint intervals.

**THE SIBLING SWEEP, LISTED IN FULL AS THE ACCEPTANCE REQUIRES.** The module has
exactly two child scripts and two parent-side readers of a child marker:

| Site | Ordering | Carried the defect |
|---|---|---|
| `_HOLD_THEN_RELEASE`, `child_released` vs `release` | marker announced state about to be TORN DOWN, so it must precede it | YES - this item |
| `_HOLD_THEN_RELEASE`, `child_acquired` vs `try_acquire` | marker announces state already ESTABLISHED, so following is the safe direction | no |
| `_HOLD_FOREVER`, `child_acquired` vs `try_acquire` | same safe direction | no |
| `_await_file` at both call sites | existence vs content | YES, a SECOND family the sweep as filed would have missed |

`_await_file` returned the instant a path existed, and `write_text` creates and
truncates before it writes, so both process arms could read an empty marker and
crash in `int(...)` with an uncaught `ValueError` - an error of unknown provenance
on exactly the contended runner this item was filed from. It now waits for a byte,
which closes the window at the reader rather than asking every writer to be atomic.
An explicit 0.3s empty-marker window planted in BOTH children now passes.

Verification: `python -m pytest tests/ops/test_suite_ration.py -q` is 12 passed.
For the teeth, delete `ration.release(claim["token"], root=root)` from
`_HOLD_THEN_RELEASE` and re-run the blocking arm: it must FAIL on
`_MAX_PARENT_WAITS`, taking about two minutes. For the race, insert
`time.sleep(0.5)` between the child's released-marker write and its release: it
must still pass.

### 2026-09-18 - CS-1145 - CLOSED. The tier 1 duration arms bracket the reported figure between clocks they read themselves

**THE DEFECT.** Two arms allowed the staged duration plus a fixed two seconds. The
step computes its figure as `$(date +%s) - TIER1_STARTED`, so the reading is the
staged duration PLUS the wall clock between the harness staging the start and the
shell reading its own clock - a property of the runner, not of the step. The
windows-latest leg of tier 2 spent three seconds there and the lane went red with
nothing wrong in the workflow; the ubuntu leg of the same job passed.

**THE REPAIR IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN A WIDER NUMBER.** The arm reads the clock
before the spawn and again after the process returns. `floor` is monotonic, so the
shell's own read lies between those two, and the reading is bounded below by the
staged duration and above by the later read. A slower runner WIDENS the bracket
instead of breaking it; on an idle box it closes to zero slack. No constant sizes
it, which is the point - CS-1133 and CS-1134 exist because bands in this lane were
sized by guesswork twice, and a third guess was available and refused here.

**A DISCLOSED LIMIT, recorded because it is not obvious from the code.** The bracket
alone cannot kill a step that hardcodes a figure equal to the staged value: the
within-budget arm survives that mutant. The stall arm kills it, and so does the
over-budget arm, which stages a different duration. The repair is three arms for
that reason and not because three reads better.

**MEASURED BOTH WAYS BY THE MERGER, not only by the builder.** With the step mutated
to ignore `TIER1_STARTED`, all three arms go red; pristine, all three pass. The
mutation was confirmed present at all three call sites before the run, since a
mutant that never applied is indistinguishable from one that survived. The workflow
was restored from a byte snapshot and `git status` confirmed clean.

Verification: `tests/test_tier1_budget.py`, arms

`test_a_slow_harness_does_not_push_the_reading_outside_what_the_clock_allows` and

### 2026-09-17 - CS-1125 - CLOSED. The mypy gate's arms run under an environment they build, not the one they inherit

**WHAT CHANGED.** `tests/test_mypy_gate.py` built its throwaway projects correctly and then ran
mypy under whatever the shell handed it, so an inherited variable decided what the arm reported.
`PYTHONPATH=.` - how this lane and any developer runs the suite from the repo root - resolved the
trunk module's import away from the excluded leaf beside it, and the exclusion arm failed against an
empty mapping while mypy printed success. Every mypy run in the file now goes through one helper
that builds its environment from an ALLOWLIST of what the interpreter needs to start, matched
without regard to letter case, pins the child's IO encoding, pins the user site directory off, and
names its config file explicitly so no user or XDG config is discovered. The helper reads raw bytes
and decodes them in the test's own thread. `subprocess.run` at every site carries the file's own
runaway cutoff under one name, so the three call sites cannot drift.

**WHY AN ALLOWLIST.** A denylist was the first fix and it leaked twice: `FORCE_COLOR` reaches mypy
as the fallback its own colour code reads, and `PYTHONIOENCODING` set to a UTF-16 codec breaks the
output parse. A denylist that must name every variable mypy or its interpreter reads is the shape
this project has already measured leaking four times.

**TESTS.** Ambient arms that PLANT each hazard and prove it is live: the three `PYTHONPATH`
spellings, `FORCE_COLOR` together with `TERM` (on POSIX mypy colours only when `setupterm` finds a
terminfo entry, so the plant carries both), a UTF-16 IO encoding, a `.pth` in the per-user site
directory located through `site` rather than a hardcoded layout, and a user mypy config planted in
a fake home and XDG root. Each arm is RED when the environment is inherited and GREEN under the
controlled one; the discovery control still reddens when mypy genuinely stops filtering discovery.
A session fixture builds one warm mypy cache from an empty project and every run gets its own copy,
which halved the arms' local wall time without letting two runs share state.

**HOW IT WAS GRADED.** Builder, four adversary rounds on frozen SHAs, and a real CI reading. The
rounds refuted, in order: the `FORCE_COLOR` fallback; the per-user site directory and the user
config; and then ubuntu CI itself, where the `FORCE_COLOR` plant was VACUOUS because the runner
sets no `TERM` - an arm that proved the hazard on Windows and proved nothing on Linux. The cache
lens found nothing. The repo-wide subprocess-timeout guard then reddened on CI because the builder's
scoped runs never ran it; that is the fourth time this session a scoped-only run hid a repo-wide
guard. Green on both platforms at the merged candidate.

**MEASURED, NOT FIXED.** The tier-1 guard shard now runs over its stated budget and under its
ceiling with the warm cache already in place, so the shard carrying these arms has little headroom.

### 2026-09-17 - CS-1128 - CLOSED. The separate-guard ceiling is reachable by the tautology check

planted in the live file and the three citation-family modules were run: `412 passed`, exit 0.

existed and simply never read that source.

names out of a module's `FORGIVENESS_TABLES`, and `NOT_A_CITATION_GUARD` sits in the OTHER half
of the registry pair, recorded as forgiving no citation. `tests/test_bare_path_citations.py`'s
own `FORGIVENESS_TABLES` is empty, so a caller over that source reading only that half would
have had nothing to look for and would have reported a confident zero.

fence the item's acceptance states and the route CS-1127 took for a different table. Moving
`NOT_A_CITATION_GUARD` into `FORGIVENESS_TABLES` would buy reach by asserting that the table
forgives citations. It does not: it excuses a MODULE from the walk, and its recorded reason says
so. A claim about what a table forgives is argued, never typed to satisfy a checker. What the
function names as the offence is a bound whose value expression mentions WHAT IT BOUNDS, and that
is indifferent to whether the subject forgives anything - a table that forgives nothing is still
bounded, and this ceiling is that case.

through a graded seam, so nothing was withdrawn from `BOOTSTRAP.md`. The 2026-09-06 correction
appended beside this item's filing already recorded that the data exists; this entry does not restate
it.

**THE DEFECT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND, and it was in the probe rather than in the tree.** The pinned
build ships TWO build-gun producer spellings: the common one on 549 recipes and a second on exactly
one, `Recipe_SpaceElevator_C`. A first probe written for this item transcribed the common spelling
alone. It measured one recipe short and a join one building short, and the miss was
indistinguishable from a buildable the game ships no cost for - the shape of a silent wrong answer,
not of a crash. Matching the marker reproduces the leaf's own figures exactly: 550 build-gun recipes,
545 carrying ingredients, and 65 of 68 modelled buildings joined.

### 2026-09-17 - SESSION 102 - NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. NOTHING CLOSED. Tier1 and tier2 went red on the CS-1124 slice's merge, once for a CI account token in a comment and once for a test that graded real elapsed time

**THE RED.** tier1 run 35210434772 and tier2 run 35210435082, both on 72e7d46, both failure. Two
causes, kept separate because they are different classes:

  `tests/shell/test_shell_assets.py::test_no_shell_file_carries_this_machines_own_identifiers`
  flags it on CI only, because only there is that name the machine's own. The same class as the

  envelope, on a loaded ubuntu runner. The code under test was not wrong; the arm measured the host.

**THE FIX.** bfb32e4, merged at 2e08639. The comment is reworded. `shell/lib/state.js` exports a
`clock` seam (`now`, `sleep`) and the retry loop reads time and pauses through it exclusively. The
deadline arms in `shell/test/state.test.js` run on a fake clock whose pause advances it exactly, and
grade exact give-up points and the backoff shape - among them "a rename held past the deadline fails
loudly, at the deadline and not after it" and "the rename deadline holds when the wall clock steps
backwards". One real-time arm, "the real clock and the real pause are wired - a smoke arm, bounded
generously", keeps the real pause wired and is bounded at four times the deadline. The fixing session
reported both mutants - the deadline check removed, the clock seam bypassed - red, and the pre-push
whole suite green.

**VERIFIED ON THE MERGE ITSELF.** tier1 run 35218221145 on 2e08639 success; dispatched tier2 run
35218221886 on 2e08639 success in all seven jobs.

**THE LANE.** It stopped itself after five cycles, recording `stopped_by=ci_red`, and was relaunched
from a clean fast-forwarded worktree after green.

an injected clock, and keep at most one real-time smoke arm with a generous multiple of the bound.
