on the channel measured that class in its own tree: a live token tracked from its initial
commit for 133 days, green on every working-tree check.

**WHAT SHIPPED.** `tests/secret_sweep_guard.py` derives two populations and scans them;
`tests/test_secret_sweep.py` holds the arms and the controls. Merged files:
`tests/secret_sweep_guard.py`, `tests/test_secret_sweep.py`.

- THE TRACKED TREE, read from the working tree through `git ls-files`.
- EVERY REACHABLE BLOB, walked with `git rev-list --objects --all` and streamed out of one
  `git cat-file --batch` process. This is the only population that sees a credential a
  later commit removed.

**THE DETECTOR IS IMPORTED AND THE ARM PROVES IT BY SUBSTITUTION RATHER THAN BY PROSE.**
`test_the_sweep_reads_the_gates_own_pattern_list` replaces `SECRET_PATTERNS` on the gate
module with a rule that matches an ordinary word and requires the verdict to follow it. A
copy of the list inside the test family would survive that replacement and report the same
answer, which is exactly the failure the clause names. The ADMISSION rule is imported too -
`classify_for_read` and `accept_bytes` decide what is scanned - so the sweep reports only
things a commit could actually have been blocked for, and the arm named below for it
pins both directions of that on one call.

**THE GATE IS LOADED BY PATH, NOT IMPORTED AS `tools.precommit_gate`, and that is
mechanical rather than stylistic.** `tools/` carries no `__init__.py`, so a package import
puts the same source under two module names and the repo-wide mypy gate refuses the whole
tree with `Source file found twice under different module names` before checking anything
else. Measured in this cycle: the first draft did exactly that.
`tests/test_precommit_gate.py::load_gate` makes the same choice for the same reason, and this module registers under a DISTINCT name
so neither copy can be monkeypatched out from under the other.

**THE ARM'S FIRST RUN REPORTED THE MODULE THAT OWNS IT, AND THAT IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE
IN THIS ENTRY.** Three call sites in `tests/test_secret_sweep.py` spelled a field name, an
equals sign and a quote next to each other while building a fixture - the gate's
quoted-literal rule exactly - and the live arm reported all three. They now go through
`planted_line`, which takes the field name as a PARAMETER so the shape never occurs in
source. A guard whose first act is to redden on its own author is a guard with teeth.

**THE SYNTHETIC FIXTURE THAT MUST NOT REDDEN IS A MECHANISM, NOT A FORGIVENESS TABLE.**
Nothing anywhere forgives this file. The fixture is ASSEMBLED from fragments and never
spelled - this tree's oldest answer to the same question, and the one
`tools/outbound_gate.py::CANARY_CREDENTIAL` already uses. The joined value matches the AWS
rule; the source line that builds it matches nothing. So a real credential added to the
fixture file would redden the live arm exactly as it would in any other file.

**THE SIBLING SWEEP IS THE CHARSET RULE, SWEPT RATHER THAN FILED.** It shares the root
cause exactly - a check that reads only what is changing now cannot see a byte that already
landed - so `check_charset` is run over both populations with its own arms and its own
discriminating control. CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 4 is the rule it answers. The PII rule is
the same class and is NOT swept: its matchers are derived from the machine's own save
directory, so a tracked-tree arm over them would report a different population on every box
and could not run at all where no game is installed.

**A SHA THAT IS COUNTED AND NOT READ IS THE FAILURE THIS DESIGN GUARDS AGAINST.** A reader
that quietly drops an object produces a report byte-identical to a clean one, so
`blob_findings` RAISES on an object the reader did not yield.
`test_a_blob_the_reader_never_yields_is_a_failure_rather_than_a_pass` pins it.

**WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHERE, MEASURED THIS CYCLE RATHER THAN ESTIMATED.** The module runs
in roughly a minute on a full-history checkout, and effectively all of it is the history
leg: the tracked tree is a few hundred files and a few seconds, while the reachable-blob
population on this box is three thousand objects and hundreds of megabytes. THE COST DOES
NOT LAND ON TIER 1. `actions/checkout@v5` defaults to depth 1, so every tier-1 job and
tier2's `suite` job reach the tip tree only and the blob population collapses to roughly
the tracked one. The full walk is paid where history exists: the pre-push hook, and tier
2's `clean-checkout-probe`, which sets `fetch-depth: 0` and carries a 30-minute budget.
That placement was chosen against CS-896, whose note records the tier-1 fast shard sitting
inside the noise band of its own cutoff; adding a minute there would have been a knowing
regression.

**ON A SHALLOW CHECKOUT THE HISTORY LEG IS THE TIP TREE AND NOTHING MORE.** That is stated
rather than rounded up. The population is whatever the checkout reaches, and the
anti-vacuity arm pins that it is never smaller than the tracked tree - so a walk that
returned nothing fails rather than rendering clean.

**THE LIVE MEASUREMENT.** Zero findings on both rules and both populations - every tracked
file, and every blob reachable from every ref on this worktree. NO POPULATION SIZE IS
WRITTEN HERE, deliberately: both counts move with the next commit, and a figure in prose is
a lie with a timestamp on it. The arms pin ZERO findings, so they cannot go stale; the
anti-vacuity arms pin the POPULATION instead, because a sweep of nothing and a sweep that
found nothing render the same way, and the verifier re-derived both populations
independently and found the scanned set equal to the tracked set with nothing declined.

**TESTS.** `tests/test_secret_sweep.py` - 13 arms.
`test_a_planted_credential_in_a_tracked_file_is_reported`,
`test_the_assembled_spelling_of_the_same_credential_is_not_reported`,
`test_the_sweep_reads_the_gates_own_pattern_list`,
`test_an_item_the_gate_itself_would_decline_is_not_scanned`,
`test_a_planted_non_ascii_byte_is_reported`, `test_a_planted_blob_is_reported`,
`test_a_blob_the_reader_never_yields_is_a_failure_rather_than_a_pass`,
`test_no_tracked_file_carries_a_credential_the_gate_would_block`,
`test_no_tracked_file_carries_a_byte_outside_the_charset_rule`,
`test_every_tracked_python_and_markdown_file_is_actually_scanned`,
`test_no_reachable_blob_carries_a_credential_the_gate_would_block`,
`test_no_reachable_blob_carries_a_byte_outside_the_charset_rule`,
`test_the_blob_population_covers_at_least_the_tracked_tree`.

**TIER 2 PAID, AND THE VERDICT IS QUOTED RATHER THAN SUMMARISED.** `python -m pytest tests
-q -n auto` from the repo root, written to a file and read back:
`8518 passed, 7 skipped, 8 warnings in 493.42s (0:08:13)`, exit 0. `python -m ruff check .`

### 2026-09-17 - CS-990 - CLOSED. Every action pin names a supported runtime, over a population derived twice from the workflow files

**THE DEFECT.** Every action pin in both tracked workflows named a major whose Node 20 runtime
GitHub has deprecated. Nothing was red and nothing would have been: the runner does not fail a
job over a retired runtime, it force-runs the action on the current Node and prints a warning.
So the upgrade was being applied by GitHub rather than by this project, and the day it broke
would have been the day the fallback was withdrawn rather than a day this project chose.

**THE ROOT CAUSE, WHICH IS NOT THE PINS.** No mechanism owned the question. The pins were
correct when written and went stale silently, and the only record of the problem was an
aspirational `BACKLOG.md` line whose own count had already drifted - it said eight pin sites
and the derivation measured fifteen. A count restated in prose is a lie with a timestamp on
it, and this one was the proof.

**WHAT CHANGED.** `tools/action_runtimes.py` grades every pin by the runtime its major ships,
against `RUNTIME_SUPPORTED_FROM`. Both tracked workflows move to the majors that ship on Node
24. The `BACKLOG.md` entry is removed: it is superseded by a shipped guard, and leaving it
would restate a fact this ledger and that tool now own.

**THE POPULATION IS DERIVED, AND DERIVED TWICE.** `pins_by_parse` asks PyYAML what the step
reference key resolves to, at any depth. `pins_by_scan` recognises a pin by the owner/repo@ref
shape alone and names no key at all. The arms compare them as MULTISETS, so one pin present in
either reading and not the other reddens, and a duplicate cannot go missing. **A floor over
the pin count is forbidden here by the item line by name - it is the CS-988 shape, met by its
strongest member - and none was used.**

**AGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO READINGS THAT CANNOT DISAGREE IS NOT EVIDENCE, so independence is
PROVEN rather than claimed.** `test_the_two_enumerations_share_no_constant` parses both
functions' ASTs, fails on any literal they hold in common, and fails again if either reaches
for a module-level constant the other could share. A comment asserting independence is worth
nothing the first time somebody factors a shared pattern out of the two.

**THE TABLE IS LISTED AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, so the arm is loud where it is blind.** No test
here reaches the network, so the runtime table is a shipped constant. An action the table does
not name is an OFFENCE rather than a pass, and so is a ref carrying no major version - a sha
or a branch names no runtime. A table that waves through what it does not recognise fails in
the permissive direction and would forgive a real deprecation forever with nothing red.

**PROVEN BY** `tests/test_action_runtimes.py`, nine arms:
`test_no_tracked_workflow_pins_a_deprecated_runtime` is the headline and it was RED before the
bump, naming all fifteen pins;
`test_the_graded_population_is_not_empty` is its anti-vacuity bound, because an empty
population satisfies every equality above for free;
`test_the_two_enumerations_agree_as_multisets`;
`test_the_two_enumerations_share_no_constant`;
`test_a_planted_deprecated_pin_reddens_the_grade`;
`test_a_pin_in_a_second_workflow_is_graded_too`;
the unknown-action arm, renamed by the entry above;
`test_a_ref_carrying_no_major_version_is_a_loud_offence`;
`test_both_enumerations_see_a_planted_pin`, which is what shows neither reading is a no-op.
Merged files: `tools/action_runtimes.py`, `tests/test_action_runtimes.py`,
`.github/workflows/tier1.yml`, `.github/workflows/tier2.yml`, `BACKLOG.md`.

### 2026-09-17 - CS-919 - CLOSED. A sha the lane cannot show it produced is recorded `unattributable` and graded by nobody

**THE DEFECT, MEASURED RATHER THAN ANTICIPATED.** On CS-918's first real cycle the worker
committed nothing - it left ten files uncommitted in the lane worktree - while another
session on the same box pushed `f80b95af7e2e`. `ops/loop/queue_loop.py` read `origin/main`
before and after the cycle, saw the ref move, attributed it to the cycle, waited out tier1,
dispatched a tier2 run and waited 1105.9 seconds for it. The row recorded
`"ci": {"verdict": "success"}` against a sha the lane never produced. It failed in BOTH
directions and silently in both: a neighbour's green was written into this lane's ledger as
though the lane had earned it, and a neighbour's RED would have stopped the night under
`ci_red`, blaming a worker that pushed nothing.

**WHAT CHANGED.** `run_loop` grades the post-cycle remote tip only when it EQUALS the lane
worktree's own post-cycle HEAD, which is the only sha this driver knows the lane produced.
Any other moved tip - a stranger's push, or a stranger's commit landing on top of ours -
gets `verdict="unattributable"`, the five-key shape the `no-push` and `unavailable` branches
already write, and NO wait is dispatched. An unreadable lane HEAD lands in the same branch,
which is the same direction `record["commit"]` already defaults in.

**THE READING WAS ALREADY IN HAND, so the repair costs no git call.** `post_tree` is read
above for the progress counter, unconditionally and before the CI block, and the two
consumers now share one reading rather than two that can disagree.

**NOT A NARROWER WINDOW, and the item's note forbids that by name.** The window is the whole
cycle by design; shrinking it trades a large silent error for a smaller silent one. The
repair reads no clock at all.

**`unattributable` IS A SEPARATE WORD FROM `no-push` ON PURPOSE.** The two send an operator
to different places - `no-push` means the ref stood still and the worker log holds the
answer; `unattributable` means somebody pushed and it was not provably us, which is a fact
about the BOX. It joins `_CI_ROLLUP_BAD` for the reason `no-push` is already there - a cycle
with no CI evidence of its own is not good news - and it is NOT a hard stop, because a
neighbour pushing is not a broken branch and must not end the night.

**PROVEN BY.** `tests/test_queue_loop.py::test_a_foreign_sha_landing_in_the_window_is_unattributable_and_grades_nothing`,
which drives a tip the lane tree never held and requires both that the verdict word is
written AND that `waits == []` - a verdict with the wait still dispatched would have paid the
1105.9 seconds this item was filed over. Its control is
`tests/test_queue_loop.py::test_a_sha_the_lane_itself_produced_is_still_graded`, without
which a driver answering `unattributable` to everything would pass.

**THE SIBLING SWEEP, AND IT IS THE MOST REUSABLE THING THIS CYCLE PRODUCED.** Six existing
arms reddened, and not one of them was a behaviour regression - every one was a FIXTURE
driving the CS-919 defect while standing in for a healthy night. `_moving_ref` and
`_committing_tree` each walk their OWN counter, so the remote tip and the lane HEAD never
agreed in any arm built from the pair. That was invisible while the driver graded whatever
the tip said. `_lane_push` is the repair: one piece of state, advanced on the POST tree read,
answered by both seams. Rewired arms -
`test_the_driver_waits_between_cycles_and_the_next_cycle_cannot_start_first`,
`test_one_cycle_writes_exactly_one_jsonl_row_carrying_its_verdict`,
`test_ci_going_red_stops_the_night`,
`test_a_cancelled_ci_run_is_recorded_but_does_not_stop_the_night`,
`test_completed_cycles_that_push_run_the_whole_budget`,
`test_a_one_cycle_night_that_shipped_exits_zero`.

**ONE ARM WAS PASSING FOR THE WRONG REASON AND ONLY THE SWEEP FOUND IT.**
`test_a_cancelled_ci_run_is_recorded_but_does_not_stop_the_night` asserted only `cycles_run`
and `stopped_by`, and `unattributable` does not stop a night either - so it stayed green on a
night that graded NOTHING, with the cancelled verdict it is named for never reaching a row. It
now pins the verdict per row.

**AND `test_a_foreign_push_is_not_this_lane_s_progress` MOVED ITS CONTROL RATHER THAN LOSING
IT.** That arm's sharp edge was that the counter had to catch a night whose every row looked
healthy - `verdict: success`, `ok: true`. Those same rows now read `unattributable` and

### 2026-09-16 - SESSION 102 - NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. NOTHING CLOSED. A tier1 red exposed a memory reachability walk that followed routing children only on a case-insensitive filesystem

**THE RED.** Tier1 CI went red on 645663c. `tools/drift_guard.py`'s memory reachability walk built
each `INDEX_*` routing child's path from a LOWERCASED link token. A case-insensitive filesystem found
the file anyway and a case-sensitive one did not, so routing children were followed only where names
fold. The defect was pre-existing and platform-dependent. A CS-1120 plant exposed it, and nothing in
CS-1120 introduced it.

directory's own entries. Two routing files that fold to the same name are a FAIL and are never
resolved silently. A refused listing is a WARN. An arm emulates case-sensitive lookup on Windows, and
it was proven to fail against the old code. Arms:
`tests/data/test_drift_guard_data.py::test_the_case_sensitive_emulation_refuses_the_lowered_spelling`,
`::test_a_routing_child_is_followed_where_names_are_case_sensitive`,
`::test_two_routing_files_differing_only_by_case_are_a_finding` and
`::test_a_memory_listing_the_walk_is_refused_is_a_warn`.

### 2026-09-16 - CS-895 - CLOSED. The memory citation guard now has a container model, and the three pinned residuals are inverted

**THE DEFECT.** Guard (b)'s code scanner was line-oriented with no container model, so three
shapes read as prose and had their contents resolved as citations. The failure direction is a
FALSE POSITIVE and guard (b) runs in the pre-commit and pre-push path, so each shape did not
merely mislead a reader - it would have BLOCKED EVERY COMMIT AND PUSH in the repository until
the document was rewritten. CS-890 recorded all three rather than guessing at them, because a
wrong container model trades a loud failure for a silent one.

**THE ROOT CAUSE, WHICH IS ONE THING AND NOT THREE.** Every indent the scanner tested was
measured against the DOCUMENT MARGIN. P1's fence sits four columns in because a nested list
item put it there; P2's fence never starts its line because a blockquote marker precedes it;
P4 has no fence at all and is defined purely by an indent. All three are the same missing
fact - the column the innermost open container's content begins at.

**WHAT CHANGED.** `tools/drift_guard.py`: `_strip_blockquote` peels and counts blockquote
markers, `_list_content_column` derives the content column a list marker opens, and
`_outside_code` carries a stack of open columns. The opener cap and the four columns that
open an indented code block are both measured against the innermost container rather than the
margin. `_fence_step` advances an open fence and ENDS IT WITH ITS CONTAINER - a line at a
shallower blockquote depth or a lesser indent closes the fence, which is the same erring-
toward-closing choice P3 already recorded, and it is what stops the model swallowing a file.

**THE HALF THAT GOES SILENTLY WRONG, AND THE ARM THAT OWNS IT.** Four spaces from the margin
is a code block; four spaces inside a list item whose content column is two is ORDINARY
CONTENT. A model that excluded the second drops a real citation with nothing to notice
afterwards, which is strictly worse than the loud failure being repaired.
`test_four_spaces_inside_a_list_item_is_content_and_not_a_code_block` fails the moment that
distinction stops being made, and `test_an_indented_line_may_not_interrupt_a_paragraph` holds
the other half of the same rule.

**THE DEFECT.** `tests/chained_exemption_guard.Exemption` keyed each recorded reason to a

TRADED AWAY.** Duplicates are KEPT rather than collapsed, so the multiset still carries the
cardinality, and a read arriving with no deletion changes it too - the CS-888 arm

green.

`rendered_exception_lines`. Separating them needs the statement around the read, which is a
bigger key than this item's clause asks for. `_read_key`'s own docstring carries this.

TWO OBJECT REFERENCES out of the region CS-828 and CS-1068 left carried as

carry one off the body being read AND derives which of two forms that body writes.
`read_properties` takes the derived vocabulary as `reference_pair_classes` and reports the
pair as `TrailingRun.references`, with `unread` falling by the width it consumed. The
region entry in `UNMEASURED_PAYLOAD_REGIONS["trailing_run"]` records the narrowing and
names both functions, so the shipped table and the reading cannot drift apart. Merged
files: `clockspeed/save/objects.py`, `tests/save/test_reference_pair.py`,
`docs/item_notes/phase4-followups.md`, `ROADMAP.md`.

input and it was half false.** CS-1068's own entry describes this shape as two references
"followed by a 24-byte tail that nothing in the run describes". Measured across this
project's library, the tail is written by ONE schema and NOT by two others, which write the
same two references and stop. The partition is exact and no payload crosses it, and it is
corroborated by an independent second signal - every tail-bearing record lacks the two
wire-geometry properties and every tail-free record carries them, so the newer schema moved
that geometry out of the run and into properties. **A READER BUILT FROM THAT SENTENCE WOULD
HAVE OVER-READ EVERY TAIL-FREE PAYLOAD BY 24 BYTES.** The transferable finding is the
general one: a prose description of an unmeasured region in this tree is a hypothesis, and
CS-828's own note already says a filed citation is a hypothesis until re-probed.

wide it is. The tail is one of the two widths `REFERENCE_PAIR_TAIL_WIDTHS` allows, and that
set is DERIVED by solving rather than assumed - across the whole library the bytes left
after the four prefixes take exactly two values, so the non-zero one is the only width
under which those payloads walk exactly onto their declared end. The declared end is a
BOUND and a VALIDATION and never a source of width: the walk refuses rather than stretching
to reach it.

form on the version pair would have worked on today's library and would have been a

consistency requirement is the anti-vacuity property: a reader taking each record at
whichever width happened to fit would admit any mixture, which is arithmetic wearing a
derivation's clothes.

makes the per-body derivation worth having rather than ceremony over a constant.

**WHAT CHANGED.** `clockspeed/save/objects.py` gained `read_item_list`, which reads a

**THE DEFECT.** CS-828 read the int32 the run opens with and nothing past it. The remainder is
class-keyed rather than pair-keyed, so no single grammar reads it, and its width is whatever the
bytes are - which means any partition of it sums to the declared end and no reading of it could have
failed. That is the defect that refuted CS-830 after it had merged, and it is why the clause asked
for a width derived from something self-describing inside the run.

EMPTY item list is four zero bytes, and so is the entire remainder of several classes that carry no
list at all. The two are byte-identical, so no grammar reading the run alone can tell them apart: a
reader admitting a run because it parsed would zero the remainder of every one of those classes, and
`and nowhere else` would be false. A class earns its place in the vocabulary by DEMONSTRATING the
grammar - one of its records in the same body must carry a NON-EMPTY list whose count prefix,
per-entry length prefixes and fixed fields agree with each other and land on the declared end. That
cannot happen by accident, and a body that stops carrying one derives nothing rather than going
quietly green.

**WHERE EVERY WIDTH COMES FROM.** The count prefix says how many entries follow; each entry's own
length prefix says how wide its class path is; `ITEM_LIST_ENTRY_HEAD_BYTES` and
`ITEM_LIST_ENTRY_TAIL_BYTES` are shipped constants, the tail width DERIVED by solving rather than
assumed - it is the only width in 0..32 under which every entry of every list in this project's
library walks exactly onto its declared end. The declared end is a BOUND and a VALIDATION and never
a source of width: the walk refuses rather than stretching to reach it.

**THE ARM THE CLAUSE NAMES.**
`tests/save/test_item_list.py::test_the_width_is_derived_from_the_prefixes_and_not_from_the_declared_end`
offers the same bytes twice - once with the declared end where the prefixes say it is, once with it
moved out past them. The first reads and the second is REFUSED, which is exactly the outcome that
inverts when the derivation is swapped for `end - at`; that forbidden reading is spelled out in the
module as `_width_from_observation` so the swap is a one-line change rather than a thought
experiment. `test_a_declared_count_short_of_the_entries_written_is_refused` is its twin from the
other side: the bytes fill the run either way and only a prefix-driven walk notices.

**THE SIBLING SWEEP.** The remainder's other shapes were measured on the corpus before any code was
written and are NOT swept here, because they do not share this root cause. One class's remainder
reads as two length-prefixed object references followed by a 24-byte tail that nothing in the run
describes; another is a large nested structure. Reading either by the width left over would be the
CS-830 defect again. They stay carried as `unread` and CS-828 stays open over them.

**WHAT REMAINS OPEN.** CS-828's clause asks for the run's contents on EVERY payload of the three
pairs and this reads one derived class set's. That item is unchanged and is not closed by this one.

### 2026-09-16 - CS-1103 - CLOSED. A blind inbox read no longer writes, and no longer invents a withdrawal

**WHAT CHANGED.** An inbox directory that EXISTS but cannot be LISTED made
`deliverables()` swallow the `OSError` and return an EMPTY LIST, so every caller received
"there is nothing there" for "I could not look". CS-1095 repaired only the READING half.
The two WRITE halves were live until this entry.

**THE TWO DEFECTS, MEASURED IN THIS TREE** against a synthetic inbox holding one live note
and one honest prior acknowledgement, not inferred from a sibling's report:

- the withdrawal derivation reported `1 WITHDRAWN` and named the note that never left. A
  withdrawal is the ONE inbox event with no on-disk artifact left to check it against, so
  nothing downstream could refute a fabricated one.
- `--ack` rewrote the seen store from that note's digest to exactly `{"seen": []}` while
  printing `acknowledged 0 item(s)`. That is destruction of the durable state the tool
  exists to keep, triggered by a permission bit.

**WHO FOUND IT.** A sibling tree, which reproduced CS's own published finding six under a
REAL access-control denial - something this tree could only simulate - measured it as THREE
defects where CS had published one, and sent the result unprompted. Its sentence is the one
worth keeping: A BLIND READ IS RECOVERABLE; A BLIND READ THAT WRITES IS NOT.

**FIVE CALL SITES, where the merger's reproduction had found two.** `notes_in`,
`unread_items`, `withdrawn_items`, `render` and the `--ack` path in `main`, plus two
further logging calls that would have escaped as a traceback.

**TWO DESIGN POINTS THAT ARE THE REASON THIS HOLDS.** `InboxUnreadableError` is
deliberately NOT an `OSError` subclass - every `OSError` handler in the module would have
swallowed it again, reinstating the defect through the repair. And `inbox_blind_reason` was
DELETED rather than fixed: it re-probed the directory AFTER the listing had already
returned, so the two could disagree and the wrong one would win. `EXIT_BLIND_INBOX = 4` now
separates "here and unreadable" from "never here".

**GRADED BY MUTANTS, NOT BY ASSERTIONS. Nine mutants, nine killed, zero survivors**, each
guard mutated individually - because the sibling added four guards and its FOURTH survived
at exit 0 over a path its arms never entered, and a guard nothing grades is not a guard.
Two of the nine are process-boundary pins: the same sibling lost a suppression mutant
across its ENTIRE 240-arm suite because the code sat where only a real child process could
reach it. This tree is safe there only because `__main__` is one line, and nothing graded
that it stays one line. Now something does, by PARSING the block rather than grepping it.

**Verification:** `tools/inbox_watch.py`, proven by
`tests/test_inbox_watch.py::test_an_unlistable_inbox_makes_ack_refuse_and_write_nothing`,
`::test_the_withdrawal_derivation_refuses_rather_than_deriving_from_nothing`,
`::test_the_enumerator_refuses_rather_than_returning_an_empty_listing`,
`::test_the_main_guard_carries_no_logic_beyond_dispatching_to_main` and
`::test_the_module_run_as_a_child_process_reaches_stdout_and_exits_zero`.
The original reproduction was re-run against the merged tree: the fabricated withdrawal is
gone, the acknowledgement refuses, and the watermark survives BYTE-IDENTICAL to the honest
acknowledgement.

**NOT VERIFIED:** no real access-control denial was attempted here. The fault is

### 2026-09-16 - CS-1095 addendum - NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. The section 14 licence gate, RUN against the vendored doc after the fact, and CLEARED

**WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS.** `docs/CHANNEL.md` was vendored on a direct operator
instruction and this tree's own `CONVENTIONS.md` section 14 gate was NEVER RUN against
it. That gap was found by a SIBLING rather than here: LL refused the same file at its own
licence gate on 2026-09-15 for naming no licence, no holder and no repository, and that
refusal applied to this copy exactly as it applied to the original. The sending tree
conceded the omission plainly - it had named a commit and called the tree public, and
public is a VISIBILITY, not a GRANT.

**THE GATE WAS RUN HERE, TRAP BY TRAP, AGAINST THE SOURCE REPOSITORY'S OWN FILES** rather
than against the sending tree's summary of them. Section 14's first trap is that a repo
can contradict itself and one source alone gives the wrong answer, so a summary could not
have discharged it.

- TRAP 1, self-contradiction: NONE. `LICENSE`, the README licence paragraph and `NOTICE`
  agree. The `LICENSE` carries a SCOPE OF THIS LICENSE block stating the grant covers the
  source code and the authored documentation, naming "the Markdown that describes them",
  and carving out only the third-party data under `data/`. `docs/CHANNEL.md` is authored
  documentation and is not under `data/`. The scope block states that it CONTROLS where a
  data file and the licence appear to conflict.
- TRAP 2, a holder who cannot relicense: NOT PRESENT. One holder, `Moonbeam`, named in
  both `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`, and the sending tree wrote the doc's bytes itself.
- TRAP 3, a licence naming NOBODY: NOT PRESENT. The copyright line is RENDERED, not a
  template: `Copyright 2026 Moonbeam` at `LICENSE` line 189. Read the line, not the name.
- TRAP 4, truncation: NOT PRESENT. 219 lines, the warranty clause present.
- TRAP 5, source-available: NOT PRESENT. Zero occurrences of Elastic, BUSL or an
  all-rights-reserved reservation in `LICENSE` or the README.

**VERDICT: CLEARED FOR VENDORING.** Apache-2.0 is permissive and one-way compatible with
this tree's outbound licence.

**THE OBLIGATION THAT SURVIVES THE CLEARANCE**, because a permissive licence is not an
absent one. Apache-2.0 section 4 asks a redistributor to retain the attribution. The
vendored file is BYTE-PINNED and carries no notice of its own, and this tree may not add
one to it - so the attribution is recorded in the section 4 topology row, which is
auto-loaded every turn, and here. There are no changes to state: the copy is byte-identical
and its digest is pinned by an arm.

**STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE NOTICED: the named holder is also this repository's own
commit identity.** The same operator owns both trees. That is not an exemption from the
gate and it did not shorten it - the gate was run as if the holder were a stranger, which
is the only way its result means anything - but a reader who spotted it later and found it
unmentioned would be right to discount the verdict.

**WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES NOT CLOSE.** Nothing. CS-1095 is already closed above; this records
a gate that should have run before that entry and did not. The lesson belongs with the
record: an operator instruction moves the DECISION, not the GATE, and this tree ran the
vendoring without noticing it had skipped one of its own.

### 2026-09-15 - CS-1087 - CLOSED. A token carried only by an unparseable header is matchable without parsing it

**WHAT CHANGED.** `clockspeed/save/header.py` gained `scan_framed_tokens` and
`scan_world_tokens`: a bounded raw-byte scan that recovers a world token from the FRAMING
the engine writes around it - a length prefix, `WORLD_TOKEN_LENGTH` characters of the
token alphabet, a terminator - without parsing the header at all. `tools/precommit_gate.py`
calls it when `read_header` refuses, inside the SAME `SAVE_HEADER_BUDGET_SECONDS` clock on
the same `started` value, reading at most `MAX_HEADER_BYTES`, over only the files
`MAX_SAVE_HEADER_FILES` already admitted. Recovered candidates pass through the same
`_matchable` filter a parsed token does. The frozen-file GRANT recorded before the edit
binds all of this; its clause 2 preferred exactly this limb of the acceptance, and the
exit-status limb was DENIED because `.githooks/pre-commit` maps every non-zero status to
BLOCKED, which is the wedge the item forbids.

**HOW TO VERIFY IT INDEPENDENTLY.** Build a synthetic save, corrupt the version prologue,
and drive the gate's real discovery: `read_header` refuses with
`UnsupportedHeaderVersionError` and `scan_world_tokens` returns the token. Overwrite the
same file wholesale and the scan returns nothing. The arms are graded with an unreadable
header ACTUALLY PRESENT beside a parseable sibling, on leak IDENTITY and never on the exit
code, and the reader is proven ALIVE - exactly one header reported unparseable, both
tokens leaking.

**WHAT THE GRADERS CHANGED, because the first cut was not the shipped one.** An
adjudicator sent the candidate back and an adversary refuted three further claims. The
candidate cap counted raw hits BEFORE de-duplication, so one value repeated to the cap
followed by a DIFFERENT value discarded the second; and `hits` was shared across both
framings, so a full narrow population starved the wide scan entirely. Both lost real
tokens. The cap now counts DISTINCT values with a per-framing budget, and its truncation
reaches the exit status BLOCKING with an anti-hollowing control that fails if the scan is
disabled. Separately, `scan_framed_tokens` bound the prefix BARE in its own frame - the
first bare holder of a save prefix in the module, where the parse path leaves only dotted
holders - and the arm claiming otherwise was blind to it BY CONSTRUCTION, monkeypatching
the very function that held the buffer. It now scrubs on its own unwind and the arm
refuses through a shipped inner function.

**THE RESIDUE, MEASURED AND NOT GLOSSED.** Recovery is 4 of 4 tokens PRESENT in the bytes,
but only 4 of 9 unreadable SHAPES. Five carry no recoverable token: truncated before the
identifier, truncated mid-identifier, overwritten wholesale, zero-byte, and a file that
cannot be opened at all. A sixth shape recovers nothing though the characters ARE on disk -
the identifier is intact behind a DAMAGED COUNT PREFIX, so the framing the scan keys on is
gone. On the live library this run: 31 files, 1 unreadable, and that one recovered NOTHING -
it is the truncated-before-the-identifier case. So the coverage limb is 0-for-1 on real
data today, which is a floor on this item's value and not a defect in it. CS-1083's cited
0-of-28 was re-measured as ordered by the grant and is now 1 of 31.

**ONE LABELLED RESIDUAL IN THE NEW BLOCKING PATH.** It differs in KIND from the five bounds
beside it: those trip on how many files the operator has, while this one trips on the
CONTENT of a single file the gate may never remove (non-negotiable 1), and its reason names
neither the value (grant clause 7) nor the file. If it ever fired, the only escape would be
`--no-verify` - the wedge this item exists to avoid, arriving by another door. Measured
probability is effectively nil: a real header carries about ten strings, and 16 DISTINCT
framed candidates of the measured length inside the byte bound is unreachable for random or
compressed bytes. It is recorded because it is a real difference, not because it is likely.

### 2026-09-15 - CS-1093 - CLOSED. The 7-bit walk names every offending module rather than the first

**WHAT CHANGED.** `test_every_module_this_split_created_is_seven_bit_ascii` in
`tests/test_bare_path_citations.py` asserted INSIDE its `for path in paths` loop, so the
first module carrying a byte above the 7-bit range short-circuited the walk and every
later offender stayed invisible until that one was repaired. That is the pooled-guard
shape this project has filed before: a guard that reports one member of a failing
population teaches the reader the damage is smaller than it is. The arm now collects
every offender and asserts once on the collected set. The missing-file case was folded
into the same collection rather than left as a second in-loop assert, which would have
re-introduced the short-circuit by another door.

**THE SCALAR BINDING IS THE POINT, NOT A STYLE CHOICE.** pytest's assertion rewriting
renders the asserted EXPRESSION independently of the message, so `assert not offenders`
prints the list whatever the message says - measured on the pre-repair arm, which printed
`assert not [195, 169]`. The count is bound to a plain scalar first and the assert reads
`offending_modules == 0`, so the rewriter renders `assert 2 == 0` and the names reach the
report only through the authored message.

**HOW TO VERIFY IT INDEPENDENTLY.** Append a non-ASCII byte to BOTH
`tests/archive_rot_guard.py` and `tests/bare_path_guard.py`, then run
`python -m pytest tests/test_bare_path_citations.py -k seven_bit`. The failure names BOTH
modules and renders `assert 2 == 0`. Snapshot the two files first and restore from the
snapshot, never with `git checkout`, which would discard uncommitted work. The plant
REPORTS rather than crashing because the walk reads bytes and never decodes, so no
UnicodeDecodeError can destroy the fixture - the failure mode that killed an equivalent
plant earlier in this project.

**WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** The walked population is the modules this split created, seven of
them, and not the whole tests tree. Widening it was not in the acceptance and was not done.

   not a new class of access. The gate already opens save files: `_world_tokens_from_headers`
   calls the header reader, and `read_header` in `clockspeed/save/header.py` does
   `target.open("rb")` and reads at most `MAX_HEADER_BYTES`. Non-negotiable 1 forbids
   WRITING to the save directory and to the install; it has never forbidden reading, and
   `_save_root_dirs` already says so for the listing.
   The fallback opens `"rb"`, never any write or append mode, never `os.remove`, never a
   rename, never a temp file beside the save.
4. THE FALLBACK IS BOUNDED BY THE SAME CONSTANTS THAT ALREADY BOUND THE HEADER SCAN, and
   this is mandatory rather than advisory. It runs inside the same
   `SAVE_HEADER_BUDGET_SECONDS` aggregate wall clock, tested at the same point in the same
   loop, on the same `started` clock; it reads at most `MAX_HEADER_BYTES` per file; and it
   examines only files already admitted by `MAX_SAVE_HEADER_FILES`, itself derived from
   `MAX_SAVE_ROOT_ENTRIES`. No new budget constant is introduced, because a second budget
   is a second thing to drift. Per CS-1083 clause 3, no existing bound may be silently
   removed and `SAVE_HEADER_BUDGET_SECONDS` keeps a live refusal path.
5. THE HARVEST IS IDENTITY-CONSTRAINED, NEVER A GENERAL STRING SCRAPE. A candidate enters
   the blocklist only if it passes the token's own measured shape - `WORLD_TOKEN_LENGTH` in
   `clockspeed/save/header.py`, which `_warnings_for` in that module enforces - and
   then `_matchable` against `MIN_WORLD_TOKEN_CHARS` and `GENERIC_ACCOUNT_NAMES`, exactly
   as a parsed token does today. A scrape that admits arbitrary runs would add engine
   strings to a whole-word blocklist, and because clause 7 forbids ever naming the value,
   the operator gets an UNCLEARABLE false positive whose only remedy is `--no-verify` -
   which is the wedge this item exists to avoid, arriving by a different door.
6. THE RAW PREFIX IS SCRUBBED ON EVERY PATH, INCLUDING THE UNWIND. This is the one
   genuinely NEW exposure and the clause that matters most. Today the gate NEVER holds raw
   save bytes in a frame of its own: it delegates to `clockspeed/save/header.py`, whose
   CS-963 scrub inside `read_header` deletes the buffer before re-raising, with the comment "this
   frame holds a bounded PREFIX of the file, which is precisely the personal-data-bearing
   region". A fallback that binds that prefix inside `tools/precommit_gate.py` reproduces
   that defect one level up, in a file whose module docstring already states that a
   traceback cannot be honestly redacted and that `CLOCKSPEED_CRASH_TRACEBACK=1` reveals
   one. The fallback therefore mirrors the CS-963 shape: `del` the buffer on the exception
   path, and never store it on an object that outlives the call.
7. NO DIAGNOSTIC, SKIP, COUNT LINE OR EXCEPTION MAY RENDER A SCANNED VALUE, and the
   existing design already holds this - MEASURED rather than assumed. `check_pii` builds
   its `Diagnostic` with a CONSTANT reason; `_discovered_rules` states the rule
   and its four reasons carry no value, the world-token one being "a world token
   for this machine appears";
   `_matchable`'s reasons never contain the value; skip lines render
   `display_label` plus the reason and the world label is a non-path label
   returned unchanged; checked lines render label, origin and byte count; every
   exception text routes through `safe_exc_text`. ADDING RAW BYTES TO THE
   BLOCKLIST THEREFORE CREATES NO ECHO PATH THAT DOES NOT ALREADY EXIST - the exposure is
   clause 6's frame, not the blocklist. A regression arm asserts this rather than leaving
   it to a reader: for a planted candidate value, no byte of it appears in stdout, in
   stderr, or in the rendered text of any diagnostic or skip.
8. Must NOT change, carrying CS-1083 clause 5 forward unaltered and adding two: a skip line
   never printing the value it skipped; the never-fail-to-start property; the `PASS` banner
   being the last line AND ITS FORMAT, because `.githooks/pre-commit` pins that format with
   an anchored `case` pattern and a format change drags a second frozen file in; the gate's
   documented exit-code contract, "0 pass, 1 block. Nothing else"; and the blocking
   semantics of every skip other than the world-token one.

**WHY `.githooks/pre-commit` IS DENIED.** The second limb of the acceptance - a distinct
exit status - cannot be taken without it and cannot be taken safely with it. The hook maps
every non-zero status to BLOCKED and exits with it, so a third status BLOCKS until the
unreadable file is gone, on a file the gate may not remove (non-negotiable 1) and
intermittently on every autosave in flight (non-negotiable 7). Making that status advisory
means teaching a tier-0 hook that some non-zero exits do not block, which creates a class
of gate failure that no longer refuses - the CS-703 and CS-823 failure mode restated, in a
file whose whole body is the record of closing it. WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE FOR A GRANT:
clause 2's route measured INFEASIBLE - that is, a token carried only by an unparseable
header is shown unrecoverable from the raw prefix under clauses 4 and 5 - and the advisory
status shown, by a planted unrun and a planted truncated gate, not to weaken the CS-823
banner proof. Route back through an adjudicator with that measurement; do not assume this
denial.

**THE ARM IS GRADED AGAINST A REAL UNREADABLE HEADER, WHICH IS THE ACCEPTANCE AND NOT A
DETAIL.** CS-1083's own record shows why: its first cut HOLLOWED the CS-436 arms, which
then passed with world-token detection completely destroyed. A suppressed or monkeypatched
reader reproduces that exactly - it proves the code path was entered and nothing about
whether a token was recovered. The fixture is a synthetic `.sav` whose header genuinely
does not parse, carrying a synthetic token of the measured length, in a temporary save root
the test owns. No real save, no fixture directory, no committed bytes (non-negotiable 11).

**THE UNPROVEN CLAUSE, NAMED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR A MEASURED ONE.** Nothing here
measures that a token IS recoverable from the raw prefix of a header that fails to parse -
that depends on where the parse fails, and a file truncated before the identifier carries
no token at any offset. Clause 2 may therefore turn out to cover only part of the
population, and the residue after this item is that part. Separately, the single
measurement that makes the whole design safe - 0 of 28 headers unreadable - is one sample
from one day; re-measure on the live library before shipping rather than citing CS-1083's
number.

### 2026-09-14 - CS-302 - CLOSED. The refusal diagnosis cost one full elimination per row, and it was measured at live scale before it was replaced

**WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND.** `ratio._name_unsatisfiable_item` recovered the name of the
unsatisfiable item by dropping one row at a time and re-solving, which is one full exact
elimination PER ROW on top of the solve that already refused. The item's own note recorded
that as reasoned acceptable for optimizer-sized sets and NOT measured at real scale. Measured
now, against the registry this machine's install actually builds - 750 items, 872 recipes, 0
recipes excluded - the system the whole recipe set produces WITH ONE TARGET ON IT is 750 rows
by 872 columns under `BYPRODUCT_BALANCED` and 153 by 872 under `BYPRODUCT_SINKABLE`. The
target matters to the second number and not the first, and saying so is a correction: under
`sinkable` an unconsumed byproduct gets no equation, so the same recipe set with NO target is
152 by 872 and naming one of those 598 sunk items as the target is what adds the row. Under
`balanced` every one of them already carries a balance row, so the count does not move. One `solve_linear` over the
balanced system takes 4.86 s and one leave-one-out probe over it takes 4.73 s, so the loop's
worst case of 750 probes is 3549 s - 59 minutes to explain a refusal the solve itself reached
in under five seconds. The sinkable system's 153 probes are 193.6 s. NOT ACCEPTABLE, so the
diagnosis was replaced rather than blessed.

The 3549 s is one measured probe times the loop's own bound and not a wall-clock run of all
750; the loop is a `for` over `range(len(system.rows))` and the bound is therefore exact,
but this entry says which half was measured so the number is not read as a stopwatch reading.

**WHAT REPLACED IT.** `clockspeed/solve/exact.py` gains `isolating_rows`, which answers the
same question in ONE elimination. The elimination carries the transform that produced it, so
every row whose coefficients vanish is a left null vector `y` of the matrix in original row
order and the constant beside it is `y . rhs`. Those vectors are a basis of the left null
space `N`, because the accumulated transform is a product of elementary operations and is
therefore invertible. Writing `f(y) = y . rhs`, striking row `i` leaves `N_i = {y in N :
y[i] == 0}` and the reduced system is consistent exactly when `f` vanishes on `N_i` - which,
since `N_i` and `ker f` both have codimension at most one in `N`, happens exactly when the
coordinate functional `y -> y[i]` is a NONZERO multiple of `f` on `N`. That is a column
comparison against the constants, not a solve. Measured on the same balanced system:
8.94 s against the loop's 3549 s, a factor of 397. On the sinkable system, 1.48 s against
193.6 s, a factor of 131.

**THE VERIFIER REFUTED ONE OF THESE ARMS AND IT IS REPAIRED HERE.** The arm named for the
empty answer was pointed at the wrong system: `x + y = 1`, `y + z = 1`, `x + z = 1` against
`x + y + z = 2` is contradicted as a SET, and striking any one of those rows leaves a system
that HAS a solution - so every index is isolating and the arm was measuring `(0, 1, 2, 3)`
while its name and its docstring both said empty. It passed anyway, because its only
assertion was equality with the oracle. That is the lesson worth keeping: an arm whose whole
claim is delegated to an oracle cannot notice it is aimed at the wrong subject. The empty case
is now two independent contradictions over disjoint variables, it asserts the empty tuple
DIRECTLY as well as against the oracle, and the original fixture is kept under a name that
says what it does - it is the only one here whose answer is every row.

**THE EQUIVALENCE IS PROVEN AGAINST THE LOOP ITSELF, NOT ASSERTED.** The replaced loop is
written out again in `tests/solve/test_exact.py` as `_brute_force_isolating` and used as an
ORACLE. `test_isolating_rows_answers_exactly_what_the_leave_one_out_loop_answered` runs both
over a 240-seed corpus, 227 of which are inconsistent, and requires the answers to be equal
index for index. The corpus is dense with rows that are exact scalar multiples of earlier
rows, deliberately: that is what drives the left null space above one dimension, and a
criterion that works when the contradiction has a single witness is not the same as one that
works. Two mutations were planted and both were killed by that arm - dropping the nonzero
clause from the multiple test, and letting a zero-constant basis vector stop constraining.

**THE COST CLAIM IS A COUNT AND NEVER A CLOCK.** A wall-clock bound asserted in the suite
would be a statement about the machine that ran it and would pass on a fast enough machine
against the implementation this item replaced. Both cost arms count elimination passes at
`exact._validate_system`, which every entry point that eliminates calls exactly once before
touching a coefficient. `test_isolating_rows_does_not_grow_its_work_with_the_row_count` pins
one pass at 6 rows and one at 96, and requires the ORACLE's cost to grow between those two
sizes so the arm cannot quietly become a comparison of two constants.

**SIBLING SWEEP: ONE SITE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POPULATION.** `grep` for the drop-and-resolve
shape over `clockspeed/` returns exactly `ratio.py:644`, and `solve_linear` has no other
caller in the package that loops. Nothing else to sweep, which is reported rather than
assumed.

**THE ZERO-WIDTH SHAPE IS GRADED BECAUSE `ratio.py` BUILDS IT.** With every selected recipe
excluded there is no variable, so there is no column, and what is left is a demand with nothing
on the other side. Those rows carry no coefficients at all, every one of them is trivially a
left null vector, and the whole question falls to the constants - the thinnest the criterion
ever gets. Five such systems are held to the oracle. The empty system is held to a written
answer INSTEAD of the oracle, and that is deliberate: the oracle calls a row isolating when
removing it leaves a consistent system, which every row of an already-consistent system
satisfies vacuously, so it is an oracle for inconsistent systems only and is guarded as one
everywhere it is used.

**BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED, INCLUDING THE FALLBACK.** The cheap all-zero-row check still runs
first and still returns the first such row. When no single row isolates the contradiction -
three or more mutually dependent rows - `isolating_rows` returns empty and the caller still
names the first balance row, because a refusal with no subject is one nobody can act on. The
three refusals the suite already pinned name the same items they named before, and that was
re-derived rather than assumed: the old loop and the new code were both run against the real
`_System` each of the three builds, and all three agree on the item.

**THE FALLBACK IS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL NOT REACHED BY ANY TEST THROUGH THE CALLER**, which
the verifier measured rather than inferred - a `trace` run over `tests/solve/test_ratio.py`
puts zero hits on that return while the fast path takes two and the isolating branch four.
It is reachable: a system from the corpus generator drives it, and it names the first row as
its comment says. This is a coverage gap that predates this item and is unchanged by it, so it
is FILED as CS-1067 rather than closed here - `isolating_rows` returning empty is now cheap to
construct, which is what makes the gap worth filing now and not before.

**PROVEN BY.** `tests/solve/test_exact.py::test_isolating_rows_answers_exactly_what_the_leave_one_out_loop_answered`,
`tests/solve/test_exact.py::test_isolating_rows_does_not_grow_its_work_with_the_row_count`,

### 2026-09-14 - CS-301 - CLOSED. The variable-power law was unmeasured, not unmeasurable, and the obvious cross-check was wrong

**WHAT CHANGED.** `clockspeed/solve/power.py` gains `bounded_draw`, which answers the two shapes
that declare no scalar with two exact `Fraction` bounds at the reference clock. The variable shape
takes its bounds from the recipe through the law ADR 0021 measured - minimum is the constant,
maximum is the constant plus the factor - and the struct-range shape reads both bounds off the
declaration and consults no recipe. Before this, all four of those buildings reported unmodeled and
contributed nothing to a power plan.

**THE REFUSAL WAS CORRECT AND ITS PREMISE WAS NOT.** The item note said the semantics of
`mVariablePowerConsumptionConstant` and `mVariablePowerConsumptionFactor` were unmeasured anywhere in
this project. True when written, and it was read for a year as though it meant unmeasurable. ADR 0020
had since made the publisher's own headers queryable; the two members carry doc comments stating the
law in as many words, and `clockspeed/data/assets.py` found them in an index of 8024 reflected
property declarations. The lesson is the note's shape rather than its content: a refusal recorded
without the condition that would lift it reads as a permanent verdict.

**THE FIRST IMPLEMENTATION WAS WRONG AND THE DOCUMENT CAUGHT IT.** The obvious cross-check is that
the recipe's two numbers EQUAL the estimated range declared on the building. That was written,
tested green against the synthetic corpus, and then measured against the shipped document, where it
holds on 25 of 25 recipes for one building, 6 of 6 for a second, and 0 of 12 for the third, whose
recipes carry two distinct bands. The building estimate is the ENVELOPE over its recipes, not any one
of them: taking the minimum constant and the maximum constant-plus-factor across each building's own
recipes reproduces its declared range on 3 of 3. So the published check is CONTAINMENT, and it holds
on 43 of 43 real pairings. It is not vacuous - asked against the pairings the document does not
declare, it rejects 1705 of 2573.

**WHAT IS STILL NOT PUBLISHED.** No scalar. The instantaneous draw rides `mPowerConsumptionCurve`, a
`UCurveFloat` asset the docs document does not export, so the cycle average is unknown and
`BoundedDraw` has no field that could hold one - the same fence `ClockCeiling` carries.

**THE SECOND HALF, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The item also asked for two unexercised branches
to be covered. Only one was a behaviour gap. The un-sharded base below the reference clock passed on
its first run, because `clamp_to_unsharded_base` already handled it and no fixture had ever declared
a base other than exactly one - a FIXTURE gap, and the test is coverage rather than a fix. The
two-producer case is real: a recipe naming two producing buildings has no single answer, because the
operands are per recipe and the envelope they are checked against is per building, and the two
pairings now return different outcomes in one test.

tree. A Phase 6 filing owes `config/lane_scopes.json` AND its second pin, and a new ADR owes the
citation guard, and neither cost is visible from the module the row is about - which is exactly why
a cycle that ships a solve-core change and runs only the solve suite reports green and is not.

**WHAT WAS ADJUDICATED.** The dashboard map underlay. No baked map image ships - the in-game
map is a live SceneCapture2D - and the real transform (`mUpperLeftWorld`,
`mWorldToMapScale`, `mDataWidth`) sits behind Oodle Data, which the install ships no callable
copy of.

underlay. The save's `mFogOfWarRawData` (1024x1024, structurally proved) may become a
toggled layer ONLY after a fit whose registration is proved by held-out containment of built
placements, a sign-flip negative control that reddens, and cross-save invariance; failing any
of those it carries a visible "registration unverified" flag or does not ship. Oodle Data
adoption stays GATED at CS-G01 pending a written `CONVENTIONS.md` section 14 verdict.

underlay registered to `WorldBounds`; a fitted transform accepted on visual plausibility
without the negative control; any Oodle-dependent extraction slice before CS-G01 rules in
writing; and any lifted map tile, table or image from a wiki or community source (CS-485).

**WHY `WorldBounds` IS NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLIED.** It bounds THIS WORLD'S placements
and moves every time the operator builds anything, so a transform registered against it
drifts under the operator's own hands. That is the obvious implementation and it is the
wrong one.

**THE SECOND HALF OF THE RULING, RECORDED WITH IT because the two were argued together.**
Node purity is closed BY DECLARATION rather than by sampling: `FGResourceNode.h` in the
install's `CommunityResources/Headers.zip` declares `mPurity` with NO `SaveGame` specifier,
so it cannot be serialized on any build. That is a stronger result than ADR 0003's
zero-occurrence measurement and it retires the question permanently. The substitute is an
operator annotation whose published provenance reads operator and never measured - a scope
change recorded as one, and NOT the CS-G01 gate clearing.

**READ IT AT** `docs/adr/0019-the-map-underlay-and-the-purity-declaration.md`, `accepted`
2026-09-13, adjudicated by an agent that produced none of the work it ruled on.

### 2026-09-13 - CS-1009 - CLOSED. A claim now survives the exit of the process that made it, and three designs were refuted before one held

**THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS DESIGNED.** `_state_of` decided HELD against the pid
recorded in the claim. A worker reaches python through a fresh subprocess per call, so the claiming
process exits at once and the row read RECLAIMABLE for the rest of a cycle that runs for thousands of
seconds. Measured with two real processes and a control on the same tree: the long-lived holder read
HELD and refused a second lane, the claimant that exited read RECLAIMABLE and a second lane CLAIMED
THE ROW. That is the double-booking CS-991 exists to stop, restored by the calling convention.

**WHAT CHANGED.** Liveness DELEGATES to the lane lock of the lane the record itself names, matched on
the run id the store READS OFF THAT LOCK rather than accepts from its caller - `launch_lane` never
hands the worker the driver's run id, so a caller-supplied one would have mismatched on every real
fire and answered RECLAIMABLE for every claim. The lock directory is derived from the claim root, so a
worker importing its own checkout's copy still anchors on the main tree. Ownership for release is
DERIVED too: `running_cycle_here` matches the checkout the module was imported from against the
worktree each lane lock records, and no credential crosses a subprocess boundary at all. Merged files:
`ops/loop/claims.py`, `ops/loop/lanes.py`, `tools/headless-queue.md`, `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

**PROVEN BY.** `tests/ops/test_row_claim.py::test_a_claim_outlives_the_process_that_made_it_while_its_cycle_runs`
and `::test_a_genuinely_dead_cycle_returns_its_row`, with
`::test_a_live_cycle_holds_its_row_however_old_the_record_is` fencing the age floor the acceptance
forbids by name - an inserted `age_s > 3600` floor reddens five arms. A second, independent
reproduction by an adversary that did not build it: the old tree double-books, the new tree refuses
`row_claimed`, and removing the lane lock flips the same probe to `RECLAIMABLE/pid`, which is the
control that separates graded-clean from graded-nothing.

**THREE RELEASE DESIGNS WERE REFUTED, AND THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING.** A caller-supplied `run_id` was
refuted because run ids are policed nowhere - two live claims under the identical string both
succeeded, `""` was accepted, `None` became the string `"None"` - so a crashed cycle's late wrap
deleted the live holder's record with NO malicious actor and both sides following the documented
convention. A sha256 RECEIPT over the record's bytes was refuted because every lane can read every
claim file, so the attacker recomputed it in one line - and re-hashing was the ONLY recovery path the
worker prompt left a cycle that lost the string, so the convention steered a worker into the attack.
What held was removing the credential entirely: an attacker derives its own lane, finds a record
naming another, and refuses structurally rather than by comparing a string it could compute. EVERY
CREDENTIAL A READER OF THE PROTECTED OBJECT CAN CONSTRUCT IS NOT A CREDENTIAL.

**AN ADJUDICATOR RULED THE ANCHOR FORK, and the ruling is why the provability gate is not on the state
path.** A repair that required a lock to PROVE its holder before anchoring a claim was measured to
invert the item where `proc_started` cannot read - unconditionally without psutil, which
`pyproject.toml` declares optional, and on this box through `psutil.AccessDenied` for an elevated or
scheduled-task driver - handing a LIVE cycle's row to the other lane. The ruling was strict
delegation, on the ground that `lanes.holder_is_a_stranger` already decided this exact trade one layer
down: freeing a lane on a guess is strictly worse than the wedge, and a row is a smaller unit than a
lane, so the ranking cannot invert going up. The cost is disclosed rather than hidden:
`ANCHOR_LANE_UNPROVEN` is a declared third reading, and `docs/OPERATIONS.md` section 11 documents the
operator's escape - clear the stale lane lock, never the claim record.

**A FOURTH BREACH WAS FOUND AFTER THE SUITE WENT GREEN.** Two lane locks recording ONE worktree made
`running_cycle_here` resolve by roster order, so `LANES[0]` won every time: the other lane could not
release its own records and could delete the first lane's live one by naming the public row id.
`claims.py` ASSERTED that no two lanes share a worktree and nothing enforced it. Repaired on both
sides - `lanes.try_acquire_lane` refuses a worktree another lane's live lock records, and an ambiguous
checkout now derives NO lane rather than a guess. Proven by
`::test_a_second_lane_is_refused_a_worktree_another_lane_is_running_in`,
`::test_an_ambiguous_checkout_derives_no_lane_rather_than_the_first_one` and
`::test_a_lane_sharing_a_worktree_cannot_delete_the_other_lanes_record`.

**VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AT THE MERGED SHA.** 7269 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed, exit code read from a
log sentinel rather than after a pipe; the seven skips are the same seven classes as the previous SHA
and none is new. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, bare `mypy` over 217 files, `drift_guard` and
`doc_budget` all exit 0. No frozen file is in the delta; 0 non-ASCII and 0 CR measured byte-wise on
the blobs rather than with a CR grep.

**WHAT REMAINS, stated rather than rounded up.** In a shared worktree NEITHER lane can release, so
records leak there - bounded, because the next claim clears a record whose cycle ended, and it is the
declared cost of refusing to guess. A row wedges alongside a wedged lane when a stale lock cannot
prove its holder; the escape is documented and CS-1010 carries the behaviour that would take neither
harm. The driver renders the new refusal as `lane_held` because it never reads the reason - CS-1011.
NO REAL LANE NIGHT HAS RUN: every measurement here is processes and locks driven directly, never a
driver fired end to end.

environment-variable disarm surface to a tier-0 gate.

issues no suite and the ration covers zero of the two invocations that do run. The conditional was
written correctly at the call site and wrongly in the summary, which is the half a reader sees.

### 2026-09-12 - CS-987 - CLOSED. The bind-failure arm's leak oracle asked a process-global question and attributed the answer to the call under test, so it went RED on a correct refusal and would have gone GREEN on the leak it exists to catch

**WHAT CLOSED.** `tests/surface/test_server.py::test_run_exits_non_zero_on_a_bind_failure_and_binds_nothing_else`
ended with a population question - every thread whose name contains `serve`, summed over
`threading.enumerate()`, asserted to be zero. `threading.enumerate()` is PROCESS-wide, one
xdist worker runs many modules in one process, and `clockspeed/surface/server.py` names its
serving thread `clockspeed-serve`. So a SUCCESSFUL `server.run` anywhere in that worker left
a daemon satisfying the filter for the rest of the process's life, and the arm read a
neighbour's residue as its own leak.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND, and it was not a read.** A whole-suite run on the CS-964 merge candidate
under `-n auto` went red on gw3 at `assert 1 == 0` while everything the arm is actually about
BEHAVED: the bind failed as designed, the exit was `EXIT_BIND_FAILED`, and the refusal printed
naming the port and `OSError 10048`. Because `-x` was in effect the red stopped the whole
suite at 3048 passed, which is a tier-1 cost on its own.

**THE FALSE RED WAS THE LESSER FAULT.** A population question cannot tell the subject's own
leak from a neighbour's live thread in one direction, nor from a neighbour's already-exited
thread in the other. On a run where no sibling had served yet it reported 0 whether or not
the subject leaked. It could not observe the value it was asked about, which is the one way
an arm passes for no reason at all.

**THE REPAIR.** The set of thread IDENTITIES is taken before and after the call and the
assertion is on what APPEARED. Identity rather than name, because a name is not unique and a
neighbour may start another thread sharing one.

**WHAT WAS REFUSED, and why each would have left the defect.** Narrowing the FILTER instead -
excluding daemon threads, matching the name harder, or marking the arm serial - each leaves
the oracle asking a global question and merely shrinks the population able to answer it. The
false green survives all three. The written fence in the item note said so before the repair
was attempted, and the repair did not depart from it.

**PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what the acceptance required.**

- POSITIVE: a leak planted in `server.run`'s bind-failure path - a thread named
  `clockspeed-serve-LEAKPLANT` started before the refusal returns - reddens BOTH arms, and the
  failure message names the planted thread. The plant was asserted to have LANDED before the
  run, from a script written with a file-writing tool after a quoted heredoc silently ate the
  backslashes out of the matched source line and the resulting unmutated run reported green -
  a mutant that never applied and a surviving mutant produce identical output.
- NEGATIVE: `test_the_leak_oracle_ignores_a_serving_thread_this_call_did_not_start` holds a
  foreign `clockspeed-serve` thread alive for its whole duration and stays GREEN. It also
  asserts the NAIVE population oracle still SEES that thread, so the arm measures the
  difference between the two questions rather than restating one of them. Reverting that
  arm's oracle to the population question reddens it.

**HOW TO VERIFY INDEPENDENTLY.** `python -m pytest tests/surface/test_server.py -q -p no:randomly`
reports 131 passed. The arm and its control are `test_run_exits_non_zero_on_a_bind_failure_and_binds_nothing_else`
and `test_the_leak_oracle_ignores_a_serving_thread_this_call_did_not_start`. The sibling grep is
clean and was part of the close: `threading.enumerate()` appears at exactly ONE site across
`tests/`, `clockspeed/` and `tools/`, so there is no population to repair beside it.

**THE ITEM WAS FILED AND CLOSED IN THE SAME SESSION**, which is recorded rather than hidden:
it was filed when it blocked a merge verdict, and repaired the same day because
`.githooks/pre-push` runs the suite with `-x`, so a nondeterministic cross-test red could
block every push in the project until it was fixed.

### 2026-09-11 - CS-980 - THE (14,60) PROPERTY WALL WAS OURS, NOT THE FORMAT'S. Every payload of the pinned world now decodes, and a documented gate's premise is refuted

**What changed.** `clockspeed/save/objects.py` gained a third dispatch on the version pair,
beside the two it already had for the body prefix width and the transform delta. The pair
carries a different tag grammar: one lead byte between the payload head and the first tag,
a recursive type NAME where the legacy shape has a type word plus tag-extra strings, and a
flags bitfield where the legacy shape has a guid flag. Merged files
`clockspeed/save/objects.py` and `clockspeed/save/world.py`, verified by
`tests/save/test_property_payload_14_60.py` against a synthetic fixture in
`tests/save/synthetic.py`, so the arm runs on a machine with no game and no save.

**WHY IT WAS LOOKED AT AT ALL, recorded because the trigger matters more than the fix.**
The operator demonstrated a third-party tool rendering container contents and miner
settings out of a save on this machine while this project decoded zero property tags from
the same file. `CLAUDE.md` section 8 says ground truth beats every document; `docs/GATED.md`
was the document, and it lost.

**WHAT THE GATE SAID AND WHY IT WAS WRONG.** CS-G05 recorded that every record of every
`(14,60)` save decodes zero property tags and that such a save "cannot exercise the decoder
at all - it is the CONTROL", cause unestablished between payload framing and value grammar.
The zero was real and reproduced on demand. The inference from it was not: a save that
decodes nothing under ONE grammar is not a save that carries nothing. The answer was
framing AND grammar, which is why neither candidate alone closed it.

**THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, since a plausible fix and a correct one look alike here.**
Four readings were driven against the whole record population and compared: the lead byte
alone left every container value unreachable; the lead byte plus a guid-flag reading broke
hundreds of records, almost all on `StructProperty`; a sixteen-byte struct guid was worse
still; the flags bitfield read every record with no breaks. One bit's width rests on two
tags and is recorded as weak. A bit never observed refuses the payload rather than assuming
a width - non-negotiable 7.

**WHAT IT UNBLOCKS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.** Every walked payload of the pinned development
world now reads, and container values, object references and integers are published where
none were. Struct INTERIORS are deliberately still not read: CS-829 owns that, and carrying
a new grammar into the interior reader in the same change would have made one measurement
answer for two. So an item total is still not derivable, and the reason is now a narrower
and named one - see CS-981.

**A SECOND ARM WENT VACUOUS AND WAS NARROWED RATHER THAN DELETED.**
`tests/save/test_properties.py::test_save_60_refuses_the_grammar_the_other_pairs_accept`
still passes and its zero is still true, because the sweep it runs carries its own
independent reader of the LEGACY grammar. Its DOCSTRING claimed the save reached a
terminator on no payload at all, which ground truth refutes. The claim is now stated as
what it measures - the legacy reader must go on refusing this pair, or the two grammars
have converged and the dispatch between them grades nothing. The symbol was deliberately
NOT renamed: `docs/LEDGER.md` and `docs/history_notes.md` cite it by name and both are
append-only, so a rename would rot two citations in records that are never edited.

**The license gate that ran first is the entry above this one.** No third-party source was
copied, and the two refused candidates - including the tool the operator demonstrated -
were not read. The grammar above was derived from the bytes of saves on this machine.
