### 2026-09-11 - CS-980 - LICENSE GATE RESULT. Five third-party save parsers triaged before a byte of format knowledge entered the tree, and the one the operator watched is the one that is refused

**This entry closes nothing.** It records the `CONVENTIONS.md` section 14 gate that had to
pass before the CS-980 decode work could consider an external format reference, per the
rule that the gate result is recorded BEFORE the project acts on it. Retrieved 2026-09-11.

**Why the gate ran.** The operator demonstrated satisfactory-calculator.com's interactive
map rendering container contents and miner settings out of a save on this machine, while
this project's own reader decodes zero property tags from the same file. That makes a
third-party parser the obvious hypothesis generator and therefore a license question.

**The project's own license was read, not assumed:** `LICENSE` is the MIT License,
copyright line `Copyright (c) 2026 Clockspeed contributors`. It is a frozen file under
`CLAUDE.md` section 6, so any inbound term that attaches to the whole work conflicts with
it and is refused without a verbal clearance being available.

**Per-candidate verdicts.**

- `AnthorNet/SC-InteractiveMap` - **REFUSED for every purpose, including reading.** No
  LICENSE file, GitHub reports no license, `package.json` carries no `license` field and is
  marked private. Its README states that reuse of the source and data assets is not
  permitted in any case and that the source is available for educational purposes only -
  wording that reaches past copying toward a derived independent implementation, so the
  safe default is refusal. It is very probably the code behind the map the operator
  watched, which makes it the most tempting candidate and the most clearly fenced. Its
  repository root also carries a third party's save file, so cloning it would import one.
- `etothepii4/satisfactory-file-parser` - **CLEARED WITH OBLIGATIONS.** MIT,
  `Copyright (c) 2021-2025 etothepii`, notice-retention and warranty paragraphs both
  present, manifest and license agree. Reading requires nothing. Lifting any portion would
  require reproducing the MIT text and that copyright line in a third-party notices file.
  It does NOT relicense this project. Its README states GAME versions, never numeric save
  versions - the version pair mapping stays this project's own pin.
- `ficsit-felix/ficsit-felix` - CLEARED WITH OBLIGATIONS (MIT, holder bitowl), but
  format-stale and therefore low value.
- `GreyHak/sat_sav_parse` - **REFUSED, including for reading.** GPL-3.0. Copyleft bars
  vendoring absolutely, and it is written in this project's own language, which carries the
  highest structural-copying risk of any candidate.
- `FabianFG/CUE4Parse` - reading CLEARED WITH OBLIGATIONS, vendoring REFUSED. Apache-2.0
  with an unfilled template copyright line and a NOTICE naming twenty-plus upstreams
  including a path into Epic's engine source. A clean license that is not vendor-safe.
- `moritz-h/satisfactory-3d-map`, its save-format document - reading CLEARED WITH
  OBLIGATIONS, copying REFUSED. The repository is GPL-3.0,
  `Copyright (C) 2021 - 2026 Moritz Heinemann`, and the document carries no separate grant,
  so the prose is covered by it. Not one sentence, field-name table or list may enter this
  tree. It is nonetheless the only current document found that addresses the decode
  question at all.
- `satisfactorymodding/Documentation` - UNRESOLVED and therefore refused for copying. No
  license file at the repository root and the license endpoint returns 404. Absence is not
  permission. It adds no byte-level fact.

**The wiki's save-format pages, re-measured.** They still do not cover the body of the
version pair this project parses: the page states the body has not been analyzed beyond
Patch 1.0.0.3. It now names header version 14, but as a header-only note. The byte this
project already measured false is still labelled with a name implying a meaning the bytes
do not carry, now annotated as unused garbage - which partially converges with
`BOOTSTRAP.md` section 2.4 and still refutes any flag reading of it. CS-485's verdict and
`CLAUDE.md` section 7's no-lifted-datasets fence are unchanged and were not re-litigated.

**The operative distinction, recorded because this project has conflated it before.**
Reading a source to learn a byte layout and then writing an independent implementation is
not what MIT, Apache-2.0 or GPL-3.0 attach obligations to - their duties attach to
distributing copies or conveying a derivative. Copying a line, a table, a constant list or
a fixture is a different act with a different answer per license, and under GPL-3.0 it
would relicense this project and conflict with the frozen `LICENSE`.

**The standing instruction this puts on the decode work.** Restate every adopted fact in
this project's own words and confirm it against the local bytes before it becomes code. The
always-legal path is the one CS-482 already used - derive the grammar from the saves on
this machine with a structural anchor, with any cleared reading serving only as a
hypothesis generator. No test fixture from any candidate may be copied under any license;
the synthetic-fixtures settled entry and non-negotiable 11 bar it independently of this
gate.

**No save file, no fragment of one and no hex dump of one was uploaded, pasted or
submitted anywhere during this gate.** All retrieval was outbound fetches of public
repository metadata and documents.

### 2026-09-11 - CS-970 - CLOSED. The lane names why it refused, and no night that accomplished nothing reports success

**Two acceptance clauses were AMENDED, and this record is the amendment.** The
adjudicator required the change be written down rather than inferred from its verdict,
because an agent that rewrites its own acceptance after the fact is how an acceptance
stops being a fence.

- `ROADMAP.md` asked for a test driving the DIRTY-WORKTREE precondition. No such check
  exists anywhere in `ops/loop/lane_launcher.py`: `ensure_worktree` returns early once
  `.git` is present and runs no git at all on a reused worktree. The ROADMAP line itself
  labelled that reading "unproven". A clause cannot require an arm for a precondition with
  no code, so the arm drives the real lock-repoint refusal instead. Adding a dirty-tree
  check was considered and REFUSED: a dirty lane worktree is normal between cycles, and
  refusing it would convert a recoverable state into a permanently dead lane.
- `ROADMAP.md` asked for ELEVEN identical consecutive launch failures to stop the driver.
  The driver stops at THREE. Eleven was the count observed in the incident, not a designed
  threshold, and three matches the existing consecutive-error precedent. Stopping sooner
  discharges the clause strictly.

**What shipped,** across `aa5a828`, `6814f90`, `e3276bb`, `6bad0e4` and `03bcf1c`. Merged
files: `ops/loop/lane_launcher.py`, `ops/loop/queue_loop.py`, `tests/test_lane_launcher.py`,
`tests/test_queue_loop.py`. A closed thirteen-member `LAUNCH_REASONS` vocabulary, one
path-free code per raise site; the driver validating an incoming code against its OWN copy
and rendering its own literal by index; a consecutive-launch-failure stop with its own exit
code; a no-push cycle recorded as a verdict and refused by the roll-up; and a progress
counter that stops any night which never produces a commit. Verified by
`tests/test_lane_launcher.py::test_every_launch_error_raise_site_names_a_reason`,
`::test_every_raise_site_keeps_the_reason_code_it_was_reviewed_with`,
`tests/test_queue_loop.py::test_the_driver_and_the_launcher_hold_the_same_reason_vocabulary`,
`::test_the_launch_fault_row_never_renders_the_caller_s_object`,
`::test_a_night_that_never_completes_a_cycle_cannot_run_the_full_budget` and
`::test_a_night_committing_to_the_lane_branch_runs_its_whole_budget`.

**THE SUITE WAS GREEN AT EVERY REFUTED COMMIT.** Four adversarial rounds landed findings
against trees that had just passed 6224, 6241 and 6256 tests. Round 1: `lane_held` reset the
counters, so a night whose lock was held every cycle ran all twelve and exited 0. Round 2: a
COMPLETED cycle that pushed nothing did the same; a budget at or below the limit exited 0;
and an unlisted stop word read as success through a `.get(stopped, EXIT_OK)` default. Round
3: the progress test read the `ok` roll-up, which is false on a no-push cycle, so a worker
following `tools/headless-queue.md`'s own instruction to push the LANE BRANCH on a rejected
push had its night killed at cycle 3 - a REGRESSION this work introduced, worse than the
burn it was written to stop. THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING: the same defect reappeared four
times wearing a different field each time, and only an allowlist over what counts as
progress, rather than a denylist of what does not, finally held.

**A PRIVACY GUARANTEE THAT WAS NEARLY TRUE.** The driver validated the reason by VALUE and
then rendered the CALLER'S OBJECT, so a `str` subclass whose data is honestly a vocabulary
member but whose `__str__` returns a home path was written verbatim into the durable JSONL
row. Two adversaries broke it by different mechanisms. Never reachable in the field, since
every raise site binds a module constant, but the fix is structural: `type(reason) is str`
plus an index substitution, so this module renders only its own literal. Either defence
alone is insufficient.

**THIS FILE'S OWN 2026-09-11 RECORD IS CORRECTED.** The entry above states that CS-970's
eleven consecutive failures "were a launcher meeting a bare repository". That cannot be the
mechanism. Every failing cycle left a 134-byte worker log containing the `lane start` header
that `ops/loop/run_lane.ps1` writes, and a bare-repository fault raises in `ensure_worktree`
BEFORE any worker is spawned, so no log would exist at all. The runner started every time and
died before writing its exit line. The trigger remains UNDIAGNOSED.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE.** No arm calls `launch_lane` through to a real spawned worker;
every arm injects seams. Eleven of the twelve reasons could be recorded WRONG in the field
with the suite green. If the lane is re-armed and cycle 2 fails as before, the row will most
likely read `runner_exited_early` or `spawn_failed`, naming the proximate mechanism and
sending the reader to the runner rather than to the contended tree. The work makes the next
failure self-describing; it does not make the lane start.

**RESIDUALS, all filed rather than left implicit.** CS-974 holds the `_CI_ROLLUP_BAD`
denylist, under which a cancelled, skipped, timed-out, unavailable or unknown CI verdict
still rolls up as a good cycle. CS-975 holds the fact that nothing reads the driver's exit
code at all, so `EXIT_NO_PROGRESS` and `EXIT_UNKNOWN_STOP` are decorative in production.
Accepted and not filed: a worker that advances HEAD with a junk commit reads as progress,
and the site-to-code mapping arm encodes a reviewed reading rather than ground truth.

**Independently verified** at `03bcf1c` in a worktree pinned to that SHA, tree confirmed
unmoved at both ends: `pytest tests -q -n auto --dist loadfile` exit 0, 6262 passed, 7
skipped; `mypy` exit 0, 189 source files; `ruff check .` exit 0; `tools/drift_guard.py` exit
0, 11 guards, 10 PASS, 1 WARN, 0 FAIL, the WARN being CS-971's ROADMAP budget;
`tools/doc_budget.py` exit 0, VERDICT WARN, 1 soft failure. Every behavioural claim was
DRIVEN against the real `run_loop` and the real `main`, with a control run proving a
`time.sleep` patch changed no outcome.

### 2026-09-11 - CS-973 - CLOSED. The suite copied 23 of the operator's real saves into the live copies directory, and the repair is three redirects plus one session-wide count that discovers the NEXT writer rather than the two already known

**Filed and closed from outside.** The finding came from Legion Wallpaper's
write-attribution tracer, run against this tree on operator direction; the repair
below was made in this repository by that session. No other sibling tree was
touched.

**The defect, reproduced here rather than taken on report.** `world.load_world`
copies its subject through `workdir.copy_for_read` before it parses a byte, and
the work root that copy lands in DEFAULTS TO `<repo>/work`. Three arms reached a
real save with no redirect in place: `test_phase4_gate.py`'s
`test_a_real_world_parses_end_to_end` and
`test_every_real_save_in_the_library_loads_through_the_one_entry_point`, and
`test_acceptance.py`'s `test_every_endpoint_bootstrap_names_answers_over_verified_tls`,
which drives the live server through `providers.SaveWorldProvider`. A traced run
of those two modules alone wrote 23 files carrying `COPY_SUFFIX` into
`work/saves/`, one per save in the library, with the tracer's planted control
proving the instrument was live. Non-negotiables 1 and 11 both held: the
originals were untouched and the directory is gitignored with no `.sav` tracked.
This was corpus pollution, not a leak - and that directory is what the save layer
is measured against, so anything globbing `*.sav` there saw 23 worlds that are
not worlds.

**Why the acceptance module was a writer at all, which is the part a reader will
not guess.** No arm in it names the save layer. The copy happens inside
`observations`, two fixture levels below any signature, during MODULE setup. A
function-scoped redirect would therefore have been installed and torn down
entirely AFTER the writes it was meant to prevent, which is why the fixture there
is module-scoped, autouse, and holds its own `pytest.MonkeyPatch.context()`
rather than requesting the function-scoped `monkeypatch`.

**What shipped.** Three files, additions only, no line deleted or moved.
`tests/save/test_phase4_gate.py` gains an autouse `isolated_work_root` matching
the shipped fixture of the same name in `tests/save/test_world.py`, plus
`test_the_library_sweep_leaves_its_copies_off_the_repo`.
`tests/surface/test_acceptance.py` gains the module-scoped autouse redirect plus
`test_the_work_root_the_live_server_copied_into_is_outside_the_repository`.
`tests/conftest.py` gains the session-scoped autouse guard
`_the_live_copies_directory_is_left_as_it_was_found`, appended at the FOOT for
the reason the CS-968 scrub above it is: the deep archive pins line numbers into
that module.

**AUTOUSE RATHER THAN REQUESTED BY NAME, DELIBERATELY.** Attaching the redirect
to the two arms that copy today closes those two and leaves the next arm that
loads a real save to re-open the hole, which is exactly how this one was opened.

**THE SESSION GUARD DISCOVERS THE WRITER RATHER THAN ENCODING IT,** which is what
the acceptance criterion asked for and what the per-module fixtures cannot do. It
counts before and after over the whole run, so a writer added by a module that
does not exist yet is caught where it lands. It derives the live directory from
`conftest.py`'s own position instead of calling `workdir.work_root()`, because
that resolver reads `ENV_WORK_ROOT` and would make the guard watch every
directory except the one at risk. It reports a DELTA and never a listing: a copy
carries the name of the save it came from, so a set of names in a failing
assertion is a set of the operator's world names (non-negotiable 12). Attribution
is the tracer's job and the failure message says so.

**THE FIRST ATTEMPT MANUFACTURED THE ROT IT WAS REPAIRING, and the full suite
caught it.** Both phase 4 blocks were first written into the Clause 1 section
where they read best. That moved `WRITER_WRITE_SURFACE` off line 2089 and
reddened `test_docs_citations.py` twice, because `docs/item_notes/phase4.md`
pins that line for the still-open CS-446 note. The guard offered two remedies

### 2026-09-11 - CS-303 - CLOSED. ADR 0006's name-fence on `Building.unsharded_clock_base` is now mechanical, and the round was REFUTED once on a gate the new file left red

**The defect.** ADR 0006 decided how the one shipped ceiling operand reaches the model
and said in as many words what it did not close: "nothing mechanical stops a future
caller reading `Building.unsharded_clock_base` directly and clamping without going
through `clamp_to_unsharded_base`. This ADR claims the name and the docstring as that
fence and claims no more." A name is a hint. The trap ADR 0005 named is that the
un-sharded base READS as an achievable maximum, and because every shipped entry reports
the same un-overclocked value, a caller that clamps to it caps every solve at 100
percent and looks correct on every building nobody has overclocked - invisible in
exactly the worlds where testing is easiest.

**The root cause, stated as a class rather than as this field.** A fence whose only
enforcement is the reader's diligence is enforced by nothing. The repair is a guard that
refuses the READ, not a better name.

**What shipped.** `tests/solve/test_ceiling_fence.py`, an AST guard over the whole
tracked-and-not-ignored Python tree. `clockspeed/solve/power.py` is the one owner, held
as an exact PATH rather than as a package - widening it to `clockspeed/solve/` would let
any sibling clamp silently, which is the defect. The test corpus is exempted by exact
repo-relative path with a reason per entry, never by a glob, and three arms keep the
table honest: no key may carry a glob metacharacter, every key must name a file git
actually tracks, and every key must still hold a read it forgives. A dead forgiveness is
prose the next reader cannot tell from a live rule.

spelling the name in a string, so a guard reading only the attribute node is evaded by
typing the hand-back. Both spellings are detected and each has its own arm. The
anti-rot direction is swept the same way - a stale, globbed, untracked or reasonless
exemption, and an owner path that no longer reads the field at all, which would make
every other arm pass for the wrong reason.

`test_every_exemption_names_a_file_git_actually_tracks`,
`test_every_exemption_still_holds_a_read_it_forgives`,
`test_every_exemption_records_a_reason`.

**REFUSE VERSUS STATE, RULED.** Refuse on a tracked difference; state loudly on untracked
files and on a pushed sha that is not HEAD. The file's own trade governs and it is written
there twice: in a gate a LOUD FALSE REFUSAL beats a SILENT FALSE ACCEPT. The false-refusal
surface is named rather than waved at - pushing a finished commit while work-in-progress
edits sit in the tree, and the autonomous lane if it ever leaves a tracked modification
uncommitted. Untracked files must STAY stated: refusing a new untracked file under `tests/`

local sha. Where they agree the comparison is identical. Where they differ - `git push
origin HEAD~1:main`, or pushing a branch other than the checked-out one - the suite graded
content that is a statement about no shipped commit at all, and the message must say the
gate is VACUOUS FOR THAT REF in the CS-703 register, not merely that a different branch is
being pushed. HEAD-equality decides refuse-versus-state; it is not the thing being asserted.

### 2026-09-11 - CS-968 - CLOSED. A push from a WORKTREE exports GIT_DIR, and the suite rewrote the repository it was running in

**THE MECHANISM, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED.** `git push` exports `GIT_DIR` to the
pre-push hook WHEN AND ONLY WHEN the push originates in a LINKED WORKTREE. Measured
side by side, same repository, same hook:

    push from the main checkout   GIT_EXEC_PATH, GIT_PREFIX
    push from a linked worktree   GIT_EXEC_PATH, GIT_PREFIX, GIT_DIR

`.githooks/pre-push` runs `pytest tests`, so the whole suite can run holding a pointer
at a repository nobody in it named. A throwaway `git init --bare` then re-initialises
THE REAL REPOSITORY, and `core.bare` plus any `git config` write land in the config
every worktree SHARES. That is why a lane worker that never touched the main checkout
broke the main checkout, and why it read as repository corruption.

**IT HAS TWO INDEPENDENT HALVES AND FIXING ONLY THE FIRST LOOKS COMPLETE.**

- CHILD-SIDE, the damaging half. A spawned `git` or nested `pytest` inherits the
  pointer. Fixed by `tests/git_env.py`, the one owner of the scrub, applied at five
  spawn sites in `tests/test_precommit_gate.py`, `tests/test_hook_interpreter_ladder.py`
  and `tests/test_pre_push_ref_race.py`. `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`
  are deliberately KEPT - they are how a fixture cuts the operator's own configuration
  off, so scrubbing them would undo the isolation.
- IN-PROCESS, the silent half. `load_gate()` imports `tools/precommit_gate.py` in
  process, so it resolves its repository from `os.environ` at call time; the dated
  headings driver enumerates documents the same way. Neither goes through a child, so
  a clean child-side measurement says nothing about them. Fixed by a process-wide
  scrub at the FOOT of `tests/conftest.py`, run at import because module-level code in
  a test module executes during COLLECTION, before any fixture could fire.

**VERIFIED BY.** `tests/test_git_env_scrub.py::test_a_scrubbed_environment_keeps_an_init_inside_the_directory_it_was_aimed_at`,
`::test_a_scrubbed_environment_keeps_a_config_write_inside_its_own_repository`, and the
control that makes both mean anything,
`::test_an_inherited_git_dir_really_does_relocate_an_init`, which does the damage ON
PURPOSE with the pointer left in place and asserts the decoy turns bare. Plus
`tests/test_repo_config_hygiene.py::test_this_repository_is_not_configured_bare` and
`::test_this_repository_does_not_carry_the_fixture_identity`, which grade the STATE so
a recurrence is loud whatever causes it.

**THE END-TO-END MEASUREMENT.** A push of `cs964-seam` FROM ITS WORKTREE - the exact
operation that stranded `core.bare` twice - returned 0 with 6209 passed, 7 skipped, and
the shared config CLEAN afterwards. Before the fix the same operation blocked and left
the repository unusable for every checkout on the machine.

**THREE MECHANISMS WERE PROPOSED AND REFUTED BEFORE THE RIGHT ONE.** The refutations
were real measurements and the conclusions drawn from them were too broad: "no hook
exports GIT_DIR" was measured only from a MAIN CHECKOUT, which is the one arrangement
where the bug cannot fire. A sibling tree's adversary made the identical mistake, and
its note was cited here as independent corroboration - two measurements agreeing
because both were taken in the wrong configuration. A NEGATIVE IS ONLY AS BROAD AS THE

### 2026-09-10 - CS-210 - CLOSED. The absent-`mMaxPotential` branch is grounded in the shipped document, and the two sets ADR 0006's common-mode risk could not separate are MEASURED IDENTICAL

**The defect.** ADR 0006's adjudication named a COMMON-MODE RISK: both fences the ADR
relies on read the same hand-authored corpus, so the registry-layer and solve-layer tests
were one fixture read twice rather than two independent confirmations. That a
registry-published `Building` can lack `mMaxPotential` AT ALL was asserted nowhere against
the shipped data. The pin recorded per-VALUE counts (`"1.000000": 62`), and a per-value
counter is structurally blind to the absent case: an entry carrying none of the watched
fields is counted by no key at all. So the branch that reads an absent field as None -
live code in `clockspeed/data/registry.py` - rested on a corpus entry a corpus author
chose to write.

**The root cause.** The census counted VALUES and never the POPULATION. Four watched
fields each had a value counter and none had a denominator, so "62 entries carry it" could
not be read against "of how many".

**What shipped.** Census schema 1 to 2, adding `registry_building_field_presence`:
per watched field, how many registry-published buildings carry it and how many do not.
Merged files: `clockspeed/data/version.py`, `tests/data/test_version.py`,
`tests/data/test_registry.py`, `tests/test_docs_citations.py`, `tests/test_archive_rot.py`,
and the four doc files the closure moves - `ROADMAP.md`, `docs/item_notes.md`,
`docs/history_notes.md` and this file. The tenth path is a DELETION:
the Phase 2 leaf under `docs/item_notes/`, whose only item was this one, so the
leaf is named rather than spelled - a path this change deletes cannot resolve, and
pinning a dead spelling would widen the bare-path exemption for a site that did not
have to exist.

Measured from the live install this cycle by `python tools/drift_guard.py --re-extract`:
all four fields split 62 present, 6 absent over 68 published buildings. The absent half is
the number that did not exist before, and it is what makes the None branch a statement
about the shipped game.

**The predicate is restated, not imported, and the restatement is fenced.**
`clockspeed/data/version.py` may not import `clockspeed/data/registry.py` - the
allowed-import matrix in `tests/data/test_phase2_gate.py` permits `version` exactly
`docs_extract`, and that matrix is asserted in both directions. So
`is_registry_building_entry` states the published-building predicate a second time on
purpose, and
`tests/data/test_registry.py::test_the_census_building_predicate_agrees_with_the_registrys`
compares the two entry by entry over a case table carrying both a positive and a negative
verdict, so two predicates that both answered False everywhere could not pass it.

**The sibling sweep, and a finding beyond the acceptance clause.** The item's own note
recorded an open unknown - ADR 0005 measured 62 entries carrying `mMaxPotential` while
`clockspeed/data/registry.py` states 6 power-bearing entries carry no exponent, and
WHETHER THOSE SETS OVERLAP WAS UNKNOWN. Probed against the live install this cycle: the
absent sets of all four watched fields are the SAME 6 entries. The common-mode unknown is
resolved.

**That identity is NOT what the census guards, stated plainly so the caveat survives this
cycle.** The recorded key is a pair of COUNTS per field. A future build that moved which
entries lack the fields, without changing how many, would leave every count unchanged.
The acceptance clause asks for counts and counts are what shipped; the set identity above
is a measurement recorded here, not a guarded invariant.

**Tests, by name.** `tests/data/test_version.py::test_the_tracked_pin_grounds_the_absent_max_potential_branch_in_shipped_data`,
`::test_the_census_counts_the_registry_published_buildings_that_lack_a_watched_field`,
`::test_the_census_counts_a_watched_field_as_present_on_every_baseline_building`,
`::test_the_building_census_ignores_an_entry_no_recognized_group_holds`,
`tests/data/test_registry.py::test_the_absent_max_potential_branch_is_grounded_in_the_shipped_document`,
`::test_the_census_building_predicate_agrees_with_the_registrys`.

**The failing-first order, with the reason quoted.** The three assertions that read the
tracked pin failed `KeyError: 'registry_building_field_presence'` against the
implementation with the pin left unregenerated - which is the defect itself, the pin
carrying no such census - and went green only after `--re-extract` measured it from the

**The census reads the RECOGNIZED groups, and that is the one place it deliberately reads
less than the whole document.** `census()` is otherwise handed `DocsDocument.all_groups`,

### 2026-09-10 - CS-963 - CLOSED after three rounds. Refuted three times by an adversarial lens, each time against a green suite

**THIS IS THE CLOSING RECORD.** Two earlier CS-963 entries below it stand as written: the
first states a claim that was too strong, the second corrects it. Nothing in this file is
edited once written, so the three together are the actual history - which is the point of
the rule, and in this case the history is the more useful artefact.

**WHAT CLOSED.** No shipped frame in a raised traceback - cause chain included - holds the
raw save, the decompressed body, or a decoded personal-data string in a form any rendering
channel prints. Fifteen scrubs across four modules, EACH MEASURED LOAD-BEARING AT THE TREE
THAT SHIPS: `header.parse_header`, `header.reveal_strings` twice (the buffer and the four
decoded strings), `header.read_header`, `header._Cursor.string`, `header._Cursor.__repr__`,
`objects._Cursor.string`, `objects._Cursor.__repr__`, `objects.parse_body`,
`chunks._read_size_pair`, `chunks.read_frame`, `chunks.iter_frames`,
`chunks.decompress_body`, `world._walk_body`, `world.load_world_from_bytes`. Fifteen of
fifteen killed, zero survivors, graded against a pristine green floor with each mutation
asserted to have landed and every file restored from a byte snapshot.

**THE ACCEPTANCE AS FILED WAS UNACHIEVABLE, and that is the item's most durable result.** A
parser holds the bytes it parses, so the only tree in which no frame HOLDS the save is a
tree with no parser. `CLAUDE.md` section 8 - the probe beats the document. The clause is
narrowed where it is checked, in
`tests/save/test_world.py::test_the_only_retained_buffers_are_encapsulated_and_every_holder_withholds`:
no frame may hold either buffer in a form a renderer PRINTS, and every remaining holder
must reach it through an object that withholds it across `__repr__`, `__str__` AND
`__format__` - asserted against each holder the sweep FINDS, never against a list.

**THE DEFECT THE ITEM EXISTED TO FIX, and it was never the scrubs.** Every privacy arm in
the layer shared a walker following `exc.__traceback__` alone, so a frame arriving as a
`__cause__` was outside all of them BY CONSTRUCTION. The arms were green and the save was
live in shipped frames at the same time.
`tests/save/test_properties.py::_frames_in_the_cause_chain` follows `__cause__` and
`__context__`, terminates on cycles, and honours `__suppress_context__` - the last MEASURED
against `traceback` itself, so a renderer that began showing suppressed frames makes the
walker wrong rather than merely different.

**A SECOND ORACLE, because one was never enough.** `_leaking_locals` asks what a frame
RENDERS; `_reaches_the_needle` and `_structural_holders` ask what it HOLDS - reflexively
through attributes, MRO-declared slots, container members, closure cells, partials, bound
receivers, suspended generator frames and decoded strings.
`::test_the_structural_sweep_sees_what_the_repr_sweep_cannot` states the gap between the
two as a positive fact over one value, so it cannot pass by both being blind.

**THREE REFUTATIONS, AND WHAT EACH ONE TAUGHT.**

Round one shipped green with four leaks live and one introduced. The arm that should have
caught the worst of them - the decompressed body in `world._walk_body` and
`objects.parse_body` - was green because its fixture cut the body at its halfway point
while the planted marker sat past the cut. Its control asserted the marker was in the
UNTRUNCATED blob, a different byte string from the one the sweep walked. A CONTROL THAT
PROVES THE ORACLE CAN SEE A VALUE THE SWEEP NEVER ENCOUNTERS IS WORTH LESS THAN NO CONTROL.

Round two introduced a disclosure while removing one: the `__repr__` added to withhold the
buffer printed `len(self._data)`, the exact size of the player's save, which
`object.__repr__` never emitted. No arm could flag it - the sweep matches a planted marker
substring and a size is not a substring of anything.

Round three found the byte-identical TWIN of a scrub round two had just applied.
`objects._Cursor.string` is the same code as `header._Cursor.string` against the
decompressed body, and round two's commit message said the sibling grep had condemned the
siblings. It had not been run against that module. A CLAIMED GREP IS NOT A GREP.

**THREE SEPARATE ARMS WERE VACUOUS AND ONE SCRUB WAS UNMEASURED, all found by mutation
rather than by reading.** The first `_Cursor.string` arm reused a fixture that corrupts the
FIRST byte of its own probe and plants no markers at all, so it swept for something never
in the bytes and SURVIVED its own mutant. The first wide-encoding arm built a correct wide
fixture and then drove a TRUNCATION, which raises before any slice is bound - wide and
narrow gave byte-identical verdicts. And the `body` scrub's arm drove two cases that
between them discriminated nothing, so "deleting either left the suite green" was read as
evidence of redundancy when it was evidence of a blind arm. AN ARM CAN CARRY A CORRECT
FIXTURE AND STILL MEASURE NOTHING: what a sweep grades is the frames the refusal enters.

**THE STRUCTURAL ORACLE RETURNED A FALSE CLEAN and was repaired.** `seen` was a flat
identity set: a value first reached AT the depth boundary was recorded, its children cut
off by the boundary, and a SHALLOWER path to it afterwards hit the set and returned
nothing. It now maps identity to the shallowest depth walked, pinned by
`::test_the_structural_sweep_does_not_go_blind_when_a_deep_path_is_walked_first`, whose
chain length is exact - one hop either side and the old walker passes it too.

**ONE SCRUB WAS DELETED RATHER THAN ADDED.** With the unconditional guard in place, the
`ObjectError` handler's own `del body` was redundant - and a redundant scrub is
UNMEASURABLE, because removing it changes nothing and it cannot be told apart from a scrub
that never worked.

**RAISED WITH THE OPERATOR, NOT DECIDED HERE.** `chunks.DecompressedBody.__repr__` renders
the payload's SIZE. An adversary calls that the same disclosure this item removed from
`_Cursor.__repr__`, and the comparison is fair - the same category is live in
`objects.ObjectRecord.__repr__` (offset and length), `objects.PropertyName.__repr__` (three
string lengths) and `header.SaveHeader.__repr__` (body offset). But it is a RECORDED CS-852
decision and reversing one of those quietly inside a repair round is not an agent's call.
See `ROADMAP.md` under CS-965.

`clockspeed/save/world.py`, `clockspeed/save/objects.py`,
`tests/save/test_properties.py`, `tests/save/test_world.py`, `tests/save/test_header.py`,
`tests/save/test_chunks.py`, `tests/test_exception_rendering.py`,
`tests/test_docs_citations.py`.

**Verify independently:** `python -m pytest tests -q -n auto` - 6186 passed, 7 skipped,

**WHAT THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF.** Every fixture is synthetic; no real save was parsed. And

### 2026-09-10 - CS-963 - CORRECTION AND REPAIR ROUND. The entry below overstated what closed, and three lenses refuted it after a green suite

**THIS CORRECTS THE CS-963 ENTRY BELOW IT RATHER THAN REPLACING IT.** That entry is
accurate about what it did and wrong about what that finished. Nothing in this file is
edited once written, so the correction is a later record - and the two read together are
the actual history, which is the point of the rule.

**WHAT THE ENTRY BELOW CLAIMED AND SHOULD NOT HAVE.** It said no clockspeed frame anywhere
in a raised traceback, cause chain included, holds the raw save or the decompressed body.
Three adversarial lenses were dispatched against the frozen commit and all three REFUTED
it. The suite was green, 6165 passed, at the moment every one of the findings below was
live. That is the third consecutive time this item family has been refuted after a green
suite, and the second time by the privacy lens specifically.

**THE ACCEPTANCE AS FILED WAS UNACHIEVABLE, AND SAYING SO IS THE MAIN RESULT.** A parser
holds the bytes it parses. `header._Cursor` and `objects._Cursor` retain the buffer for as
long as there is a parse in progress, so the only tree in which no frame HOLDS the save is
a tree with no parser in it. `CLAUDE.md` section 8: the probe beats the document. The
clause is narrowed where it is checked, in
`tests/save/test_world.py::test_the_only_retained_buffers_are_encapsulated_and_every_holder_withholds`,
to two things that are both achievable and stronger than what was there before. First, no
frame holds either buffer in a form a renderer PRINTS - a structural holder path with no
attribute hop in it is a frame local that IS the buffer, and there must be none. Second,
every remaining holder must reach the buffer through an object that WITHHOLDS it, asserted
against each holder the sweep FINDS rather than against a list written down in advance.

**FOUR LEAKS THE FIRST ROUND LEFT LIVE.**

`world._walk_body` and `objects.parse_body` both bind the WHOLE decompressed body with no
scrub, and the object stage's refusal unwinds through both. A renderer prints the body out
of either. THE ARM THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS WAS GREEN THE WHOLE TIME, and its failure
is the same one this item exists to abolish: `_truncated_body_blob` cuts the body at its
halfway point while the planted marker sits past that cut, so the payload the walk refused
never contained the marker at all. Its control asserted the marker was in the UNTRUNCATED
blob - a different byte string from the one the sweep walked. A control that proves the
oracle can see a value the sweep never encounters is worth less than no control.

`header._Cursor.string` slices one header string into `raw` and raises `HeaderFormatError`
out of that frame when it will not decode. That slice is not the whole file, it is exactly
the options string or the session name. Both header arms drive a TRUNCATION, which raises
before `raw` is ever bound, so the scrubbed path and the driven path were disjoint.

`load_world_from_bytes` dropped the body only in its `ObjectError` handler, on the stated
grounds that this was the only handler in which the name was bound. That was false for
every other exit.

**AND ONE LEAK THE FIRST ROUND INTRODUCED.** `_Cursor.__repr__`, added to withhold the
buffer, printed `len(self._data)` - the exact byte size of the player's save file, which
`object.__repr__` never emitted. A change whose entire purpose was to reduce what a
renderer prints added a disclosure, and no arm could have flagged it, because the sweep
matches a planted marker substring and a file size is not a substring of anything.

**THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM WAS WRONG IN KIND FOR ONE SCRUB.** `_Cursor.__repr__` was graded
by making it LEAK. The mutation that matters is REMOVAL, because the baseline it replaced
was the inherited `object.__repr__` - and with the method deleted, 604 arms stayed green.
AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT IS NOT A SURVIVING MUTANT: it is an unmeasured property, and the
answer is to measure the property structurally rather than to weaken the claim. The
invariant arm now asserts that every retained holder DECLARES its own `__repr__`, so a
holder withholding by accident reddens. It found its own sibling immediately:
`objects._Cursor` was relying on `object.__repr__` and now states the requirement.

**A SECOND ORACLE, BECAUSE ONE WAS NEVER ENOUGH.** `_leaking_locals` asks what a frame
RENDERS. `tests/save/test_properties.py::_reaches_the_needle` and `::_structural_holders`
ask what it HOLDS, following attributes, slots and container members reflexively to a
bounded depth with identity tracked for cycles. Reflexive rather than a list of known
types, because a list is silent the day a third holder is written.
`::test_the_structural_sweep_sees_what_the_repr_sweep_cannot` states the gap between the
two as a positive fact over one value, so it cannot pass by both being blind.

**THE ORACLE BLIND SPOT THAT MATTERS MOST ON A REAL SAVE, AND IT IS NOT FIXED HERE.**
Every fixture in this suite writes header strings as UTF-8. Unreal writes UTF-16-LE the
moment a string carries one non-ASCII character, which a real session name or player
display name routinely does. The marker oracle searches `repr()` for an ASCII needle, so a
wide-encoded string is invisible to it while a renderer prints it legibly.
`tests/save/test_header.py::test_the_marker_sweep_is_not_blind_to_a_wide_encoded_header_string`
now pins the gap and sweeps the WIDE spelling, which is the one the file actually
contains. THIS IS CS-963'S OWN DEFECT ONE LEVEL UP and it is filed, not finished: the
remaining ASCII-only arms in this layer are still measuring an encoding the personal-data
fields do not use. See `ROADMAP.md` under CS-964.

**ONE SCRUB WAS DELETED RATHER THAN ADDED.** With the unconditional guard in place, the
`ObjectError` handler's own `del body` became redundant - and a redundant scrub is not
belt-and-braces, it is UNMEASURABLE. Removing it changed nothing, so it was
indistinguishable from a scrub that never worked. Both survived mutation while both were
present; one alone is killed.

**FOURTEEN OF FOURTEEN SCRUBS MEASURED LOAD-BEARING, ZERO SURVIVORS**, including both
`__repr__` DELETION mutants. Re-graded against the shipped tree after every repair, not
carried forward from the earlier round.

**A FIXTURE THAT MADE ITS OWN ARM VACUOUS, caught by the same mutation run.** The first
`_Cursor.string` arm reused `_blob_with_an_undecodable_session_name`, which corrupts the
FIRST byte of its probe and plants no markers at all - so the arm swept for something that
was never in the bytes, and SURVIVED its own mutant. The replacement corrupts a byte
APPENDED AFTER the marker, so the slice will not decode and still spells what the sweep
hunts.

### 2026-09-10 - CS-963 - CLOSED. The walker was the defect and the scrubs were the symptom; nine of nine measured load-bearing

**What was wrong.** `clockspeed/save/header.py` and `clockspeed/save/chunks.py` bound the
raw save as a frame local and never dropped it. `world.py` scrubs its own frame, but
`raise ... from exc` puts the CAUSE's frames in the rendered traceback, so
`pytest --showlocals` and `TracebackException(capture_locals=True)` both printed the
plaintext options string out of them - platform, account id and player display name on a
real save, which is the echo path non-negotiable 12 forbids.

**THE DEFECT THAT HID IT IS THE HALF WORTH KEEPING.** The sweep every privacy arm in the
layer shared followed `__traceback__` alone and never `__cause__`, so a frame arriving as
a cause was outside all of them BY CONSTRUCTION - not missed, unreachable. The arms were
green, a verifier confirmed, and the save was live in four shipped frames at the same
time. An oracle that cannot observe the value it is asked about returns an empty verdict
about ITSELF, and that is indistinguishable from a pass.

**What shipped.** Merged files: `clockspeed/save/header.py`, `clockspeed/save/chunks.py`,
`tests/save/test_properties.py`, `tests/save/test_world.py`, `tests/save/test_header.py`,
`tests/save/test_chunks.py`, `tests/test_exception_rendering.py`,
`tests/test_docs_citations.py`.

The walker is `tests/save/test_properties.py::_frames_in_the_cause_chain` over
`::_chained_exceptions`, with `::_shipped_frames` applying the package-root filter. It
follows `__cause__` AND `__context__`, tracks identity so a cycle terminates, and HONOURS
`__suppress_context__`. That last is a measurement rather than a preference: `traceback`
prints neither a suppressed exception nor its frames, so sweeping them would report a leak
through a channel no renderer has, and this layer uses `from None` deliberately where a
library message could quote bytes.

**THE CONTROLS DEPEND ON NO PRODUCTION CODE, which is the point.** A control that broke
when a scrub landed would disarm itself alongside the leak. All three raise over a marker
local to the test module:
`::test_the_direct_walker_cannot_see_a_local_held_in_a_cause_frame` pins the old walker's
blindness as a POSITIVE fact, so reverting the widening reddens rather than going quietly
green; `::test_the_cause_chain_walker_sees_a_local_held_in_a_cause_frame` is the known-good
control; `::test_the_walker_honours_suppression_exactly_as_the_renderer_does` runs the
renderer and asserts agreement, so a CPython that began showing suppressed frames makes
the walker wrong rather than merely different.
`::test_the_cause_chain_walker_terminates_on_a_self_referential_chain` covers the cycle.

**Seven scrubs, two shapes.** `parse_header` and `reveal_strings` UNBIND the buffer as
soon as `_Cursor` encapsulates it - strictly stronger than an unwind guard, because the
name is gone for the function's whole lifetime and no later `return` can forget a handler.
`read_header`, `_read_size_pair`, `read_frame`, `iter_frames` and `decompress_body` take
the `except BaseException: del ...; raise` guard `world.py` already used.
`decompress_body` drops the inflated body with the raw save and pre-binds `stream` and
`inflated`, because `del` on a never-bound name raises from inside the handler and would
MASK the real refusal with a `NameError`.

**TWO SITES THE FILED MEASUREMENT DID NOT NAME, both from the sibling grep - which is
where the value of that step is.** `_read_size_pair` is a private helper that binds the
same whole buffer and raises out of it on a size-block disagreement. And `reveal_strings`
holds the DECODED options string, not merely the bytes: the four header strings are read
one after another, so a refusal on the last unwinds with the earlier ones bound as
plaintext. The opt-in flag says the CALLER is a render site; it says nothing about where a
traceback out of that frame ends up, and ADR 0007 decision item 4 forbids putting these
values in exception context at all.

**`_Cursor.__repr__` now STATES its withholding** rather than inheriting it from
`object`. After the early unbind the buffer survives only in `self._data`, and every
cursor method that raises leaves `self` in a frame a renderer prints - so making that class
a dataclass later, whose generated repr would dump the whole file, is now a deliberate act
and not a one-line accident. Measured load-bearing: the dataclass-shaped repr reddens
three arms.

**NINE OF NINE SCRUBS MEASURED LOAD-BEARING, ZERO SURVIVORS.** Each was neutralised in
turn against a pristine green floor, with the mutation asserted to have landed and the
bytecode cache purged first, and both files restored from a byte snapshot rather than from
git. Killed: `parse_header`, `reveal_strings` buffer, `reveal_strings` decoded strings,
`read_header`, `_Cursor.__repr__`, `_read_size_pair`, `read_frame`, `iter_frames`,
`decompress_body`.

**THE FIRST MUTATION RUN GRADED CODE THAT IS NOT WHAT SHIPS, and three scrubs SURVIVED
it.** `reveal_strings`, `read_header` and `_read_size_pair` had no arm at all - the fix
was live and unguarded, which is a fix with no guard. Their arms were written, and the run
was then repeated against the final tree after the sweep was relocated, because a verdict
covers only the state it ruled on.

**A LOCAL HELPER PULLED TWO SILENT MODULES INTO THREE GUARDS AT ONCE.** The first cut
computed the package root inside `test_header.py` and `test_chunks.py`. `Path(...).resolve()`
is a library primitive, so both modules - which had never declared a reach - entered the
scope of the reach guard, the live-locals guard and the assertion-rendering guard, and
about twenty PRE-EXISTING findings appeared that have nothing to do with this item. The
sweep moved to `test_properties.py`, which already declares its reach, and the two modules
kept their silence. The module-scope reach is declared there with its reason.

**One pin retired to symbol form.** `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-850.md` pointed at a
LINE NUMBER in `clockspeed/save/header.py` - the number is deliberately not restated here,
because writing it down again would be a live pointer at a tracked module and this record
would then have to be repaired every time that file is edited, which is the whole reason
the pin was retired. The line moved and its content carried over byte-identical
- verified against `HEAD` rather than taken on trust, because a slice reported two moved
pins as identical in session 79 and was wrong about one. A repoint was still refused by the
citation guard, correctly: a line pointer at a tracked Python module is invalidated by any
edit above it. It is now `clockspeed/save/header.py::read_header`, its grandfather entry is
gone, and `FORGIVEN_LINE_POINTER_CEILING` came down 64 -> 63 with it, because a ceiling
left with slack is that arm's own finding.

**How to verify independently.** `python -m pytest tests -q -n auto` - 6165 passed, 7
skipped, exit 0 at `4e8b13e`. `ruff check .` clean, `python -m mypy clockspeed` clean. To
re-derive the load-bearing claim, neutralise any single `del` in either module and run
`python -m pytest tests/save/test_world.py tests/save/test_header.py tests/save/test_chunks.py -q -p no:randomly`.

**WHAT THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF.** Every fixture is synthetic. No real save was parsed, so
this measures that no frame holds the PLANTED marker and infers the real case from the
fact that the same local holds the same file. The inference is sound and it is still an
inference.

### 2026-09-10 - CS-961 - MEASUREMENT RECORD. What the second pass costs. NOT A COMPLETION RECORD - CS-961's is above

**Relocated from `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-900.md` 2026-09-10**, because a
closed item's detail may not sit in a live leaf and this figure has no other owner:
`ARCHITECTURE.md` may not carry a count, and `CLAUDE.md` section 4 gives every
measured number exactly one home.

**THIS IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A BUDGET.** No threshold is proposed here and no
performance test was added, because no threshold is grounded yet. The planner
declined to name one and that still stands; what was missing was the number, not
the limit.

**THE METHOD, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE TWO CANDIDATE METHODS MEASURE DIFFERENT
THINGS.** The "before" figure was NOT obtained by checking out a pre-CS-961
`world.py`. It was obtained by timing the walk alone against the decode pass
alone, in one process, on one already-decompressed body: `_walk_body` called
directly, then `_decode_properties` called directly on the table it returned.
That measures the MARGINAL cost of the second pass over a body the first pass
already read. It does NOT measure the delta in `load_world_from_bytes` between
two revisions, and it credits the decode with nothing the walk got slower by. A
whole-load timing was taken alongside it as the cross-check, and the two agree:
walk plus decode reproduces the full load to within the run-to-run spread, which
says the header parse, the decompression, the usmap resolve, the unlock read and
the node extraction together cost almost nothing beside these two - the usmap is
cached by the time the timed runs begin.

**WHICH SAVE.** The largest reachable save BY RECORD COUNT, which is NOT the
largest by file size - a fact worth keeping, because picking by file size lands
on a smaller world. Its body decompresses to about 18.0 MB. Nothing about the
file, the world or the account is recorded here, per non-negotiables 3 and 11.

**FIVE RUNS EACH, AND THE SPREAD IS REPORTED RATHER THAN A MEAN.**

| Pass | Five runs, seconds | Spread |
|---|---|---|
| Whole `load_world_from_bytes` | 1.9745, 2.0035, 2.0074, 2.0143, 2.0091 | 0.040 s, about 2 percent |
| Walk alone (`_walk_body`) | 0.1994, 0.2078, 0.1918, 0.1934, 0.1838 | 0.024 s, about 12 percent |
| Decode alone (`_decode_properties`) | 1.8457, 1.8228, 1.8124, 1.8352, 1.8979 | 0.086 s, about 5 percent |

The spread is narrow enough that the ordering is not in doubt: **the decode pass
costs roughly nine to ten times the walk it follows, and is about nine tenths of
the whole load.** A load that took about a fifth of a second now takes about two
seconds. The walk figure carries the widest relative spread of the three and is
the one to re-measure before anything is built on it.

**COUNTS FROM THE SAME LOAD.** 25769 records walked; 25769 property entries, the
mapping being TOTAL over the record table by construction; **0 entries reported
`payload_read=False`**; 19721 entries carried at least one value, so 6048
decoded to an empty mapping without being flagged; 45347 top-level values in
all. Schema resolution split 7699 `True` against 18070 `False`, with 0 `None` -
a map was supplied, so the third state does not arise on this run.

**A DIFFERENT SAVE IN THE SAME LIBRARY REPORTED 3923 OF 3923 WITH
`payload_read=False`**, which is the (14,60) wall above showing up as a whole
world of unread payloads rather than as a refusal. It is recorded here only as
the contrast that makes the 0 above meaningful; it settles nothing about CS-G05.

**MEMORY, MEASURED BY DROP RATHER THAN BY SNAPSHOT DIFF.** Under `tracemalloc`,
holding the decode's result and then releasing it moved the traced total by
133321730, 133321722 and 133321714 bytes across three runs - about **133 MB
retained, and the three runs agree to within 16 bytes.** Traced peak during the
pass was 276814540 bytes, identical on all three. So the published model holds
roughly **7.4 times the size of the body it was decoded from**, and the pass
transiently touches about fifteen times it.

**WHERE THOSE BYTES GO, AND IT IS NOT SPREAD EVENLY.** The dominant site is the
`ContainerEntry` construction inside `clockspeed/save/world.py`'s
`_published_value`: about 1.08 million live instances holding about 103 MB, some
78 percent of everything retained. Those come from roughly six thousand
container-valued properties. **The eager-versus-lazy choice is not what costs
here - the container fan-out is**, and anything that wants this cheaper should
look at how a container publishes its elements before it looks at the pass that
builds them.

**WHAT THIS FIGURE DOES NOT COVER, AND THE LIST IS NOT SHORT.** One machine, one
library, one save, one Windows box with the game installed on it. It says
nothing about a second machine and nothing about a different world. **It says
nothing at all about CI**, where no install exists, every payload decodes with
no map, and the corpus is synthetic - so `resolved` is `None` there where it was
`True` or `False` here, and the container fan-out that dominates the memory
figure is whatever a hand-authored fixture happens to build. Do not carry any
number above into a CI expectation. It is also a measurement of the tree at the
CS-961 merge and of nothing after it.

### 2026-09-10 - CS-961 - CLOSED. A world load publishes decoded property values, and the item was REFUTED TWICE by one lens before it was true

**What shipped.** `WorldProperties` and `RecordProperties` are built during the walk
that already holds the bytes and are keyed BY RECORD INDEX, never by offset, which
is what the acceptance means by a stated model. `WorldModel.properties` is defaulted,
so the single construction site stayed the only edit. The payload dies with the walk:
no published type carries a `bytes` or `Path` field, and the frame is scrubbed on any
unwind. `resolved` is carried verbatim from CS-960 - three states, never flattened.
Merged files: `clockspeed/save/world.py`, `tests/save/synthetic.py`. Verified by
`tests/save/test_world.py::test_a_synthetic_world_publishes_one_decoded_property_value_end_to_end`,
`::test_the_two_determinate_resolved_states_are_both_reachable`,
`::test_no_body_byte_reaches_any_echo_path`,
`::test_no_published_world_type_annotates_a_carrier_field`,
`::test_a_published_container_keeps_every_element_without_its_position`,
`::test_no_published_property_value_carries_an_absolute_body_offset`,
`::test_no_clockspeed_frame_holds_the_raw_save_on_any_refusal_path` and
`tests/save/test_synthetic.py::test_the_decodable_payload_agrees_with_the_independent_encoder`.

**THE ACCEPTANCE COULD NOT BE WRITTEN WHEN IT WAS FILED, AND THAT WAS FOUND BY THE
PLANNER RATHER THAN BY A FAILING TEST.** It asked for one decoded value read end to
end from a SYNTHETIC world. Every levelled fixture built its payload as
`bytes(payload_size)` - zero bytes - and `synthetic.py` said so in its own prose:
payload content is opaque filler, and any slice decoding a field out of one is
decoding an invention. A fixture slice had to come first. **AN ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE CAN
NAME AN ARTEFACT THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and nothing catches that until someone tries to
write the arm.**

**THE COMMON-MODE RISK WAS MADE THE FIXTURE SLICE'S OWN ACCEPTANCE.** A slice that
authors both the payload encoder and the arm proving it decodes has measured its own
consistency and nothing else. So S0 had to reach byte equality against
`tests/save/test_properties.py`'s separately authored encoder, and did. The
independence was re-measured twice rather than inherited: that file is absent from
S0's diffstat, predates the base, and shares no import. An adversarial pass then found
the one input the check cannot see - the two encoders differ on the EMPTY STRING, one
writing a bare zero count and the other a count of one plus a null, neither measured.
Neither was declared right; the divergence was PINNED so a later arm cannot lose the
second opinion silently.

**REFUTED ON THE FIRST CUT, ON THE DEFECT THE ITEM EXISTS TO PREVENT.** A decoded
`ArrayProperty`, `SetProperty` or `MapProperty` is a `ContainerValue` whose elements
each carry an ABSOLUTE OFFSET INTO THE BODY - so the published model handed out
offsets into a buffer nobody holds, which is verbatim the defect CS-961 was filed to
abolish, while its own docstring claimed it never would. **Neither decodable fixture
produced a container, so no arm could have caught it: the fixture was built parallel
to the assumption rather than against it.** The repair publishes the type word, the
extent and the value with no position, recursively through struct interiors, and its
arm is a REFLEXIVE DEEP WALK rather than a list of known types, so a container type
added later is caught too.

**REFUTED ON THE SECOND CUT, ONE LEVEL DOWN, BY THE SAME LENS.** `load_world_from_bytes`
bound the raw save as a frame local, so a renderer showing locals printed the
plaintext options string. Scrubbing this layer's own frames was not enough:
`parse_header` and `decompress_body` bind the same blob in THEIR frames, and
`raise ... from exc` puts those in the rendered traceback. That half is pre-existing,
lives in two modules this item never scoped, and is FILED AS CS-963 rather than
absorbed - burying a non-negotiable 12 finding inside an unrelated merge is not a fix.
What changed here is the CLAIM: both sentences asserting no frame holds the raw save
now say what was measured, which is this layer's own frames only.

**THE SHAPE BEHIND BOTH REFUTATIONS, and it is the transferable part.** Each time, the
suite was green, a verifier had CONFIRMED, and the arm that should have caught the
defect was STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF FAILING FOR IT - the first because no fixture
produced the type, the second because the frame walker follows `__traceback__` and
never `__cause__`. **AN ORACLE THAT CANNOT SEE THE VALUE IT IS ASKED ABOUT RETURNS AN
EMPTY VERDICT ABOUT ITSELF, AND THAT VERDICT READS EXACTLY LIKE A PASS.** Only the
adversarial lens found either. Agreement among the other passes was not evidence.

**PINS: THREE REPOINTED, TWO RETIRED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE DIGEST.** A repoint is
honest only while the digest carries over unchanged, because that is the guard itself
proving the new line holds byte-identical content; three did and were re-checked
independently. The `STAGE_HEADER` raise did NOT - it gained an indent level when the
blob was scrubbed - so its line changed as well as moved, and re-cutting a digest from

retired to symbol form instead, and `FORGIVEN_LINE_POINTER_CEILING` came down 66 to 64
with them, because a ceiling left slack is that arm's own finding in the other
direction. **A SLICE REPORTED BOTH AS BYTE-IDENTICAL AND WAS WRONG ABOUT ONE**; the
merger checked rather than accepted, and a verifier re-derived the same conclusion.

**What this is NOT evidence for.** That real saves decode - the arms are synthetic
throughout. That any consumer exists; none does. That the wire stays safe once

ALIGNMENT, which `objects.py` states the synthetic corpus cannot corroborate - only
the real saves do. Byte equality between two independent encoders proves encoder
consistency, never that either matches the shipped format.

**Independently verified.** Three graders, none of which produced the work. Whole suite

### 2026-09-09 - CS-960 - CLOSED. The decode path accepts an absent property map, and the requirement it dropped was self-imposed by a docstring written when the function decoded nothing

**What shipped.** `objects.read_properties` and `objects.parse_properties` now take
`PropertyMap | None` and decode either way. `PropertyResult.resolved` becomes
`bool | None`: None means NO REGISTRY WAS SUPPLIED, and False keeps its only prior
meaning - a registry was supplied and does not model this class.
`WARN_UNRESOLVED_SCHEMA` is emitted only when a map was supplied, because with none
there is nothing to be unresolved against. That mirrors the position
`known_classes=None` already takes downstream, where no registry claims nothing.
Merged files: `clockspeed/save/objects.py`, `clockspeed/save/world.py`. Verified by
`tests/save/test_properties.py::test_a_decode_with_no_map_differs_from_the_mapped_one_in_nothing_but_resolution`,
`::test_resolution_reports_absent_unmodelled_and_modelled_as_three_distinct_states`,
`::test_no_unresolved_schema_warning_is_raised_when_no_map_was_supplied`,
`::test_a_zero_length_payload_reports_an_absent_map_the_same_way`,
`::test_no_clockspeed_frame_holds_the_body_when_the_extent_raises` and
`tests/save/test_objects.py::test_class_flagging_and_schema_resolution_answer_from_separate_inputs`.

**WHY IT WAS EVER MANDATORY, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART.** The docstring said
the parameter was non-optional because handling the no-install None was the world
layer's job - a LAYERING assertion, never a measurement. `git log -S` finds exactly
one commit introducing that signature, and at that commit the function DECODED
NOTHING: the schema lookup was its entire body, so the map was mandatory because
resolution WAS the function. Decoding was added later and the signature was never
revisited. **A PARAMETER'S NECESSITY IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE FUNCTION AS IT IS NOW,
NOT AS IT WAS WHEN THE PARAMETER WAS ADDED.** Until this closed, the project
decoded no property on CI or in any fresh clone, because `cached_usmap()` returns
None with no game install.

**THE PROOF IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A SAMPLE, and the adversary is what made it so.** An
arm over the fixtures its own authors chose is the weakest possible evidence for a
universal. The refutation pass traced the parameter to exactly FOUR executable
sites - one conditional expression, two privacy `del` statements and one
pass-through - and established that no helper below `read_properties` accepts a
map, and that there is no cache, module global or interned state. The value
therefore flows from one expression into the two exempt fields and nowhere else, so
NO PAYLOAD CAN DISTINGUISH the two decodes. The empirical half agreed: 23
hand-built payloads verified BY CENSUS to have reached the shapes claimed - nested
structs, arrays of structs, empty containers, sets, maps, enums, named and raw
`ByteProperty`, `TextProperty`, `SoftObjectProperty`, unknown type words, both
record kinds - plus 8000 fuzz payloads and every truncation prefix, each decoded
mapped-hit, mapped-miss and unmapped, in both orders and repeated. Zero differences
outside `resolved` and `warnings`. A NON-VACUITY CONTROL was run: putting `resolved`
back into the comparator reddens it immediately.

The change inserted nine lines above four cited declarations. Each pin moved to its
new number with its DIGEST UNCHANGED, so the guard itself proves the new line holds

**ONE DEEP-ARCHIVE POINTER MOVED BUCKET AND WAS NOT REPAIRED.** `_ROT_FORM` 14 to 13
and `_ROT_EMPTY` 3 to 4 are ONE pointer, not two findings - the same inversion
CS-921 recorded in the other direction, and pooled it would have moved no total at

so its citation was right when written and the module moved underneath it. That is
rot by construction, which is the stated exemption; editing the archive to repair it

### 2026-09-09 - LICENCE GATE RESULT for the save-parser field, and a refuted premise this project had been building on. NOT A COMPLETION RECORD

**Nothing closed. This is a gate verdict plus a measured correction**, recorded before
anything acts on it, the way CS-485's wiki verdict was. Two researchers worked
independently from different starting points and converged.

**THE REFUTED PREMISE.** This project has treated a `.usmap` mappings file as a
precondition for decoding a save's property payloads - `read_properties` takes a
non-optional `PropertyMap`, `cached_usmap()` returns None with no install, and the
world layer therefore steps over roughly three quarters of every save body. That
premise is a CATEGORY ERROR. Satisfactory saves use Unreal's TAGGED property
serialization: every property carries its own name, type word, size and inner-type
metadata inline, so the payload is self-describing. A mappings file is required for
UNVERSIONED serialization and for reading COOKED ASSETS out of the `.pak`, which is a
different job - it is why `FactoryGame.usmap` ships in the install for asset tooling.
Three independent implementations were read and all three walk the tag stream with no
mappings file anywhere in the path. AN IN-TREE PROBE IS THE ONLY THING THAT SETTLES IT
FOR THIS CODEBASE and it is what a later session must read before relying on this
paragraph - an external agent's reading is a hypothesis, not a measurement of our tree.

**THE OTHER BLOCKER IS REAL AND IS OURS.** `WorldModel` carries no body bytes, so a
record's `body_offset` points into a buffer nobody kept. Every tool examined decodes
properties DURING the object walk and hands the caller decoded values rather than
offsets into a dropped buffer. That is architecture, not format, and no external
knowledge is needed to change it.

**A TESTABLE CAUSE FOR THE (header 14, save 60) WALL**, where this project's tag walk
reaches a terminator on ZERO payloads. Recent Unreal versions replace the tag's inline
inner-type strings with a type-name TREE - name, then a tree of nodes, then size, then a
flags byte, with the array index and the guid present only when their flag bits are set.
The discriminator is a per-OBJECT UE5 file version carried in the object's own version
data for save versions at or above 53, NOT a field in the file header. A decoder that
never parses that structure cannot select the right layout at all, and would mis-parse
at the first property of every object - which is exactly the observed failure. Two
sources give the gating constant as 1011 and 1012 and DISAGREE; neither number is to be
hardcoded from a citation. Probe it against the operator's own save.

**GATE VERDICTS.** `CONVENTIONS.md` section 14, all five traps checked per candidate.

- **REFUSED - GPL-3.0, copyleft, do not vendor regardless of any verbal clearance:**
  `moritz-h/satisfactory-3d-map` (and its PyPI `satisfactory-save`),
  `GreyHak/sat_sav_parse`, `PhysoxNB/SatisFacts`. Vendoring any of them would relicense
  this project, which is MIT. For two of the three no author copyright line was observed
  at all, so trap 2 is OPEN and the grantor is not established.
- **REFUSED - source-available, not open source:** `AnthorNet/SC-InteractiveMap`, the
  parser behind the interactive map the operator named. No LICENSE file, `private: true`
  in its manifest, and a README stating reuse of the source and data assets is not
  permitted in any case. Its bundled game-data API is doubly refused, by that README and
  by the standing no-lifted-datasets decision. Its own site terms could not be read - the
  domain returned 403 - so that leg is UNRESOLVED, which doctrine treats as refused.
- **CLEARED WITH A CONDITION - MIT:** `etothepii4/satisfactory-file-parser`. Full
  permission and warranty text in both the licence file and the manifest, single named
  holder, no NOTICE and no undeclared upstreams found. THE CONDITION: it is TypeScript,
  so the realistic use is READING it. A file-for-file port is a TRANSLATION and therefore
  a derivative work - it is not a reimplementation and must not be called one. Vendoring
  is cleared only if it is ever consumed as-is, with the copyright line reproduced.

  entry is. One nuance worth keeping: the best format document in the field sits INSIDE a
  GPL-licensed repository, so its PROSE AND TABLE LAYOUT are licensed accordingly even
  though the facts it states are not.

**THE DISTINCTION THAT GOVERNS WHAT HAPPENS NEXT, stated so it is not re-litigated.** A
file format is an interface and a set of facts. "The tag is a name, then a type-name
tree, then a size, then a flags byte" is a protocol fact. So is "clock speed is stored in
`mCurrentPotential`" - a property name is the GAME's identifier, not any parser author's
creation. Learning those by reading and then writing an original decoder is not
derivation of anyone's code. What IS protected is source text, file and function
organisation, comments, and a document's prose. So: external sources are HYPOTHESIS
GENERATORS ONLY; every hypothesis is confirmed against LOCAL BYTES - the operator's own
save and the shipped install, both lawful runtime inputs this project already reads and
never commits - and every confirmed fact is recorded in this project's own words beside
the probe that confirmed it. Never transcribe a table, never mirror a decomposition.

**THE ONE THING THAT IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE TAG STREAM ALONE**, and it is small: map
and set ELEMENT interiors carry no type information, so a table keyed by parent class
path plus property name is required. Build it by observation from local saves, one
verifiable entry at a time. Do NOT copy any existing project's table - one of them is
explicitly refused above, and such a table is authored judgement about game content,
which is closer to a dataset than to a format fact.

**NO EXTERNAL GATE BLOCKS THIS PROJECT.** Nothing the field's map tools display comes
from information this project cannot legitimately obtain. The format is self-describing,
the version discriminator is inside the file, and the reference world is on this machine.

### 2026-09-08 - CS-954 - FROZEN-FILE GRANT, recorded BEFORE the edit per CLAUDE.md section 6

**This is a grant record, not a completion record.** It authorizes ONE edit to
`.githooks/pre-push`, which CLAUDE.md section 6 freezes. An adjudicator that
neither proposed the change nor wrote the hook, the item note or the
reproductions ruled GRANTED WITH CONDITIONS. The closing record is separate.

**THE CANDIDATE IS PINNED.** HEAD `c9474bd1b8021c6e827e8dae34acb150d8ff085e`,
`.githooks/pre-push` at sha256
`485bc24c3536d9d853f1659e4c8d0456962797888eb76c0452f3a000062c62c8`.

**WHAT IS AUTHORIZED, and nothing else:** two additive regions and their comment
block - a stdin capture placed BEFORE the interpreter ladder, and a ref re-read
placed AFTER the pytest status is taken. Everything else survives byte-identical:
the CS-703 probe block and its rationale, the interpreter ladder, the pytest
importability check, the entire CS-906 invocation block and its comments, the
exit-5 guard and the exit path. The grant is SINGLE-USE and expires on
application. It covers no other frozen path, and it does NOT cover the standing
trailer-range-scan proposal against this same file, which CS-906's grant already
ruled needs its own.

**WHY.** The hook has never read its stdin - every redirect in it is
`</dev/null`, and nothing consumes the ref list git supplies - so it grades the
WORKING TREE and never learns which commits are being pushed. A gate that can
report on a commit that never ships and stay silent about one that does is the
CS-821 and CS-824 family one level up.

**THE INCIDENT IS MEASURED, AND THE FORGE SETTLES IT.** `git reflog show
refs/remotes/origin/main` records `update by push` to `5192aaf` at 2026-09-07
18:28:04 -0500, while the local reflog records `1ee8b64` committed at 18:27:44
-0500 - inside that push. `gh run list --commit` on the FULL 40-character SHA of
`5192aaf` returns empty: no CI run has ever existed for the commit the hook
graded. Exactly one push-event run exists for `1ee8b64`, created 23:28:07Z,
three seconds after the ref update. One push event, and its tip was never graded.

**STRONGER THAN FILED, and found by the adjudicator rather than by the proposer:
git's own ref-update report disagreed with what shipped.** The tracking reflog
named `5192aaf` while CI and the later fetch fast-forward both show the remote
took `1ee8b64`. Git's reporting path and its shipping path already disagreed once
in this incident.

**THE MECHANISM REMAINS UNESTABLISHED AND IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN AS THOUGH IT WERE.**
Two controlled reproductions on 2026-09-08 - one over a plain local path, one
over `file://` - advanced the local ref mid-hook and BOTH shipped exactly the SHA
the hook was handed, with a control proving the ref really had moved by the time
the hook returned. The real incident used HTTPS to the forge and the difference
is unexplained. **The authorized change is therefore MECHANISM-AGNOSTIC:** it
grades the hook's own refusal, never git's transport. Whichever half is true, the
outcome is safe - either git ships the graded SHA and the check never fires, or
it ships a later one and the push is blocked before it can.

**WHY NOT A NON-FROZEN ROUTE.** Ruled on and rejected, each for a measured
reason. A CI-side check cannot block a push and grades only the tip. A wrapper
script is bypassed by the bare `git push` that caused the incident, and CLAUDE.md
2.2 makes the hooks authoritative and everything else a convenience layer. A
second hook does not exist as a git concept - `scripts/install_hooks.py` names
exactly three hooks and there is no `.d` chaining - so dispatching to one is
itself a frozen-file edit, and a worse one whose absence fails open. The
operator discipline the item already records cannot bind `ops/loop/queue_loop.py`,
which commits autonomously with no operator in the loop, and the window is a
function of suite duration and so grows monotonically.

**THE FIFTEEN CONDITIONS BIND THE GRANT.** Recorded here in full so the edit can
be graded against them by someone who was not present:

1. This record is committed BEFORE the commit that edits the hook.
2. Scope is the two regions and their comment block; everything else byte-identical.
3. Stdin is read EXACTLY ONCE, into a variable, before the ladder runs.
4. The re-read runs ONLY when the pytest status is 0. It never rewrites, masks or
   clobbers a non-zero status - a red suite still reports as a red suite.
5. A zero-SHA or delete ref is SKIPPED, not refused. Nothing was graded and
   nothing ships.
6. Any other mismatch or unresolvable local ref REFUSES, naming the ref, the
   handed SHA and the observed SHA.
7. NEVER echo the remote URL or any raw stdin line. An HTTPS remote can carry an
   embedded credential and a local remote carries a home path - non-negotiables 3
   and 12, the same reason the hook already refuses to echo its interpreter
   variable.
8. Every new variable is initialised before first use, including on the failure
   path that renders it. `set -u` precedent: the probe's own two initialisations.
9. Empty stdin is LOUD on stderr and does NOT refuse, with its own arm, so a
   no-op is distinguishable from a check that never ran.
10. The comment block states plainly that this NARROWS the window to the
    hook-exit-to-git-resolve gap and does NOT close it, and that the mechanism
    remains unestablished. No claim of closure anywhere.
11. An end-to-end arm drives a REAL push to a throwaway bare remote with the
    local ref advanced during the hook, asserting non-zero exit AND that the
    later commit did not land. RED demonstrated first. A paired arm asserts a
    clean push still succeeds when the ref does not move.
12. Every existing arm that runs the real hook bytes gets explicit stdin, and one
    arm asserts the hook does not block on a closed or empty stdin.
13. `python scripts/install_hooks.py` runs clean after the edit; every added byte
    is 7-bit ASCII, LF, no BOM.
14. A byte-identical file is a legitimate outcome. If a mechanism is later
    established under which the check cannot fire, the grant is spent unused and
    that is the finding.
15. Single-use, expires on application, covers no other frozen path.

**THE COMMON-MODE RISK IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DISCHARGED.** Both reproductions
and the authorized check read the LOCAL REF as the authority on what ships. Any
mechanism where the shipped SHA comes from somewhere else - a packed-refs versus
loose-ref disagreement, or a resolution inside the HTTPS remote helper that never
touches the loose ref - defeats the check silently, and neither the reproduction
nor the check tests it. It would have fired on THIS incident, because the local
ref genuinely moved. This is a coverage gap, not a defect in the proposal.

**WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE RESIDUAL.** `GIT_TRACE_PACKET=1` with `GIT_TRACE=1` on a
real HTTPS push whose ref is advanced mid-hook, capturing the update command
actually sent. Until that exists, condition 10 governs what may be written down.
