### 2026-09-07 - CS-949, CS-950 - the watcher now reports what LEFT the channel, and records that it ran at all - two holes the cross-project sync measured in this tree

**CS-949 - a withdrawal is reported.** Before this, a key that left the inbox
dropped silently out of the seen store on the next acknowledgement. The channel
proved the cost the same day: a sibling delivered a payload to five inboxes,
withdrew it after a personal-data finding, and then cited it twice more in later
notes. No watcher anywhere said the bytes had gone, and this tree could not tell
"never delivered" from "delivered then pulled" from the inside. The answer had
to be supplied by two other repositories reading their own disks.

Merged file: `tools/inbox_watch.py` - `withdrawn_items`, `_key_parts`, and a
`render` that no longer returns early when the only finding is a withdrawal.

Verified by 9 arms in `tests/test_inbox_watch.py`, of which two carry the
design:

- `::test_a_withdrawal_stops_being_reported_once_acknowledged` - the harder
  half, and it is LL's, not this project's. An acceptance criterion that only
  proves a withdrawal APPEARS is not the same criterion as one proving it can be
  acknowledged AWAY, and a report that cannot be discharged is a permanent
  banner - a worse outcome than the silence it replaced.
- `::test_an_edited_note_is_not_reported_as_withdrawn` - matching a stored key
  against the whole present key set is the obvious implementation and it reports
  every EDITED note as withdrawn. A false withdrawal in the one report whose
  entire value is telling a real absence from a delivery that never happened.
  **MUTATION-VERIFIED**: pristine floor 44 passed, the name-match mutated back to
  a whole-key match, the mutation asserted to have landed before running, the
  arm KILLED it, and the file restored from a byte snapshot rather than from git.

Matching on the NAME rather than the key is deliberate and costs something: a
RENAME still surfaces as a withdrawal, because from the inbox's point of view
the old name did leave. That cost is accepted, consistent with
`::test_a_renamed_note_resurfaces_and_that_cost_is_accepted`.

**CS-950 - the invocation log, and a correction to a property this project
published.** Clockspeed has been reporting `/clear` survival as UNVERIFIED and
argued by construction, as have four sibling repositories. Measured this
session: `tools/inbox_watch.py` read no hook payload and wrote no record of
having been invoked, so a firing left nothing behind at all. The status was not
UNVERIFIED, it was **UNMEASURABLE**, and that is a strictly worse claim than the
one this project had been publishing on the channel.

The general defect is the one LL named first about a Task Scheduler trigger and
then declined to draw a conclusion from: a REGISTRATION is not a BEHAVIOUR. All
five repositories were reading their own hook CONFIGURATION and calling it
argued by construction.

Merged file: `tools/inbox_watch.py` - `hook_source`, `read_hook_payload`,
`append_invocation`, a `--source` flag, and both `main` branches wired to it.
One line per run at `data/inbox_watch_invocations.log`, gitignored.

Verified by 10 arms in `tests/test_inbox_watch.py`, of which three carry a
reason:

- `::test_an_ack_is_distinguishable_from_a_listing` - a log proving that
  something ran and nothing about what is the same dead end as no log.
- `::test_a_hostile_source_cannot_forge_a_log_line` - the payload is external
  input landing in a log a human reads, and a newline in it forges an entry.
- `::test_a_log_that_cannot_be_written_does_not_break_the_watcher` - an
  instrument that can take the thing it measures offline is worse than none.

`read_hook_payload` reads stdin on a DAEMON thread with a bounded join, because
stdin from a terminal never reaches EOF and a plain read would hang until the
15 second hook timeout killed the process. A killed hook surfaces nothing, which
is the same outcome a directory junction already cost this channel once.

**MEASURED END TO END, not just under pytest.** Piping
`{"hook_event_name":"SessionStart","source":"clear"}` produced
`mode=list source=clear`, and `source=startup` produced `source=startup`. A bare
terminal run produced `source=unknown` in 0.139s.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO.** It does not measure `/clear` survival. It makes the
measurement POSSIBLE - clear once, read the file - and the first real firing is
the measurement. Until an operator does that, the property stays UNVERIFIED here
and this entry claims nothing else.

**Also confirmed, not built:** the junction and both-false walker holes reported
to the channel are already fixed in this tree - reparse-point pruning at
`tools/inbox_watch.py:_is_reparse_point`, a pruned `iterdir` walk, a per-payload
budget, and every undigestable entry FORCED into every report with its reason.
Two siblings still have the junction hole open.

### 2026-09-07 - CS-940, CS-934 - the inbox watcher keys on CONTENT, sees the WHOLE channel, and refuses to be silent about what it cannot digest; both items were REFUTED once before they closed

**What shipped.** `tools/inbox_watch.py` was rewritten. The seen key is the pair
of NAME and CONTENT DIGEST, separated from the DISPLAY, so an in-place
correction surfaces and the report stays a list of names. A deliverable is now
any of four things - a top-level note, a top-level file of any other kind, a
subdirectory payload digested as one unit from the files on this disk, or an
entry the tool cannot classify. Merged files: `tools/inbox_watch.py`,
`tests/test_inbox_watch.py`. Verified by 34 arms in `tests/test_inbox_watch.py`,
among them `::test_an_edit_that_restores_the_timestamp_still_resurfaces`,
`::test_a_payload_changed_at_constant_length_and_count_resurfaces`,
`::test_no_window_of_payload_content_reaches_the_report`,
`::test_an_unreadable_file_is_reported_on_every_run` and
`::test_an_entry_that_is_neither_a_file_nor_a_directory_is_still_accounted_for`.

**THE ONE-TIME RE-BASELINE, recorded here rather than only in the module.** The
store previously held bare filenames, which match no key under the new scheme,
so the first session after this change reports every item in the inbox as unread
exactly once. That is correct and is not a bug. An adversary's finding is the
reason this paragraph exists: a re-baseline recorded only inside the artifact
that causes it is not a record anybody reads in time.

**THE INVERTED PARAGRAPH IS DELETED, NOT REWORDED.** The module had argued that
keying on a content hash would make an EDITED note read as already seen. An edit
changes the content, so it changes the hash - a content key is what SURFACES the
edit and the name key is what hid it. The false premise was doing the work of a
design rationale, which is why it survived review and why it was quoted onward
to four sibling projects before a probe refuted it. RC replied with the useful
refinement: delete is right for an INVERTED rationale, while a rationale that is
merely stale in its description should be corrected with its true part kept.

**REFUTED TWICE BEFORE IT CLOSED, by two read-only adversaries that wrote none
of it, against a candidate frozen at a digest.** Neither verdict was a style
note. The acceptance-and-vacuity lens returned REFUTED on both items with two
surviving mutants; the correctness-and-hostile-input lens returned REFUTED on
the claim that the tool was safe to run against untrusted sibling payloads, with
four inputs that made a deliverable report ZERO times.

**THE TWO MUTANTS, AND WHY THE FIRST SUITE COULD NOT SEE THEM.** Replacing the
content digest with `st_mtime_ns` passed all 22 arms. Replacing the payload file
digest with `st_size` passed all 22 arms. The reason is general and was sent to
every project on this channel: AN ARM THAT VARIES CONTENT VARIES MTIME, SIZE AND
CONTENT AT ONCE, SO IT PINS NONE OF THEM. The content leg is now pinned by an
arm that edits a note and RESTORES its timestamp, and by two that change content
at CONSTANT BYTE LENGTH. Both mutants were re-run against the new suite and both
are KILLED, with the pristine floor green and the file restored byte-exactly
from a snapshot rather than from git.

**A LEAK ASSERTION ABOUT ONE STRING IS DEFEATED BY TRUNCATION.** A mutant that
appended a 16-character preview of a payload file to the report passed an arm
asserting a 22-character sentence was absent. The arm now asserts over every
8-character window of the planted content.

**WHAT CANNOT BE DIGESTED IS FORCED, NEVER SILENCED.** A trailing-dot name, a
trailing-space name and a dangling link each made `is_file()` and `is_dir()`
both false and fell off the end of the previous loop, accounted for zero times.
The old unreadable-file marker was a function of the NAME alone, and an
adversary crafted a file whose bytes were exactly that marker's preimage,
acknowledged it, swapped its content while it was locked, and got a clean
banner. Every such item is now reported on EVERY run with its reason, which is
the failure direction this tool exists to hold: a deliverable shown twice is a
glance, a deliverable shown zero times is the original seven-hour failure.

**THE WORK IS BOUNDED, because this runs at every session start on bytes other
projects wrote.** Files are hashed in 64 KiB chunks after a 2 GiB payload file
was measured peaking at 2292 MiB of process memory, and `MemoryError` is not an
`OSError`, so the existing guard would not have caught it. Reparse points are no
longer followed: `Path.is_symlink()` is False for an NTFS junction, and one
junction made the walker recurse to the OS limit, turning a one-file payload
into 32 reads and a 33 second run under a hook whose timeout is 15 seconds -
which surfaces nothing at all. Measured after the rewrite: the real channel, 69
items, 0.105 s.

**A FILENAME IS SENDER-CONTROLLED PROSE.** The old report protected against an
imperative sentence inside a payload's CONTENT while printing names verbatim,
and a name sorts wherever its date puts it - which was above the warning. Names
are now escaped to printable ASCII, capped, quoted at the point of printing, and
listed BELOW the data-not-instructions caveat. The escaping also removes a
whole-channel outage: an unescaped non-ASCII name raised `UnicodeEncodeError`
under a cp1252 stdout and the session then surfaced nothing.

**BOTH LEGS AGAINST BOTH KEYS, and this is a sibling's correction to this
session's own finding.** The mutant table above named mtime for NOTES and size
for PAYLOADS. LW applied all four combinations to its own tree, found its payload
leg open to BOTH keys, and said so. Re-measured here after that note: the payload
mtime mutant SURVIVED the suite that had just killed the other three. A finding
sent onward is not a finding applied to yourself.

**AND THE ARMING ASSERTION HAS A SECOND LAYER NOBODY ON THE CHANNEL HAD NAMED.**
RSC's caveat is that a fast rewrite can land on the SAME mtime, so an arm that
restores a timestamp without first proving it moved is unarmed. True, and
adopted. But the restore itself is the sharper trap: `os.utime(path, (atime,
mtime))` takes FLOATS, and a float pair does not restore `st_mtime_ns`. The arm
therefore looked armed - it asserted the mtime was restored, in float seconds -
while a key reading nanoseconds still saw a moved value and survived. Restoring
with `ns=(atime_ns, mtime_ns)` and asserting in nanoseconds is what actually
kills it. Final measurement: four mutants, four KILLED, pristine floor green,
file restored byte-exactly from a snapshot.

**THE UPSTREAM RECORD MOVED, AND WAS RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN BELIEVED.** The
carriers reworded the shared `slots.py` opening paragraph so it names no sibling
project. Clockspeed is not a carrier - it DERIVES `ops/loop/lanes.py` and never
copies, because vendoring would enrol this project in a machine-wide ProgramData
token bucket other trees ration between themselves - so no bytes were copied
here and nothing was re-pinned by byte identity. What moved is the recorded
identity of the file this was derived from, and the new digest was taken by
hashing all three carrier working copies ON THIS DISK, not from the note that
announced it. The change is prose only: five consecutive docstring lines and
nothing else, verified against the carrier's own history.

**Two items opened by this work.** CS-941, the watcher is silent on a
WITHDRAWAL, measured here after RC asked the channel. CS-942, `SessionStart`
fires once, measured in this session when two notes arrived mid-run and neither

### 2026-09-06 - CS-932 - CLOSED. The inbox has a watcher, and the two design points came from the two siblings that had already got them wrong once

Nothing watched `moon_sync_inbox/`. Measured this session: a note sat unread for
about seven hours, and the general case was unbounded because nothing bounded
it. Notes were read only because the operator's continuation prompt said to.

**THE DESIGN IS NOT THIS PROJECT'S.** Two sibling projects converged on it
independently and sent it through the channel the tool now watches. Both points
are reproduced in the module WITH their reasons, because a conclusion inherited
without its reason comes back:
1. Surface at SESSION START, not from a daemon: one directory listing, no
   console flash, and it survives a `/clear` by construction because a `/clear`
   IS a session start.
2. Track SEEN FILENAMES AS A SET, never an mtime watermark. A watermark advances
   on write, so it can move past a note nobody read. Both siblings built a
   watermark first and dropped it for exactly this.

**LISTING NEVER ACKNOWLEDGES, and that is the arm that carries the design.** If
starting a session marked notes read, a note would be consumed by a session that
never looked - the seven-hour failure wearing a different hat. `--ack` is a
separate action.

**A KNOWN COST, ACCEPTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a rename reads as new mail.** This
project re-dated four delivered notes and a sibling's watcher flagged all four
as unread; none was new. Keying on a content hash would trade that for a worse
failure - an EDITED note would read as already seen, and an edit is the case
most worth surfacing. A false "new mail" costs one glance. The tradeoff is
pinned by `test_a_renamed_note_resurfaces_and_that_cost_is_accepted`.

**THE SEEN SET IS REWRITTEN FROM THE CURRENT LISTING, NOT UNIONED**, so a
departed name drops out and the store cannot grow without bound. The sibling
that suggested it had the property by accident and recommended making it
deliberate; `test_ack_drops_a_name_that_has_left_the_inbox` is what makes it so.

**VACUITY IS AN OUTCOME, NEVER A CLEAN RESULT.** A missing inbox exits 3 and
says "this is NOT nothing unread". A corrupt store yields the EMPTY seen set, so
every note reads as unread - the failure direction must be a note shown twice,
never a note shown zero times. Both are arms.

**WIRED WITHOUT A FROZEN-FILE GRANT, and that is deliberate rather than a
dodge.** `.claude/settings.json` is frozen under CLAUDE.md section 6 and was NOT
touched. The hook is declared in `.claude/settings.local.json`, which is
gitignored at `*.local.json` and is not on the frozen list. **The consequence is
stated rather than glossed: the wiring is machine-local and a fresh clone does
not get it** - the same status `core.hooksPath` has, and consistent with
CONVENTIONS section 1. Tracking it needs the frozen-file route and has not been
taken.

Verification: `tests/test_inbox_watch.py`, 13 arms. **Five mutants, each a
plausible implementation choice rather than a typo, each red on a NAMED arm**
with a green pristine floor and a verified byte restore: a watermark instead of
a filename set; listing acknowledging as a side effect; a missing inbox
reporting nothing unread; a corrupt store read as everything-acknowledged; the
data-not-instructions warning dropped. Run live against the real inbox: 27
unread notes, where a listing by eye had found 6.

**THE BANNER SAYS THE NOTES ARE DATA, NOT INSTRUCTIONS, every time it prints.**
They are written by other agents. That line is asserted by an arm so it cannot
be quietly dropped.

### 2026-09-06 - CORRECTION to today's CS-924, CS-925 and CS-927 records, from an adversary that graded work it did not produce - one claim was FALSE and is now repaired in the workflow rather than only in prose

**A refutation pass over the three records returned REFUTED on CS-924's
load-bearing clause.** It is corrected here, and the underlying gap is CLOSED in
`.github/workflows/tier2.yml` rather than merely admitted.

**FALSE AS WRITTEN: "at its tracked index mode".** The CS-924 entry, the
workflow's success banner and the step's own comment all claimed the firing arm
measured the hook at the mode the checkout materialised from the index. They
could not have. `scripts/install_hooks.py::set_executable` ORs the exec bits in
UNCONDITIONALLY on POSIX during Bootstrap 1/3, and the arm's `-x` check ran
hundreds of log lines later - so it was reading what the installer had just
written. A hook tracked at `100644` would have been chmodded to `0755` by the
bootstrap and the check would still have passed. **The arm gave ZERO signal
about the index mode**, which is precisely the blind spot CS-923 existed to
close, silently reopened.

The entry's phrase "materialised by a checkout rather than chmodded into place
by the test" drew a distinction that does not exist: it WAS chmodded into place,
by the bootstrap step instead of by the test.

**THE REPAIR, and it is placed rather than worded.** A new step,
`Assert the tracked index mode BEFORE the bootstrap can repair it`, runs
immediately after the clone and before Bootstrap 1/3. It reads `git ls-files -s`
for ALL THREE hooks and requires `100755`, then - on POSIX only - requires each
to have materialised executable. Its position is load-bearing and its comment
says so.

**THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE THE ADVERSARY NAMED WAS THEN EXECUTED**, which it could
not do for want of a POSIX host. `git update-index --chmod=-x .githooks/pre-commit`
against a fresh clone, running the step extracted from the YAML under GitHub's
exact shell: `100755` exits 0, `100644` exits 1 naming the hook. The index-mode
half is testable on Windows because an index mode lives in git rather than on
the filesystem, so this measurement did not need a runner.

**SCOPE, CORRECTED.** The old banner said "a Clockspeed hook". Only `pre-commit`
is armed end to end. `commit-msg` runs during those commits but purely as a
pass-through - a non-executable `commit-msg` is INVISIBLE to that arm, because
git would skip it silently and the commit would still land. `pre-push` is never
invoked in that job at all. The new pre-bootstrap step covers all three for
MODE; the FIRING claim remains about `pre-commit` alone and now says so in the
banner itself.

**AN ATTRIBUTION GAP, ALSO CLOSED.** The refusal check accepted any
`precommit_gate: BLOCKED`, and its alternative `clockspeed pre-commit` matches
EVERY `die()` in the hook - including "gate not found", "no usable python
interpreter found" and "the gate DID NOT RUN". So a dead character-set check
plus any other blocking finding would have read as success. The arm now requires
the `CHARSET non-ASCII character` diagnostic by name, tying the refusal to the
violation the step actually staged.

**FALSE IN THE CS-925 RECORD: "no test module covered that script at all".**
`git grep set_executable -- tests/` returning zero hits is true; the conclusion
drawn from it is not. `tests/test_exception_rendering.py` copies
`scripts/install_hooks.py` into a sandbox and RUNS IT AS A SUBPROCESS, so on

more interesting statement is narrower: the script was covered and the function
was executed - only its RESULT was never read back. "Uncovered" and "ungraded"
are different defects and this record confused them.

**CS-925's residual is DISCHARGED.** tier1 run `34080228403` at `3d36050` on
ubuntu reported `4317 passed, 24 skipped` with NO skip from
`tests/test_install_hooks.py`, against `4281 passed, 24 skipped` before. Both

**CS-925, narrower than its prose:** 2 of its 4 arms are graded on a chmod CALL

identical violation must LAND under `--no-verify`, which is what attributes the
refusal to the HOOK LAYER rather than to the content.

by an assertion, which is precisely why control 1 exists.

into the workflow would violate CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 4 and tier1's own

### 2026-09-06 - CS-925 - CLOSED. The exec bit `set_executable` lands is now asserted on disk, not the fact that it was called

`scripts/install_hooks.py::set_executable` was the only thing repairing a hook's
POSIX exec bit per clone and NOTHING graded it: `git grep set_executable --
tests/` returned zero hits and no module covered that script at all. Its POSIX
branch never runs on the operator's Windows machine, where it returns
`n/a on windows`. This is the CS-605 shape exactly - a permission bit set by
code whose RESULT no assertion reads back.

**THE ARM ASSERTS THE MODE ON DISK.** A test that mocked `os.chmod` and checked
its arguments would restate the implementation and fail this acceptance, because
that is what CS-605 closed on.

**THE SKIP IS GATED ON A MEASURED FILESYSTEM FACT, NOT A PLATFORM NAME** -
the pattern already established by `tests/test_make_cert.py` for CS-605: write a
throwaway file, chmod it, read the mode back, gate on the result. Branching on
`os.name` would freeze today's answer into the suite as though it were
permanent. **The probe never calls `set_executable`**, so no defect in the
function can mute the arm that grades it.

**DISCRIMINATION: 8 mutants, all RED as expected**, installed by rebinding on
the loaded module and never on disk - never chmods; owner bit only; clobbers the
rw bits; wrong report string; unconditional chmod breaking idempotence; the nt
branch faking the bit; the nt branch claiming `executable`; a refused chmod
swallowed. A pristine floor ran green before each. The nt arms count chmod CALLS
rather than comparing modes, because on Windows a faked bit and no bit read back
identically.

**FROZEN FILE UNTOUCHED AND PROVEN SO.** `scripts/install_hooks.py` is
byte-identical to HEAD, confirmed by hash rather than by inspection. No grant was
needed because the arm lives in `tests/`.

Verification: `tests/test_install_hooks.py`, four arms. On Windows:
`2 passed, 2 skipped`, the skips naming the measured filesystem reason.

**UNVERIFIED AND SAID SO:** at the time of writing, the two exec-bit arms had
never run against a real POSIX kernel - there is no WSL distribution and no
docker on this box, so the discrimination harness used an in-process stand-in for
a mode-honouring filesystem. That proves the assertions discriminate; it does not
prove behaviour against a POSIX filesystem. The first real measurement is CI.

### 2026-09-06 - CS-923 - FROZEN-FILE GRANT, recorded BEFORE the edit. The three tracked hooks were mode 100644, so the tier-0 gate is one `git pull` away from silently not firing on any POSIX clone

**FROZEN-FILE GRANT under `CLAUDE.md` section 6.** `.githooks/*` is frozen. The
proposal was routed to an adjudicator that did not produce it, the operator approved
the verdict, and this record is written BEFORE the edit as section 6 requires.

**SCOPE GRANTED, and nothing wider.** `git update-index --chmod=+x` on
`.githooks/pre-commit`, `.githooks/commit-msg` and `.githooks/pre-push`. **No byte of
hook content changes.** The three blob SHAs `b7a4cd0`, `e12e087` and `4b3a567` are
identical after the flip, and that identity is the mechanical proof the scope held.
`scripts/install_hooks.py` is separately frozen and is NOT covered by this grant.

**What was measured.** `git ls-files -s .githooks/` returned all three at `100644`.
Git refuses to run a non-executable hook on POSIX and reports NOTHING when it
declines - no warning, no non-zero exit, no log line - so a gate that has stopped
firing is indistinguishable from one that fires and finds nothing.

**THE HOLE IS NARROWER THAN THE SIBLING'S, AND THE FIRST FRAMING OF IT WAS WRONG.**
A clone that never runs the bootstrap is NOT a mode hole: `core.hooksPath` is unset
there, so `.githooks/` is never consulted at all. `scripts/install_hooks.py::set_executable`
chmods +x on POSIX, so a bootstrapped clone is repaired. The residual is later-arriving
and specific: a BOOTSTRAPPED POSIX clone that then runs `git pull`, `checkout`, `merge`
or `reset --hard` over a REWRITTEN hook file gets it materialised at the INDEX mode,
which destroys the exec bit the bootstrap set, while `core.hooksPath` stays set. The
trigger is live rather than theoretical - `.githooks/` carries 7 commits, three of them
on 2026-09-06 under CS-906.

**WINDOWS IS UNAFFECTED, MEASURED BOTH WAYS RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** On git
2.53.0.windows.3 with `core.filemode=false`, a hook at index mode 100644 FIRED and
blocked the commit, and repeating at 100755 behaved identically. Git for Windows masks
`X_OK`. That is also precisely why this defect is invisible from the operator's machine
and had to be found from a sibling's incident record.

**NOTHING IN THE TREE GRADED THE MODE.** A repo-wide search over tracked files for
`100755`, `100644`, `ls-files -s`, `update-index` and `core.filemode` returned ZERO
hits, so no guard turns red on the flip and no guard would have caught it.
**This repo has already paid for this exact shape once.** CS-605 found
`scripts/make_cert.py` chmodding a key to 0600 with nothing grading the result, and
recorded it as "no test in the tree asserted the resulting mode - so no CI run could
ever have revealed it, because there was nothing to fail." A different file, the same
defect: a permission bit set by code that no assertion reads back.

**THE AGGRAVATING FACT: the mitigation itself is ungraded.** `git grep set_executable
-- tests/` returns zero hits and no test module covers that script at all. Its POSIX
branch never executes on the operator's machine - it returns
"n/a on windows" there - so the one function standing between this repo and the sibling's
outage has never been exercised by anything.

**Verification.** `tests/test_hook_file_mode.py::test_every_tracked_hook_is_executable_in_the_index`,
written FIRST and watched fail for the right reason at `1 failed`, naming all three
paths with their observed `100644` and printing the repair command. It refuses to pass
over a shrunken set - fewer than three tracked hooks is a failure, not a green tick -
because a stale pathspec finding nothing is the exact guard shape this item exists to
prevent. The arm lives in `tests/`, a NON-frozen file, so a fourth hook authored on

**WHAT THIS GRANT DOES NOT CLOSE, stated so it is not read as closed.** No Clockspeed

**CROSS-PROJECT, measured on this disk the same session.** Riot Commander (6 hooks),

  evidence when both rest on the same assumption.** The package route is now tried first

### 2026-09-06 - CS-918 - the headless `queue` lane lands, ported from a sibling repo with three named fixes; the END-TO-END CYCLE IS NOT YET RUN and this entry does not claim it

**CS-918 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it.** Everything below is built, graded and merged, but
the acceptance clause that matters most - one real cycle end to end writing one JSONL row -
requires the lane's own code to be reachable from a commit, so it could not run before this
one existed. A second entry records that run and its outcome. Read this entry as "the
machinery is here and it is graded"; read the next as "and it works".

**What shipped.** A one-row-per-worker headless lane and the driver that repeats it.
Merged files: `ops/loop/lanes.py`, `ops/loop/lane_launcher.py`, `ops/loop/run_lane.ps1`,
`ops/loop/winmutex.py`, `ops/loop/queue_loop.py`, `ops/loop/launch_queue_loop.ps1`,
`tools/headless-queue.md`, `tools/dashboard_probe.py`, and the runbook in
`docs/OPERATIONS.md` section 10. The fork ruling is `docs/adr/0017`.

**THE FIX THAT IS THE POINT OF THE PORT: the driver owns every wait and the worker owns
none.** The upstream wrote that rule as PROSE in its worker's prompt and MEASURED it
half-hold over six cycles - two workers blocked, four exited early, and each early exit let
the next cycle's push cancel the run the previous cycle was being graded on. An instruction
a worker can rationalize past is not a mechanism. Here the wait sits in `run_loop`, between
cycles, where the only thing that could start the next cycle is the loop that is doing the
waiting. Graded as an ORDER rather than as a call count by
`tests/test_queue_loop.py::test_the_driver_waits_between_cycles_and_the_next_cycle_cannot_start_first`,
because a wait that does not sit BETWEEN two cycles serialises nothing.

**WHAT THAT MEANS AGAINST THIS REPO'S CI, read out of the workflow files rather than
inherited from the upstream.** `tier1.yml` fires on every branch push and sets
`cancel-in-progress: true`, so the self-cancelling trap is live here. `tier2.yml` does NOT
fire on a branch push - only on the nightly cron, a `v*` tag, and `workflow_dispatch` - so
the full suite does not exist for a worker's commit unless something asks for it, and the
driver asks. Both facts are pinned against the files themselves by
`tests/test_queue_loop_ci_specs.py`, which is the only place in the suite where the driver's
job matchers are compared with the jobs that actually exist; every other arm grades
fixtures, and a fixture agrees with whatever it was written from forever.

**A VERDICT IS A SUMMARY LINE AND AN EXIT CODE, NEVER EITHER ALONE.** A crashed parallel run
leaves no summary line, and `grep -c FAILED` over that log returns 0 - indistinguishable
from green. `summarize_pytest` answers `ok` only when a line was parsed AND the code is
zero, and the row carries both verbatim. Graded by
`::test_a_truncated_log_that_exited_zero_is_not_green`. The same principle governs the CI
grader: a required job matching NOTHING is `unavailable`, an answer about the tool, never a
pass - `::test_a_required_matcher_that_matches_nothing_is_unavailable_not_success`.

**EVERY MATRIX LEG IS GRADED, NOT THE POOL.** `full suite (ubuntu-latest)` and
`full suite (windows-latest)` are two jobs, and a grader asking "did any leg pass" leaves
the weakest unmeasured while the acceptance clause still reads green.
`::test_one_failed_matrix_leg_fails_the_whole_workflow`.

**THE SHARED-FILE TRAP, AND THE RULING.** Two files in the upstream lane are
BYTE-IDENTICAL-BY-CONTRACT across three repositories, pinned by a digest table in that
repo's suite. A fourth copy here would not be covered by that pin. **Forked, not joined** -
`docs/adr/0017` records why: joining the pin means joining the PROTOCOL, and the shared
governor's token bucket rations concurrent workers between those three repositories, so a
fourth participant consumes their slots by editing a file in a fourth tree. `winmutex.py` is
an explicitly forked copy naming its upstream digest; the governor is not copied at all, and
`lanes.py` records that its two needed pieces are DERIVED. Neither sibling tree was touched.

**A NEW AUTHORED ROOT MADE THREE REPO-WIDE GUARDS SPEAK, AND EACH WAS A DECISION RATHER
THAN A WIDENING.** `ops/` joined the mypy `files` key, `chained_cause_guard.SWEPT_ROOTS` and
`toolpath_guard.SPAWN_ROOTS`. The third is the one that mattered: CS-910's finding is that
Windows searches the current directory before PATH, and **this lane spawns with the LANE
WORKTREE as its working directory - a tree whose whole purpose is to be written into by an
unattended agent for hours.** Of every root on that list this is the most exposed, so `git`,
`gh`, `powershell` and `taskkill` now resolve through `tools/toolpath.py::resolve_tool` and
`tests/test_toolpath.py::test_no_program_in_the_spawn_roots_can_be_supplied_by_the_working_directory`
covers them.

**"Does the dashboard run" is a SCRIPT now, not an opinion.** It had been relitigated three
times because it was a judgment call. `tools/dashboard_probe.py` launches it, polls the
port, asserts a named JSON key and named DOM nodes, captures one screenshot and decides by
exit code, with nine distinct codes so a launch failure and a content failure are never one
answer. It carries its own known-good controls - a finder that sees a present id AND does
not see an absent one - because a negative measurement with no control is worthless. It
pins the dashboard's own certificate rather than waiving verification, and says on its own
face when `--no-verify` makes a run no evidence about the certificate. Measured here: exit
0, 29 assertions, 0 bytes of stderr, port released.

**Verified.** 201 lane arms plus 113 in the spawn and subprocess guards, all green;
`ruff check .` clean; `mypy` clean over 170 files. A seven-mutant battery against the
substrate - a dead pid reading RUNNING, a mutating `lane_state`, a worktree guard that
accepts the main tree, a removed ABA guard, DETACHED_PROCESS restored, a launch that stops
releasing the lane, and the API-key clear removed - **caught 7 of 7**, on a verified
pristine floor with a digest-verified restore. Two of those mutants were mis-aimed on the
first pass and reported VOID and SURVIVED; both were re-anchored rather than scored, because
a mutation that never applied and a surviving one produce the same output.

**Not verified, and stated rather than rounded up.** `run_lane.ps1` has never been executed
against a live worker by any automated arm - it is parse-checked under both PowerShell
majors and graded on its executable lines. `winmutex.hold()` is called by no test, because
taking a real named mutex is forbidden. The real `_spawn`, the real `_git` and the real `gh`
are graded statically; the CI path was exercised read-only against real completed runs of
both tiers, which is not the same as having waited out a live one.

### 2026-09-06 - CS-906 - CORRECTION. The shipped speedup is 2.39x and not the 3.2x the commit above claims, and the scheduler's benefit does not show on a real push

**THE TWO ENTRIES BELOW OVERSTATE THE RESULT AND THIS CORRECTS THEM.** Nothing is edited;
a wrong record is corrected by a later one. The change is still a large win and the
direction was never in doubt - the SIZE was.

**WHAT WAS CLAIMED.** The `--dist loadfile` commit says "765s to about 238s, roughly 3.2x",
projected from standalone readings of 233s and 243s.

**WHAT A REAL PUSH DOES.** Two pushes through the shipped hook took 321s and 320s wall,
316.98s and 317.93s inside pytest. The 238s projection did not survive contact with the
gate it was projected for.

**THE HONEST SHIPPED FIGURE, all of it from REAL PUSHES rather than standalone runs:**

| | measured |
|---|---|
| before, serial | 762s, 765s, 769s |
| after, distributed | 321s, 320s |
| shipped improvement | **2.39x, about 445 seconds off every push** |

**THE SCHEDULER IS KEPT, AND ITS BENEFIT IS NARROWED RATHER THAN WITHDRAWN.** Measured
PAIRED and back to back, both matching the hook's exact invocation including `-x` and the
absolute test path: default 308s, `--dist loadfile` 253s. So the flag really is about 18
per cent faster in a clean paired run, and Riot Commander's own suite corroborates the
direction at a much larger scale. **But that benefit did NOT appear on the one real push
measured with it**, where 316.98s was indistinguishable from the 317.93s without it. Push
wall clock carries variance this comparison cannot see through at n=1 per arm.

**WHY THE FIRST COMPARISON WAS WRONG, STATED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED.** The 233s and 243s
loadfile readings were taken against default readings of 318s and 387s that were NOT
measured back to back with them. The 387s reading in particular was taken while three
builder agents were live on this machine. An unpaired comparison across a contended
machine is the same instrument error this item has already been burned by twice, and it
was made a third time here.

**WHAT IS SAFE TO QUOTE.** 2.39x, from real pushes. Not 3.2x, and not 2.59x - that earlier
figure was against the suite before condition TWELVE's arms existed and is already
corrected in the entry below.

**A SECOND CORRECTION, TO A COUNT.** `-n auto` resolves to EIGHT workers on this machine,
not sixteen. xdist counts PHYSICAL cores; this box is 8 physical and 16 logical. Two
artifacts said or implied sixteen before this was checked. Riot Commander measured the
same eight-of-sixteen on the same physical box, so the cross-project comparison is
like-for-like.


### 2026-09-06 - CS-906 - CLOSED. The pre-push suite runs distributed, all thirteen grant conditions met, and the arms caught an edit that would have reddened every push

Verification: `python -m pytest tests -q -n auto` -> 5371 passed, 4 skipped.
`python scripts/install_hooks.py` -> exit 0. The frozen-file edit is `a8eb697`, strictly
later than the grant entry below and strictly later than `b3d744e`, which carries the
test-side conditions - the ordering conditions SEVEN and THIRTEEN require, verifiable from
`git log` rather than from this sentence.

**WHAT SHIPPED.** `.githooks/pre-push` chooses serial or parallel ONCE, before the run,
from an importability probe, and never re-runs the suite. Scope held: only the pytest
invocation and its comment block moved. Everything after `STATUS=$?` compares byte-equal to
its parent, and the `cs_probe` block, the interpreter ladder, the pytest importability
check and the exit-5 guard are untouched.

**THE MEASUREMENT, AND THE FLATTERING NUMBER IS NAMED SO IT IS NOT QUOTED.** Before:
serial, 765s over three runs on 5362 tests. After: distributed, 387s on 5371 tests. That
is **1.98x and about 378 seconds off every push**. An earlier reading of **2.59x** (765s
against 296s) was taken against the suite BEFORE condition TWELVE's arms existed and MUST
NOT be quoted as the shipped figure. The grant's own 1.222x was a 2-vCPU runner; this
machine has 16 logical processors, which is why condition TEN demanded a local reading.

**THE ARMS CAUGHT A DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED GREEN AND REDDENED EVERY PUSH.** The
first edit passed when its module ran alone and failed, three of three, under an outer
`-n auto`. The hook now runs the whole suite distributed; that suite CONTAINS the arms that
grade the hook. Without condition TWELVE this would have been discovered by the first
person to push.

**THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL.** `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` is an ordinary environment variable
and it is INHERITED. Under an outer distributed run the process driving the push is itself
a worker, so the variable travels the whole chain - environment copy, git, sh, the hook -
into the nested pytest, whose CONTROLLER then reads a worker id it never earned and files
itself as a worker. Every controller-derived field returns None while the run plainly
happened. **The signature is `ran=False` beside a NON-ZERO worker count**, which is not
"nothing ran" but "everything ran and the controller was misfiled"; it was measured wearing
two different numbers, `workers=9` and `workers=1`.

**THE FIX ASKS `config.workerinput`**, which xdist injects INSIDE the worker process before
the session configures and which therefore cannot arrive from a parent. It is xdist's own
discriminator - `is_xdist_worker` is exactly that `hasattr` - and it is read with `getattr`
rather than an import because the degraded arm hides xdist from that very process. **No
assertion was weakened.** The arms still require the run to have distributed, the push to
be blocked, the ref not to land, and exit 5 to survive; a control field now records what
the environment CLAIMED so the misfiled shape cannot be silent again, and a new arm grades
the discriminator itself rather than only its consequence.

**CONDITION NINE, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** This change makes one module SLOWER:
`tests/test_hook_interpreter_ladder.py` goes 41.45s to 85.48s serially, 88 arms to 92,
because every sandbox now starts xdist workers and the new arms drive six real pushes. A
slower module against 378 seconds off every push is a trade worth stating plainly.

**CONDITION SEVEN SHRANK ON MEASUREMENT.** Of sixteen candidate modules exactly ONE was
vulnerable to the CS-448 rootdir climb. The mechanism needs two conditions at once: no ini
above the argument AND a cwd sharing a non-drive-root ancestor with it. Four gate modules
were measured immune because their in-repo argument finds `pyproject.toml` before the
fallback branch runs; four were already pinned; five are not nested-pytest sites at all.
Measured with only the cwd varied: 0.35s resolving to the sandbox, 12.27s resolving to the
temp root, 0.37s back to the sandbox once pinned.

**CONDITION SIX FOUND A SPELLING THAT LIES.** `python -m xdist` fails on an INSTALLED
plugin - a package is not directly executable - so the module channel that is correct for
pytest, ruff and mypy would have reported a working xdist as MISSING. The probe is an
import.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. CS-907 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not touch it.** The hook
still runs the whole tests directory while `CONVENTIONS.md` section 8 assigns tier 0 a
"fast unit subset" and the hook's own header still claims it runs one. This grant treated
the SYMPTOM by the adjudicator's own ruling; subsetting remains the doctrinally correct
remedy and lost only on timing. Do not read a faster hook as a corrected contract.

**AN UNRELATED GAP FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED.** `pyyaml` is in the `dev` extra and
`scripts/verify_env.py` reports it nowhere, while `tools/drift_guard.py` imports it at
module level - so its absence breaks that guard outright rather than degrading. A builder
found it and declined to widen a frozen-file grant's conditions from inside a slice, which
is the correct refusal. It is filed rather than smuggled in.

budget window is `[M, cutoff - 2N]`, and it is EMPTY once `N > (cutoff - M) / 2`. At the

the second requirement and only that one. **THE LEVELS WERE NOT TOUCHED** - `N` rests on

reading. The window is recorded so the next session knows the lever exists, not so it can
be pulled at this sample size. A distribution-free 95/95 bound on the sample maximum needs
`n >= 59` and is not available either.

**CS-896 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it.** The entry below records that a
fourth reading of the fast shard would discharge the sample objection at the 95/95 level,
and that the run of that commit would be it. **It was, and it did the opposite.**

job-seconds, fast **260**. The three before it were 323, 359 and 358.

`3911 passed, 23 skipped` in run 34021868008 AND in run 34024118253 - a byte-identical
population, since no commit between them touched a test that shard runs. Its pytest step ran
**314.64s and then 226.24s**. That is an **88-second swing on identical work**, and the step
rather than the setup is where it moved, so it is the machine and not the cache.

**WHAT THAT DOES TO THE ARITHMETIC.** Sample sd over the four readings is **46.5s**, not the
20.5s the three-reading sample gave. The one-sided 95/95 normal tolerance bound at n=4 is
therefore **564s, ABOVE the 480 ceiling** - where the entry below predicted 452.1s and
called it discharged. **Adding the fourth reading did not satisfy the criterion; it widened
the distribution and failed it.**

**AND IT FALSIFIES THIS SESSION'S NOISE FIGURE BY 2.4x.** The warn band was sized at 60s
from a measured 36s swing, with the guaranteed margin computed as 24s. The real swing on
identical work is at least 88s. **The band is again NARROWER THAN THE NOISE**, which is the
precise defect that sank the 40s band two entries down, recurring with a larger number. The
levels are NOT changed here: every one of the four readings is inside them, the worst being
359 against a 420 budget, and a fifth re-derivation on n=4 would repeat exactly the mistake

cluster within 36s; 260 sits 98s below all of them. That is the shape of a HETEROGENEOUS
RUNNER POOL - two machine classes - not one normal distribution. A normal tolerance bound
applied to a bimodal sample is the wrong test in both directions, so "n=4 discharges it" was
never going to be the right question. **What the next session needs is a distribution-free
criterion, or enough readings to characterise both modes, not one more sample.**

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE OF THE LANE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS EASY TO LOSE IN THE ABOVE.**

reports its own duration against it, proven by a run that reports the comparison" - is met
four times over. **What is not met is the CS-896 leaf's added condition that growth be
visible before it is fatal, because a band narrower than the noise cannot guarantee that
ordering.** That is why this is a record and not a closure.

**FOUR ADVERSARIAL PASSES RAN THIS SESSION AND ALL FOUR RETURNED REFUTED**, each against a

cancelled run is evidence of nothing, and it is the exact condition the item was filed
about.

guard (k) pins it, and the note beside it refuses a raise in capitals. With the cutoff fixed
and the suite at 5334 tests, the work had to be given more than one runner or taken out of
the lane. **It was SPLIT rather than trimmed.** Merged file:
`.github/workflows/tier1.yml`. The `fast` job runs `tests` with `tests/save` ignored; the
new `save` job runs `tests/save`. Every test that ran before still runs on every push, in
one shard or the other, so per-push coverage is unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by
argument.

matrix, because minutes are metered. Two jobs pay a second checkout and a second install,
roughly 35 seconds. Operator decision, 2026-09-06, taken against the alternative of moving

improved only by shrinking its own denominator. The record is in this file under CS-900.

**A PARTITION IS EXACTLY WHERE COVERAGE GOES MISSING, so it is asserted rather than
trusted.** Verified by

### 2026-09-05 - CS-900 - MEASUREMENT AND REPAIR RECORD. The liveness sweep re-parsed 8.4 MB of source 3457 times, and the fix that shipped is the one an adversary found after REFUTING the fix that was proposed

**CS-900 STAYS OPEN.** Its acceptance asks for a runner profile taken BEFORE and AFTER that
reports the most expensive test's share both times. The before half exists now; the after
half does not, because the profile below was taken on the tree that still carried the
defect.

**THE PROFILE, taken on the tier 1 runner** - run 34010764125 on the CS-900 diagnostic profiling commit, `pytest -n auto
--durations=40`, `5215 passed, 120 skipped in 554.70s`:

| seconds | test |
|---|---|
| 168.66 | `tests/save/test_phase4_gate.py::test_the_save_suite_passes_with_no_install_and_no_save` |
| 81.69 | `tests/test_liveness.py::test_the_resolved_routes_recover_only_functions_that_really_reach_grading` |
| 30.71 | `tests/save/test_absolute_claims.py::test_a_marked_claim_at_each_parse_derived_position_is_caught` |
| 26.31 | `tests/save/test_reach_guard.py::test_every_library_reaching_module_in_the_package_is_declared` |

**THE DEFECT.** `tests/liveness.py::module_function` took a module's SOURCE and called
`ast.parse` on it for every question asked. The route sweep asks 3457 questions about 156
tracked files totalling roughly 8.4 MB, so the same sources were parsed thousands of times
to answer what is a dictionary lookup. **Measured on the development machine: 89.93s for
those 3457 calls, and 0.89s for the same calls after.** Twelve sibling helpers in the same
module had the identical shape and now share one cache. Merged file: `tests/liveness.py`.
`tests/test_liveness.py` runs 100 passed in 41.19s against roughly 146s before.

**THE FIX THAT WAS PROPOSED WAS REFUTED, AND THE REFUTATION IS THE RECORD WORTH KEEPING.**
The plan was to mark the two most expensive tests `slow` and have tier 1 run `-m 'not
slow'`. An adversary that wrote none of it returned REFUTED on six of seven points. Three
were fatal:

- **CS-907's note already forbids it, in capitals** - "DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY MARKING TESTS
  `slow` UNTIL THE NUMBER LOOKS RIGHT. A marker applied to whatever is slowest today is a
  subset defined by a stopwatch rather than by risk." The plan was exactly that.
- **CS-448's acceptance would have been handed to the lane its own note refuses as
  evidence.** That acceptance asks for deterministic passing under `-n auto` across
  REPEATED runs; tier 1 generates those at 26 a day, tier 2 at one, only on main, and only
  when an opportunistic `pip install pytest-xdist` succeeds.
- **CS-900's own metric would have moved by 0.7 points.** Deleting a test from the step
  shrinks the denominator too: the post-change top test would have been 18.2 per cent
  against the 18.9 per cent the item was filed about.

It also found two real per-push coverage losses that the plan had not enumerated, in
`tests/test_mypy_gate.py`, and that the plan gave away a 1.6s fork-bomb guard for about
three seconds.

**AND IT REFUTED A NUMBER THIS SESSION HAD ALREADY REPORTED.** The claim that the most
expensive test "grew +57s" compared 111.39s at `c33afca`, which is a SERIAL reading, against
168.66s, which is PARALLEL and taken while a sibling xdist worker contends for the second
vCPU. The two are not comparable and the growth is not established by them. The share
figure has the same fault: on two workers the per-test shares of a makespan sum to about
200 per cent, not 100, so "share of the step" is not the same quantity it was when the item
was filed.

**WHAT IS STILL OWED, AND IT IS A SLOPE AND NOT A LEVEL.** Measured: 26 commits landed
between `c33afca` and the CS-900 diagnostic profiling commit in one working day, and the parallel step went 463.49s to
554.70s over them - **3.51 seconds per commit**. Any fix that buys a fixed number of seconds
buys a fixed number of commits. Verified by
`tests/test_liveness.py::test_module_function_returns_the_first_definition_of_a_repeated_name`,
`::test_module_function_does_not_answer_one_source_from_another` and
`::test_module_function_reports_a_name_the_module_does_not_define`.

### 2026-09-05 - CS-910 - REPAIR RECORD. The arm that graded a Windows-only mechanism ran on Linux and failed tier 1, and the liveness gate that should have stopped it answered TRUE where the mechanism does not exist

**CS-910 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it.** It still owes the adjudicator grant
for the four frozen sites, the runtime arms over the remaining indirect delegations, and the
31 ungraded findings under `tests/`. This records a repair to a test that CS-910's own work
introduced.

**THE HANDOFF INTO THIS SESSION WAS WRONG ON A MATERIAL POINT and it is corrected here.** It
recorded that tier 1 was red on the duration ceiling alone, with every test passing. Both
red runs read `1 failed, 5213 passed, 119 skipped`:

| run | commit | pytest step | job |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34008102419 | `4e89375` | 538.98s | 574s |
| 34009025621 | `8729191` | 546.97s | 582s |

The lane was red for TWO reasons and only one of them had been read.

**THE MECHANISM.** `tests/test_make_cert.py::test_a_planted_openssl_in_the_working_directory_is_never_run`
grades the implicit current-directory executable search, which is a Windows behaviour. Two
of the three CS-910 runtime arms carry a platform skip - `tests/test_make_shortcut.py` by an
inline `skipif` and `tests/test_toolpath.py` by `WINDOWS_ONLY`. The third carried a LIVENESS
GATE INSTEAD, written `os.name != 'nt' or NeedCurrentDirectoryForExePath(...)`, which
SHORT-CIRCUITS TRUE on POSIX. So the gate reported the mechanism live exactly where it is
absent, and the arm walked on to a control asking `shutil.which` to offer a plant in the
working directory, which off Windows cannot pass. **The control did its job and the gate
lied.**

**WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, AND THE FIRST FILED CAUSE WAS WRONG.** The first commit message on
this repair said `cancel-in-progress` cancelled the runs for `b02e174` and `af3e99d`.
**MEASURED FALSE.** `git log 53ac4b5..4e89375` is TWELVE commits and `gh run list --commit`
returns nothing for either SHA. GitHub Actions creates one run per PUSH event against the
TIP commit, so every intermediate commit of a multi-commit push is never eligible for a run
at all - nothing was queued and nothing was cancelled. `b02e174`, which introduced the test,
could not have been tested, and `4e89375` was the first run in existence to execute it. The
development machine is Windows, where the arm passes, so tier 0 could not see it either.

**THE REPAIR IS THE GATE ITS TWO SIBLINGS ALREADY HAD**, plus a structural guard, because
nothing that runs on this machine could have caught the missing gate. Merged files:
`tests/test_make_cert.py`, `tests/test_toolpath.py`. Verified by
`tests/test_toolpath.py::test_every_current_directory_arm_is_skipped_off_windows`, which
reads every test function under `tests/` for the two spellings that reach the mechanism and
asserts each carries a platform skip. It reads the WHOLE UNPARSED FUNCTION rather than the
import statements, because the arm that broke the lane named the module only inside a probe
STRING - a scan for the import would have reported a clean population over a live defect.
Its companion,
`tests/test_toolpath.py::test_the_current_directory_arm_population_is_not_empty`, asserts the
scanned population is non-empty so the guard cannot pass by matching nothing.

**MEASURED, BOTH DIRECTIONS.** The guard fails on the pre-fix tree naming exactly one arm.
The population is exactly three and they are the three CS-910 runtime arms. CI run
34010764125 reports `5215 passed, 120 skipped`, zero failures, on Linux.

**NO BACKFILL IS OWED AND HERE IS HOW THAT WAS ESTABLISHED.** The defect is confined to a
test's own skip condition. The set checked is every write site in the arm and its four
helpers - `_plant_openssl`, `_curdir_search_env`, `_child_probe` and the arm itself - and
every one writes only under a pytest `tmp_path` that is discarded. No product code changed,
so no persisted card id or world-token key can have been computed by the defective path.

### 2026-09-05 - CS-910 - MEASUREMENT RECORD. Seven spawn sites routed, and the claim that the remainder was all frozen was FALSE TWICE

**CS-910 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it.** Its acceptance asks the same
question of "every other external tool this repository spawns", and that is not answered.

**What shipped.** `tools/toolpath.py` resolves a spawned tool at runtime, walks `PATH`,
refuses any non-rooted entry and never consults the working directory. `shutil.which` was
MEASURED on the pinned interpreter to return a RELATIVE path to a file planted in the
current directory when `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` is absent - and an independent
probe confirmed that variable is absent at BOTH `HKLM` and `HKCU` on this machine, so the
arm stripping it from the child restores reality rather than manufacturing a defect.

**The done-claim was REFUTED by an adversary, and the repair was refuted again by its own
census.** The first commit's message said seven sites were routed and "the four that
remain are FROZEN". `scripts/verify_env.py` is not frozen, was on that slice's write-list,
and still put a BARE `git` into three argv in `scripts/verify_env.py::_hard_rows` - reproduced end to
end with a plant, the row flipping from the real repository root to "rev-parse says no".
Worse, both guards were structurally incapable of seeing it: the static census read that
file's single spawn as INDIRECT, and the runtime arm that was supposed to compensate
asserted `len(recorded) == 2` while a real run builds TEN argv, three of them bare. A count
bound is how it hid. The repaired arm drives the real code path and asserts every argv is
rooted with no ceiling.

**Three further blind spots, each proven by a landed mutation before being repaired.**
`from os import system` inside a spawn root produced `sites=0` - not a finding, not even an
enumerated site - because the aliased-import defence was applied to `subprocess` and to the
resolver module and never to `os`. `argv = ["git", "status"]` one line above a spawn folded
to INDIRECT, which is the plainest indirection there is. And the exemption table's
justification tested `path not in <the whole of CLAUDE.md>`, so an exemption for
`tools/drift_guard.py` passed - ten non-frozen paths appear somewhere in that document.

**What it still owes, re-derived rather than quoted.** Four exempted sites genuinely behind
CLAUDE.md section 6, needing an adjudicator grant recorded here before any edit:
`scripts/install_hooks.py::run_git` and `::run_git_optional`, `tools/precommit_gate.py::ruff_command` and `::git`. FIVE
INDIRECT delegations in spawn roots and not three - the earlier count had missed both
`precommit_gate` sites. Of those five only `verify_env`'s is re-derived; `make_cert` and
`make_shortcut` are named, not vouched for, because their test modules were off the slice's
write-list. And 31 ungraded findings under `tests/`.

**A trap worth more than the item.** A reproduction came back CLEAN and had measured
nothing: `dict(os.environ)` upper-cases keys on Windows, so popping the mixed-case gate
variable removed nothing and the child never had the defect available to reproduce. A
known-good control caught the dead instrument.

Independent corroboration by a linter nobody in this project wrote:
`ruff check --isolated --select S607` over `scripts/`, `tools/` and `clockspeed/` reports
exactly three partial-path spawns, all of them in frozen files.

Verification: `python -m pytest tests/test_toolpath.py tests/test_verify_env.py` - 96

`tests/test_make_cert.py::test_a_planted_openssl_in_the_working_directory_is_never_run`.

### 2026-09-05 - CS-600 - MEASUREMENT RECORD. SEVEN audit rounds on one style layer, no round returned CLEAR, and the operator ruled to commit on the seventh

**CS-600 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it.** It is the phase-6 gate; this
records what its ritual caught on the HUD style layer.

**What shipped.** `clockspeed/surface/web/app.css` gained the telemetry-HUD token layer
the direction in `BACKLOG.md` asks for - an industrial-orange accent, three semantic
status colours with their fills, a thin geometric rule, and `.hud`, `.hud-card`,
`.hud-status`, `.hud-figure`, `.hud-accent` and `.hud-overlay`. No component consumes
them yet: the milestone tracker needs `/api/plan` and readable unlock state, and the
throughput node needs `/api/advice`. Both are still 501.

**The measurement that set the palette.** #FA9549 scores 2.22 on `--surface`, 2.07 on
`--bg` and 1.96 on `--surface-alt` - it fails even the 3:1 large-text threshold on this
page's own LIGHT grounds, not merely over a game pixel, because a light theme IS a white
pixel that is always on screen. Hue 25.8deg and saturation 0.947 were held and only
lightness moved, to #9f4704, which scores 6.22 / 5.79 / 5.49. A status colour is graded
on its own tinted fill as well as the three page grounds: the first candidate cleared
every page ground at 4.56 and then scored 4.18 on the fill it was drawn for.

**The overlay measurement, which is the part worth keeping.** Contrast over a scrim is
NOT MONOTONIC in opacity. Accent over `--bg` over a white game pixel falls from 2.22 at
no scrim to 1.02 near alpha 0.35 - where the composited ground crosses the accent's own
luminance and the text vanishes - then climbs to 8.38 fully opaque. A designer reaching
for a light scrim to keep the game visible lands at the WORST legibility available,
strictly worse than drawing no scrim at all. Body text clears 4.5:1 at alpha 0.65, the
accent at 0.80.

**FIVE ROUNDS, AND FOUR OF THEM FOUND THE SAME FAULT ONE SELECTOR FURTHER OUT.** Round 1
found the rule's own `color` reading a scheme-FOLLOWING token onto a scheme-FROZEN ground
- 1.04:1 measured in a real browser. Round 2 found the repair had left `border` doing it.
Round 3 found a `.hud-card` nested in the overlay at 1.18:1. Round 4 found `.facts dd` at
1.04:1, `h2` at 2.25:1 and `.lede` at 3.10:1 - none of them `.hud` rules. Each repair
defined its boundary as "the tokens something I can see reads", and each next audit found
a rule outside that set. Round 4 named the pattern in its own words: "Each repair closed
the set the previous auditor named and drew the new boundary exactly where the previous
finding stopped."

**What ended it was a measurement, not another repair.** `--overlay-ground`,
`--overlay-fg`, `--overlay-accent` and `--overlay-rule` were byte-identical to the DARK
values of `--bg`, `--text`, `--accent-hud` and `--hud-rule`. Four tokens had been
spelling, one at a time, something the sheet already said whole. They are retired, and
`.hud-overlay` now redefines all 30 `:root` tokens at their dark values: inside an
overlay, the palette IS the dark palette. `test_the_overlay_redefines_the_whole_palette_as_the_dark_scheme`
derives its requirement from the `:root` declaration list, so a token ADDED to the sheet
turns it red until the rule covers it - verified by planting one.

**Two instrument faults the audits refused to report as findings**, both caught by
control: the browser pane fakes `resize` and never dispatches `blur`/`focusout`, and
`:focus-visible` never matches in it. The focus ring is graded from the CSSOM and said to
be so, rather than reported as a pass nobody measured.

**A round-3 finding worth its own sentence.** `tests/surface/audit_harness.py` published
`/api/registry` as live and then answered it 404, because `_liveness()` derives from
`health.ENDPOINT_TEMPLATES` minus `pending.UNBACKED` while `_canned()` gains nothing
automatically. The mandatory CONVENTIONS 13.2 ritual was grading the page in a state
production never reaches, and the whole suite stayed green throughout.
`test_the_harness_answers_every_route_it_publishes_as_live` now fails if any parameterless
live route has no canned answer.

**ROUNDS 5 TO 7 LEFT THE PALETTE ENTIRELY, WHICH IS WHY THE COUNT IS SEVEN.** Round 5
found `color-scheme` - not a custom property, so it could never appear in the `:root`
declaration list the arm derived its requirement from, and a `.scroll-x` nested in the
overlay painted a WHITE scrollbar on the dark ground. Round 6 found that repair had landed
on `.hud-overlay`, which renders ZERO times, while `:root` - which renders on every load -
declared no `color-scheme` at all. Round 7 found the repaired arm defeated by an OPTIONAL
TRAILING SEMICOLON: CSS lets the last declaration in a block omit it, so one character
blinded every property at once, and the comment claimed the leg was closed. It also found
that the "62 elements" repair had corrected the RIGHT number and left the wrong one,
leaving "walked 57 ... found all 62" - impossible, because a subset cannot outnumber what
it was drawn from. Measured: 62 past the edge, 5 of them structural boxes overhanging
0.333px, 57 real ones, all inside the scroller.

**NO ROUND RETURNED `AUDIT: CLEAR`, AND THIS ENTRY DOES NOT PRETEND ONE DID.** Round 7
graded the RENDERED page PASS on all five phases and measured zero live defects - 294
declarations parsed, 0 invisible, no semicolon-less declaration, no `@property`, no
`scrollbar-color`, no literal beside a token anywhere in the sheet. Every finding from
round 5 on was in a guard protecting CSS that renders zero times, or in prose. On that
evidence the operator ruled to commit. The four round-7 findings were repaired first and
each is proven by a planted mutation.

**The pattern, stated for whoever reads this next.** Four repairs in a row each closed
exactly the set the previous audit had named and drew the new boundary where the previous
finding stopped. What ended it was not a better repair but a MEASUREMENT: the four
`--overlay-*` tokens were byte-identical to the dark values of `--bg`, `--text`,
`--accent-hud` and `--hud-rule`, so the overlay palette had been the dark palette all
along. A boundary drawn around a mechanism gets stepped around; one drawn around the
sheet's own declaration list does not.

Verification: `python -m pytest tests` - 5324 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0, observed by the
merger. See `tests/surface/test_web_assets.py::test_the_overlay_redefines_the_whole_palette_as_the_dark_scheme`.

### 2026-09-05 - CS-913 - RE-SPEC RECORD. The filed cause is REFUTED by the code: the unlock reader is an argument-free stub, and the decoder it needs has no caller

**CS-913 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it.** It records that the item as
filed asked for the wrong thing, and what it should ask for instead.

**What the item said.** That unlock state is empty for every save "because its serialized
grammar has never been measured".

**What the code says, verified independently three times - by the merger, by the slice
that measured it, and by an adversary told not to read either.**
`clockspeed/save/world.py::_read_unlocks` takes ZERO arguments - no bytes, no object
table, no property map - and its whole body returns `EMPTY_UNLOCK_STATE` plus one
warning, unconditionally. Its only call site is argument-free. So the emptiness is a
property of the PRODUCER and not of any save, and it would survive the grammar being
measured in full. Meanwhile `clockspeed/save/objects.py::read_properties` is a complete
tagged-property decoder: its only non-test caller is its own thin wrapper, and the only
mentions anywhere else in the package are two lines of docstring prose. The grammar was
measured; the plumbing was never built.

**The acceptance clause also named a world that cannot satisfy it.** It asked for the
measurement to be taken against the pinned development world. ADR 0004 states plainly
that S6 must NOT be settled there and that doing so "would have produced the wrong
answer" - the pinned world is the CONTROL and must stay empty. A spike measured worse:
every record of every `(14,60)` save decodes ZERO property tags, so the pinned world
cannot exercise the decoder at all, and ADR 0004's control - reached by string scan,
which does not care about payload grammar - is not reproducible through it.

**What was measured instead**, and recorded in
`docs/adr/0016-unlock-arrays-carriers-and-serialized-grammar.md`: the six carriers by
type path, that `mPurchasedSchematics` is an `ArrayProperty` of `ObjectProperty` whose
payload is an asset reference matching no record's instance name, that the recipe set is
`mAvailableRecipes` on a DIFFERENT actor and that `mUnlockedRecipes` decodes on no
carrier at all, and that `mCurrentGamePhase` is an `ObjectProperty` naming a `GP_*`
asset - which refutes `UnlockState.current_game_phase: int | None`, since no integer
index can be filled from an asset reference without inventing one.

**Not closed, and the reason is outside the repo.** The measurement has no repeatable
home: `.gitignore` reserves `/corpus/` and the directory does not exist. Filed as
`CS-G06`. The roadmap line has been rewritten to carry the corrected cause.

### 2026-09-05 - CS-912 - CLOSED. A route publishes the registry, so the two live solver doors stop being unreachable

**What shipped.** `clockspeed/surface/api/registry.py` publishes `/api/registry` as a
tenth route template, carrying items, recipes, buildings, counts, warnings and unknown
groups. `/api/solve` and `/api/optimize` were already LIVE and completely unreachable
from the page, because both require `targets`, `recipes` and `raw_items` and nothing the
surface served let a caller name a single identifier without inventing one. Measured on
the base commit with a registry present: ZERO of the nine published templates named a
single item or recipe identifier in any body.

**Why a tenth route was a cross-cutting change rather than a new module.**
`clockspeed/surface/api/routes.py` enforces a bijection onto `health.ENDPOINT_TEMPLATES`
and raises at IMPORT on any surplus route, and the count nine was hard-coded across five
test modules. `BOOTSTRAP.md` section 7.1 says "Endpoints, minimum:", and that word is
what licensed the tenth.

**The wire constraints held.** `contract` refuses a float at any depth and `json.dumps`
cannot encode a `Fraction`, so every duration, amount and energy value goes through
`contract.rational`. The body is built by NAMING every field - no `asdict`, no `vars()`,
no `fields()` walk - so a field added upstream cannot silently reach the wire. An
adversary attacked all of that with a hostile registry carrying every optional
`Fraction` populated, an unmodelled recipe side and an Unreal-path warning subject, and
could not produce a float, a path or a save-derived string.

**The acceptance clause, satisfied end to end and at full scale.** 731 of 731 producible
items built a solve request naming ONLY published identifiers, zero foreign; 610 answered
a plan and all 121 refusals were `chain_unsolvable`, a solver verdict rather than the
`invalid_parameter` an invented identifier produces.

**The paired control was REFUTED and repaired in the same change.** As first written it
SUBSTITUTED the foreign key into a request that names exactly one recipe, so it also

`the drag strip insets the scrollport rather than covering the page` and

**THE DEFECT WAS IN THE FILE'S OWN STATED RATIONALE.** The comment read: a drag region
swallows the pointer, so the body `padding-top` "pushes the page clear, so the strip covers
nothing". The padding reserves space in DOCUMENT flow while `body::before` is `position:
fixed` to the VIEWPORT, and the two coincide only at scroll offset zero. MEASURED on the
composed page at a scroll of 369: `document.elementFromPoint` returned the band for every y
from 0 to 27, and deleting ONLY the `body::before` rule at the identical offset returned

inference.

**THE REPAIR MOVES THE SCROLLPORT INSTEAD OF PADDING THE PAGE.** `html` stops scrolling and
the body becomes a fixed scroller inset by the strip's height, which makes it GEOMETRICALLY
IMPOSSIBLE for content to pass beneath the band rather than merely unlikely. Re-measured the
same way: with the band deleted, the strip's area holds `html` and nothing else, at scroll
0, mid and maximum, sweeping the full width, at 1574 and at 375. Scrollers still overflow
and scroll with their tab stop intact, the footer is reachable at maximum scroll, the header
sits exactly at y=28, no horizontal page scroll, and the Refresh button hit-tests to itself.

**THE app-region DECLARATIONS WERE DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, AND THAT IS THE DECISION.** The
rival fix was `pointer-events: none` on the band. Whether Chromium still honours a drag
region on a pointer-transparent element is a question NOTHING IN THIS REPO CAN ANSWER -
`shell/node_modules` does not exist in a fresh clone and the module is graded without
electron on purpose. A fix that CANNOT break dragging was preferred over one that MIGHT, and
an arm now asserts `pointer-events` never appears in that CSS so the tempting fix cannot
return quietly.

present, under the heading "the strip must reserve space on the body". It now requires its
ABSENCE, plus the three properties that actually keep the page clear. Proven load-bearing:

inset, and making the band pointer-transparent each redden the suite, with a green floor
either side and `shell/lib/window.js` restored byte-exact.

is not verified. It remains one of the checks `docs/OPERATIONS.md` section 8.3 records as

`ObjectRecord` objects already in hand - and hands the SAME second-reading record to both

### 2026-09-17 - CS-899 - CLOSED. Markdown discussing-prose is DECIDED by an absence declaration the ladder checks three ways, and three recorded forgivenesses were retired to pay for it

**The defect.** `tests/bare_path_guard.py` R4 partitions a PYTHON carrier by AST into author
prose and the data a module feeds itself, and on this tree that partition is exact. Markdown
has no AST and no equivalent was built, so prose that DISCUSSES a dead path - an ADR recording
that a file is deliberately not created, a phase leaf naming the phase 5 ledger module that
does not exist yet - was indistinguishable by shape from prose that CITES one. The only
available answer was a row in `BARE_PATH_REASONS`, and CS-891's adjudicator measured four reds
on planted discussing-prose. A keyword or negation detector over the sentence had already been
priced and REFUSED for failing in the permissive direction.

**The root cause, and it is not the markdown parser.** R4 is not reading the sentence - it is
asking whether the site is DATA the module operates on or the author talking, and that question
happens to be answerable from a Python parse tree. Markdown carries no such signal anywhere,
so the missing thing was never a better reader. It was an authored signal the guard could
check, which is what `.gitignore` is to R2 and a docstring is to R4.

**What shipped.** `tests.bare_path_guard.ABSENT_DECLARATION_RE` reads an HTML comment of the
form `<!-- absent: <path> -->`, and `BarePathSite.declared_absent` records whether the LINE a
spelling sits on carries one naming that same path. The ladder answers it at a new rung ABOVE
R0, `DECLARED_ABSENT`, and it is checked in three directions rather than spent once:

- the path must still be absent, or the site is reported at `DECLARED_ABSENT_BOUND` - a
  declaration the tree has falsified is a finding and not a resolution, which is why the rung
  sits above R0 rather than below it;
- the line must still spell that path as a citation, or `stale_declaration_problems` reports
  it, so prose that is rewritten cannot leave a declaration behind;
- it buys silence for ONE path on ONE line and for nothing else.

**That third direction answers the question CS-891's merger demanded before dispatch and
nobody answered** - whether a forgiveness recorded against a carrier rewritten every session
is a working ratchet or a landmine. It is answered by construction: a declaration cannot
outlive its line. The round that asked it lost the only churning subject to an archive commit
and the question went moot instead.

**The sibling sweep, and it is what makes this a move rather than a widening.** All three of
the live markdown forgivenesses shared the root cause, so all three were swept: the ADR 0010
row and the two phase-leaf rows came OFF `BARE_PATH_REASONS`, whose ceiling fell from 4 to 1,
and onto `DECLARED_ABSENT_IN_DOC` under `DECLARED_ABSENT_CEILING`. The one row that remains is
the one that is not a markdown carrier at all. The two budgets together say that nothing was
forgiven twice.

**A SECOND DEFECT THIS CYCLE FOUND IN ITS OWN WORK, and the arm that found it was the live
one.** The first build of `stale_declaration_problems` read every line of every carrier and
reported the three controls that plant a declaration to prove the walk fires - each spelling it
inside an f-string template whose placeholder is not a path at all. The repair is R4 itself
rather than a second boundary: a declaration inside a Python string literal that is not a
docstring is a control's fixture, and `test_a_declaration_in_a_fixture_literal_is_declined_and_the_same_one_in_prose_is_not`
holds both directions.

**One contract had to widen, and it is worth reading because the narrow version was right until
today.** `test_every_pattern_in_every_walked_module_is_a_judged_shape` required every compiled
pattern in the family to be a shape the carrier boundary reads. That was true while every
pattern ANSWERED "does this text cite something". The declaration pattern answers a different
question, and admitting it to `JUDGED_SHAPES` would have moved the guarded-set boundary as a
side effect of a repair that is not about it. `NON_CITATION_PATTERNS` declares it instead, and
the contract now checks that table in BOTH directions - a row for a pattern the family no
longer compiles reddens exactly as an undeclared pattern does. The renaming evasion is closed
by the same walk: `module_patterns` reads the `_RE` suffix, so a pattern named anything else is
invisible, and a pattern this family judges by is named `_RE` and then declared in one of the
two tables.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM, stated here because a caveat said in a cycle report is not a
caveat in the artifact.** The mechanism does not INFER intent from a sentence and it was never
going to - discussing-prose that declares nothing is still REPORTED, exactly as before. What
changed is that the answer is now an authored, machine-checked, self-falsifying declaration in
the carrier instead of a row in a Python table that names nothing to check. That is the same
standing R2 gives `.gitignore` and R4 gives a docstring. A reader who wants the guard to read
the prose itself is asking for the keyword detector this item's own note refuses by name.

**Tests, by name.** `tests/test_docs_citations.py` -
`test_discussing_prose_that_declares_the_absence_is_declined_with_no_record` (the acceptance
clause, and the record table is passed EMPTY),
`test_a_declared_absence_the_tree_binds_is_reported`,
`test_a_declaration_naming_a_path_its_line_does_not_spell_is_reported`,
`test_a_declaration_in_a_fixture_literal_is_declined_and_the_same_one_in_prose_is_not`, and
`test_no_absence_declaration_in_the_live_tree_has_outlived_its_prose` over the live carrier
population. `tests/test_citation_tables.py` -
`test_every_bare_path_decline_rung_is_disclosed_in_both_directions` now parametrized over the
new rung. `tests/test_docs_citations.py` -
`test_every_decline_disclosure_is_budgeted_and_spent_exactly` likewise.

**Merged files.** `tests/bare_path_guard.py`, `tests/test_docs_citations.py`,
`tests/test_citation_tables.py`, `tests/test_bare_path_citations.py`, and the three carriers
that now declare their own absences - `docs/adr/0010-item-notes-is-an-index-over-per-phase-leaves.md`,
`docs/item_notes/phase4.md`, `docs/item_notes/phase5.md`.

**Tier 2**, for the public interface: a new rung in `LADDER_RUNGS`, a new public pattern, a new

**THE VERIFIER PASS, AND IT DID NOT PRODUCE THE WORK.** One pass, on a frozen tree, graded

a sibling `PostToolUse` hook belonging to a DIFFERENT project on this machine reads the same
envelope and has been producing real findings all along; and `tools/pretooluse_gate.py`
reads the envelope for the sibling event.

routed the invocation half to an adjudicator because it lives in `.claude/settings.json`.

the continuity oracle a SECOND ORACLE. It is a second IMPLEMENTATION, not a second SIGNAL.
**RE-DERIVED HERE with an independently written predicate: a rule that inspects NO MOVEMENT AT
ALL - the small-magnitude prior applied to the pair's two endpoints, which is
`_int_oracle_holds`'s own two counters restricted to the pair - reproduces the continuity
verdict on 145 OF 145 pairs with ZERO disagreements.** 135 of the 145 changed pairs differ only
in their lowest stored byte. The claim in the entry below that this narrows the common-mode
risk "from three shared inputs to two" is NOT SUPPORTED: the SIGNAL is a third shared input and

library - it needs data this world does not contain.** A later session must not read the
